policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Bangladesh Food Safety Authority has introduced the 'Safe Food (Registration and Licensing) Regulations, 2026', making registration and licensing mandatory for various food businesses. The regulations cover a wide range of entities, from small roadside stalls to large-scale food processing and import businesses. Businesses are required to obtain either a registration or a license depending on the nature of their food products. The enforcement of these requirements is set to begin on November 1, 2026. This measure aims to formalize the food sector and ensure compliance with safety standards.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to protect public health, ensure food safety, and establish discipline within the food business sector in Bangladesh. It follows the legal framework provided by the Food Safety Act, 2013.
beneficiaries: food traders, food establishments, food importers, food processing establishments

policydecision_details: The Government of Saint Lucia has approved the annual Christmas barrel concessions. This measure provides a 100 per cent waiver of customs duty on personal items, food, clothing, toys, and other household consumables imported in barrels. Households are permitted to import up to two barrels with a maximum value of EC$3,000 per barrel. While customs duties are waived, a six per cent Customs Service Charge remains applicable. Electronic items are explicitly excluded from these concessions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is an annual initiative designed to provide economic relief to households during the Christmas season by reducing the cost of importing essential goods and personal items.
commodity3: Meat and other animal derived products

policydecision_details: The Federal Government of Nigeria has approved a monthly transport allowance of N70,000 for public service workers across all levels. This measure is intended to provide financial relief for a period of six months, starting in November 2026. The decision was formalized through a memorandum of understanding following conciliation meetings with labor unions. Despite the announcement, labor representatives have expressed dissatisfaction, demanding permanent salary increases instead of temporary allowances.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced as a response to the rising cost of living and economic hardship in Nigeria, which has significantly impacted the purchasing power of public sector employees. The government aims to mitigate the immediate effects of inflation and fuel price increases on workers' ability to commute. However, the measure has faced criticism from labor unions and political figures who argue that temporary allowances are unsustainable and fail to address the broader economic crisis affecting all citizens.

policydecision_details: The Nigerian Government has approved a ₦70,000 wage award for workers to help mitigate the impact of rising inflation and living costs. This temporary measure will take effect in November 2026 and remain in place for a duration of six months. Additionally, the government has committed to paying outstanding peculiar allowances and addressing arrears owed to health workers. A Minimum Wage Negotiation Committee has also been constituted to address long-term wage structures.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced following negotiations with organized labor to address the financial burden on workers caused by rising inflation, particularly increased transport costs. This follows a previous ₦35,000 wage award implemented approximately two years ago after the removal of the petrol subsidy.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: President Daniel Noboa has announced a new curfew to be implemented in five coastal provinces: Guayas, Manabí, Los Ríos, El Oro, and Esmeraldas. The measure will be in effect from November 1 to November 10, 2026. This curfew is part of a series of special operations aimed at combating crime and weakening criminal structures in the region. The government expects this restriction to limit freedom of transit and improve public safety during the specified period.
contextoradditionalinfo: The provinces of Guayas, Manabí, Los Ríos, and El Oro have been under successive states of exception due to insecurity attributed to criminal gang disputes. The government claims that previous curfew measures have resulted in a 40% reduction in crime. This new curfew is the fourth implemented in Ecuador in 2026 and coincides with national holidays, which may impact travel and commercial activities.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The government of Zimbabwe is launching a national cloud seeding programme. The initiative aims to stimulate rainfall during the 2026-27 rainy season to mitigate the impacts of the El Niño climate phenomenon. Three aircraft will be deployed across Harare, Bulawayo, and Masvingo to ensure nationwide coverage. This measure is a direct response to international meteorological warnings regarding extreme drought conditions.
contextoradditionalinfo: Zimbabwe has faced severe drought conditions linked to El Niño, which caused significant crop losses and food shortages during the 2023/24 season. The government previously declared a state of national disaster in April 2024 due to these climate-induced challenges. The current programme is part of broader efforts to intensify climate change adaptation and protect agricultural production from irregular rainfall and prolonged dry spells.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Mechanisation and Irrigation Development
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Launched the $18.8 million Regional West African Resilient Rice Value Chains Project (REWARD) to address bottlenecks in the rice value chain. The project will develop 3,200 hectares of land and provide farmers with improved seeds, mechanization, and other inputs. Additionally, the government plans to link rice import quotas to local investment to encourage domestic production. The initiative also includes the establishment of 10 processing centers and the improvement of storage facilities to boost national rice output.
contextoradditionalinfo: Ghana currently spends approximately $500 million annually on rice imports, with local production meeting only 56% of national demand. The government aims to achieve rice self-sufficiency by 2028 to reduce foreign exchange outflows and support local farmers and businesses.

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development and the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty have signed a cooperation agreement, funded through the “Embadra” project, to support farmers in the municipality of Ouadane, Mauritania. The agreement aims to develop agricultural activities and improve the living conditions of local communities through targeted support to farmers.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development and the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Sovereignty

policydecision_details: Announced the restoration of the country’s full membership in the International Olive Council, opening opportunities for technical support and development of the olive sector. The Ministry is also supporting the winter agricultural plan through the provision of high-grade wheat seeds and monitoring the expansion of cultivated areas. In addition, it is preparing land and addressing land-use conflicts under the Million Farms Initiative. These efforts aim to address constraints facing agricultural activities, strengthen crop production and support the national economy.

The US EPA has issued the final 2026 Pesticide General Permit (PGP) to regulate point source discharges of biological and chemical pesticides that leave a residue. This permit covers various pest control activities, including mosquito, weed, algae, animal, and forest canopy pest control. The permit is effective from October 31, 2026, through October 30, 2031. Operators must comply with reporting requirements, including submitting a Notice of Intent (NOI) through the NPDES e-reporting tool where applicable.
contextoradditionalinfo: The PGP is a regulatory mechanism under the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) designed to manage the environmental impact of pesticide applications that result in discharges to waters of the United States. It replaces the previous 2021 PGP to ensure continued oversight of pesticide residues in the environment.

policydecision_details: The 2027 Draft Finance Law of Tunisia proposes several measures to support livestock production, the olive oil sector and agricultural exports. Under Article 35, up to TND 40 million would be allocated between 2027 and 2030 to help small cattle farmers rebuild their herds through the purchase and raising of pregnant heifers, including TND 35 million in subsidies supporting bank loans and TND 5 million in direct support. Article 36 would extend an existing tax advantage on calf feed to include a broader range of animal-feeding preparations. The draft also proposes a TND 100 million credit line for seasonal and investment loans to small olive oil producers and agricultural service cooperatives, alongside a dedicated fund for the olive oil sector. In addition, Article 42 would provide state coverage of 50% of export insurance premiums for shipments to African markets. These measures remain subject to parliamentary approval and the adoption of implementing regulations.

Established an intersectoral technical working group to identify ways to expand the reuse of treated wastewater in agriculture and industry, particularly for irrigation. The group includes representatives from water management, environment, agriculture, finance, scientific research, vocational training, industry and start-ups. Its tasks include assessing the performance of existing wastewater treatment plants, identifying technical and financial constraints, and proposing measures to improve operations and increase treatment capacity in line with applicable standards. Algeria currently has 237 wastewater treatment plants with a theoretical capacity of 1.12 billion cubic metres annually. The national programme also предусматри construction of 76 new plants, rehabilitation of 101 pumping stations, development of 802 km of sanitation pipelines, and installation of tertiary treatment equipment.

The Government of Grenada has designated Friday, 30 October and Saturday, 31 October 2026, as official VAT-Free Days. This initiative represents the final two days of a broader 6-day VAT-free program aimed at easing household financial pressures. The policy allows consumers and businesses to purchase goods without Value Added Tax during this period. Additionally, the government has implemented electricity subsidies and removed the Customs Service Charge on diesel used for electricity generation as part of the same Cost-of-Living Assistance Programme.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced as part of the Cost-of-Living Assistance Programme to help families manage rising household expenses and support economic activity across Grenada, Carriacou, and Petite Martinique. The government aims to provide practical relief to citizens while supporting the local business community amidst inflationary pressures.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Singapore and Mongolia have established an Implementation Agreement to open an application process for carbon credit projects starting 30 October 2026. This initiative allows for the authorization of projects that generate carbon credits aligned with Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. These credits are intended to help Singapore-based carbon tax-liable companies offset up to 5% of their taxable emissions. The application process involves a three-stage lifecycle, including project design, authorization, and issuance of credits. The initiative aims to support carbon mitigation activities while promoting sustainable development and job creation in Mongolia.
contextoradditionalinfo: This agreement is the sixth of its kind for Singapore, following similar partnerships with Ghana, Bhutan, Peru, Rwanda, and Thailand. It is designed to advance both countries' climate ambitions and support the International Carbon Credit (ICC) framework, which helps Singaporean companies meet their carbon tax obligations through verified international mitigation projects.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry
beneficiaries: carbon tax-liable companies, local communities in Mongolia
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policy_description: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
policydecision_details: The Jamaica Customs Agency has announced an increase in the Environmental Protection Levy rate. The rate has been adjusted from 0.5% to 0.85%. This measure affects the cost of goods processed through the agency. The policy is intended to strengthen environmental protection funding mechanisms.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Environmental Protection Levy is a fiscal measure in Jamaica designed to generate revenue for environmental management and conservation efforts. Adjusting the rate reflects a government decision to increase the financial resources allocated to environmental sustainability initiatives.
policycategory: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources

policydecision_details: Suspended live cattle imports until further notice and cancelled existing health exemptions following reported foot-and-mouth disease outbreaks in eastern Algeria. Livestock markets in Jijel and Sétif have also been closed, with restrictions imposed on animal movements and health certification required for internal transfers. The Béjaïa Chamber of Agriculture urged cattle, sheep and goat farmers to remain vigilant and strengthen disease prevention measures. The measures aim to contain the spread of the disease and protect livestock health, although the impact on domestic meat supply and prices remains uncertain. Algeria imported approximately 27,000 live cattle in 2025, excluding breeding stock, highlighting the potential implications for livestock trade.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries

policydecision_details: Mobilized 78 one-stop shops nationwide to support cereal farmers during the planting season, with 3.5 million quintals of seeds available against estimated requirements of 2.5 million quintals. The initiative facilitates access to seeds, agricultural financing and insurance through the Cereal and Pulse Cooperatives (CCLS), the Bank of Agriculture and Rural Development (BADR) and the National Agricultural Mutual Fund (CNMA). Farmers can access campaign credit and supplier credit, including arrangements for those affected by adverse weather conditions or fires. Algeria is also expanding seed-sorting capacity and strengthening storage and collection infrastructure, while regional agricultural authorities have set cereal cultivation and production targets and allocated seeds, fertilizers and irrigation resources. These measures aim to support cereal production, improve farmers’ access to inputs and strengthen national food security.

policy_description: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
policydecision_details: Launched a national research network on animal production and health, bringing together 70 laboratories, more than 300 researchers and over 100 doctoral students. The initiative aims to identify agricultural research priorities, strengthen applied research and transfer findings into livestock breeding, animal nutrition and disease prevention to support food security. One key research area is crossbreeding Ouled Djellal and D'man sheep to combine meat production and body weight with higher reproductive performance. Three research agreements also cover sheep genetic diversity, alternative treatments for subclinical mastitis and the use of microalgae and essential oils as alternatives to antibiotics in poultry farming. The network is expected to provide initial findings within six months.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research and the Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries
policycategory: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination

policydecision_details: The Government of Curaçao established a dedicated operational unit for CARICOM affairs to coordinate the island's participation in the Caribbean Community. This initiative includes the appointment of local employees and representatives to manage day-to-day interactions with regional institutions. The unit will be supported by a strategic cooperation plan to identify key areas for engagement. The government aims to leverage this structure to effectively participate in regional programs related to public health, economic affairs, and other specialized sectors.
contextoradditionalinfo: This policy is part of the government's broader 2025–2029 regionalization program, which prioritizes strengthening Curaçao's international position. By formalizing its associate membership in CARICOM, the government seeks to protect its economic, social, and educational interests through closer regional cooperation. The initiative addresses the need for a structured administrative approach to translate membership agreements into concrete regional collaboration.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: The Commission for Consumer Protection in Bulgaria has initiated proceedings against major retail chains to address unjustified price hikes on essential food products. Retailers are subject to inspections of their pricing practices to determine if markups are supported by objective grounds. Those found to be engaging in unjustified price increases face significant fines ranging from €10,000 to €100,000 per product. This measure aims to protect consumers from excessive retail margins on staple goods.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced following reports of extreme markups on dairy products, with butter prices increasing by up to 135%, fresh milk by 99%, and white brined cheese by 95%. Authorities noted that basic food products in Bulgaria were costing more than in other European cities like Vienna and Berlin, prompting concerns over unfair trade practices and the impact on household purchasing power.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: The Bulgarian government has officially ruled out any revisions to the conditions previously agreed upon for North Macedonia's path toward European Union membership. Foreign Minister Velislava Petrova confirmed that Bulgaria is not involved in any consultations to alter these commitments. The government maintains that the 2022 agreements remain the only valid framework for North Macedonia's integration. Bulgaria insists on the strict implementation of these existing obligations, including the protection of the rights of Bulgarians in North Macedonia. No additional demands are being introduced, but the current requirements remain non-negotiable.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy reflects the ongoing diplomatic stance of Bulgaria regarding North Macedonia's EU accession process, which is contingent upon specific commitments made in 2022. The statement was made during parliamentary questioning to clarify the current state of relations between Sofia and Skopje.

policydecision_details: India and Mexico have signed the Terms of Reference to initiate negotiations for a Preferential Trade Agreement. This framework establishes the scope for future discussions, covering market access for goods, rules of origin, and customs procedures. The agreement aims to boost bilateral trade, enhance investment flows, and create more resilient supply chains between the two nations. The move follows a high-level commitment made by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Claudia Sheinbaum to deepen the bilateral partnership.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative stems from an understanding reached between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Claudia Sheinbaum during their meeting on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in Canada in June 2025, where they agreed to strengthen the India-Mexico economic partnership.

policydecision_details: Twenty-one Nigerian states have adopted a harmonised tax law to dismantle the system of multiple taxation and curb illegal revenue collections. The policy streamlines over 100 different taxes and levies into nine approved categories, including income tax and road tax. It explicitly prohibits the use of roadblocks for tax collection and the sale of unauthorized stickers. The reform aims to reduce the cost of doing business and increase disposable income for eligible workers and entrepreneurs. Additionally, a unified national Tax Identification system is being introduced to improve coordination and verify taxpayer records across jurisdictions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative was developed to address the fragmented and exploitative tax practices at the subnational level that have historically increased operating costs for businesses and pushed up consumer prices. By replacing arbitrary levies with a predictable framework, the government seeks to improve tax administration and expand economic activity. The reform is also intended to support household consumption and domestic business activity by reducing personal income tax liabilities for eligible earners.

policydecision_details: Provided 70 olive harvesters and 10 kits containing ladders and harvesting mats to 12 agricultural directorates. The equipment will be loaned to agricultural institutions, local authorities, associations and individual farmers to expand access to harvesting tools and strengthen field support during the national olive harvest campaign. The initiative aims to reduce the financial and physical burden on farmers, improve harvesting efficiency, preserve crop quality and protect agricultural household incomes. It also seeks to strengthen farmers’ ability to access and cultivate their land, sustain olive production and support food security.

Distributed 184 rolls of plastic sheeting and netting to 46 farmers in Ein al-Beida and Bardala in the West Bank. The initiative aims to help farmers rehabilitate and maintain greenhouses, reduce production costs and sustain agricultural activities and household incomes. The support addresses challenges caused by attacks and restrictions that hinder farmers’ access to their land and threaten agricultural assets and livelihoods. The intervention seeks to strengthen the resilience of vulnerable farming households, maintain local agricultural production and support food security.
decision_making_institution: The Directorate of Agriculture in Tubas and the Northern Jordan Valley

policydecision_details: Highlighted measures to strengthen the domestic date industry during the International Date Fair (SIDATTES) in Erfoud, which brings together producers, cooperatives, researchers and investors. Morocco produces approximately 170,000 tonnes of dates annually, compared with domestic consumption of 200,000–250,000 tonnes. Priorities include regulating date imports, improving storage, cooling, packaging and processing facilities, creating employment opportunities and expanding exports. Under the Green Generation 2020–2030 strategy, Morocco aims to increase annual date production to 300,000 tonnes by 2030 through modern irrigation, improved production techniques and support for cooperatives.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries and Food Sovereignty of Morocco

policydecision_details: The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet has approved a 50% subsidy for the purchase of up to two cows from other states to boost livestock farming. Additionally, the government will provide 100 free chicks to poor families to encourage poultry production and launched the State Livestock Mission to improve cattle breeds and milk output. The government will also cover 85% of the insurance premium for cows. Furthermore, the cabinet approved cashless medical treatment for non-teaching school employees and established new inland water transport regulations.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was announced by the Yogi Adityanath government in the lead-up to the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. It aims to increase rural incomes, improve livestock productivity, and provide social welfare support to specific employee groups and poor families.
beneficiaries: poor families, livestock farmers, non-teaching employees

policydecision_details: Uzbekistan has updated its list of authorized Chinese enterprises and orchards permitted to export citrus fruits to the country for the year 2026. The new list includes 241 registered packing facilities located across four Chinese provinces and autonomous regions. Each facility has been assigned a specific registration number to ensure traceability and compliance with phytosanitary standards. These measures are designed to prevent the introduction and spread of quarantine pests while facilitating trade. The initiative aims to strengthen import controls and improve transparency in the citrus trade between China and Uzbekistan.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of Uzbekistan's ongoing efforts to regulate food imports and ensure that agricultural products entering the country meet strict phytosanitary safety requirements. By registering specific packing facilities, the government seeks to mitigate risks associated with quarantine pests and maintain food safety standards for imported produce.
beneficiaries: Chinese citrus exporters, Uzbekistan citrus importers

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The government of Bangladesh is renegotiating Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) for long-delayed solar energy projects. A dedicated committee is reviewing projects approved under the 2010 Special Provisions Act to align tariffs with current market rates. The initiative targets projects that failed to meet construction milestones despite repeated extensions. The government aims to reduce costs that were originally set when equipment and financing prices were significantly higher.
contextoradditionalinfo: Many solar projects in Bangladesh were approved via unsolicited proposals during the previous government's tenure with high tariff rates. As construction costs and solar equipment prices have fallen, the current government is seeking to adjust these contracts to reflect contemporary economic conditions and address implementation delays.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Pakistan has successfully completed the third phase of a project to modernize irrigation water distribution using satellite data and mathematical optimization. The system, known as the Rotation Advisory Module (RAM), aligns water allocations with actual crop requirements rather than traditional fixed schedules. This pilot, covering the Lower Bari Doab Canal system, aims to improve equity and efficiency in water delivery across 675,000 hectares of farmland. The initiative represents a shift toward digital decision-support tools to manage water resources more effectively.
contextoradditionalinfo: The irrigation network in Pakistan is facing significant pressure from climate change, water availability uncertainty, and rising agricultural production costs. Traditional irrigation delivery indicators often failed to account for actual crop water needs, leading to inefficiencies. The project, supported by the Asian Development Bank, seeks to modernize the 'software' of the irrigation system—the operational rules—to ensure fairer and more precise water distribution.

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: A sub-committee constituted by the Prime Minister has established a 120-day deadline to develop a comprehensive roadmap for the expansion of the shrimp farming sector. The initiative involves the formation of seven technical working groups and a projection and costing cell tasked with producing 14 reports to guide sector growth. The roadmap aims to address bottlenecks in production, processing, and value addition while enhancing export competitiveness. Implementation and progress monitoring are scheduled to occur over a 24-month period, involving coordination between federal and provincial institutions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The government is seeking to diversify and expand aquaculture production to increase export earnings and improve value addition within the fisheries sector. Despite potential, the sector faces significant challenges related to effective value chain development, data collection, and traceability, which this initiative intends to resolve through institutional collaboration.
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policydecision_details: Zimbabwe has launched a US$14.33 million pandemic preparedness programme to strengthen disease surveillance, laboratory testing, and emergency response systems. The initiative focuses on improving coordination between human, animal, and environmental health services to detect public health threats early. The project includes the establishment of five public health emergency operations centres and the training of over 10,000 health professionals. It is supported by significant government commitments and development partner co-financing, totaling approximately US$155 million in investment.
contextoradditionalinfo: The programme was initiated in response to previous cholera outbreaks and recurring measles cases, which highlighted the urgent need for effective surveillance and rapid intervention. By strengthening frontline systems and laboratory capacity, the government aims to prevent future health threats from escalating into wider public health emergencies. The initiative also emphasizes the role of local authorities in environmental health management and community-based disease surveillance.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Health and Child Care

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The government of Ghana has adopted a National Communiqué to establish shared priorities for climate and ESG policy and regulation. The policy mandates the integration of climate and ESG considerations into the planning and budgeting of local government assemblies. It also outlines a framework for strengthening climate finance through transparent disclosures and the use of blended finance. Furthermore, the communiqué calls for a coordinated national response to international standards like the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) to improve business competitiveness. Implementation progress will be monitored and reported at future summits.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was developed in response to the need for a unified regulatory direction for climate and ESG implementation in Ghana. It aims to prepare local businesses for emerging global environmental standards and attract sustainable investment. The summit was convened to decode policy and regulation for the 'next economy' and ensure that government, regulators, and the private sector act in alignment.
decision_making_institution: Office of the Minister of State for Climate Change and Sustainability
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The National Water Commission is investing 1.1 billion pesos (US $60 million) into the Lake Pátzcuaro Sanitation Plan to restore the environmental health of the region. The project includes the renovation of six existing wastewater treatment plants and the construction of four new ones. Additionally, the plan involves reconditioning over 116 kilometers of sewer lines, rehabilitating 10 wetlands, and conducting dredging and reforestation activities. These measures aim to mitigate pollution caused by agricultural, industrial, and domestic activities to support local livelihoods.
contextoradditionalinfo: Lake Pátzcuaro is a critical body of water for biodiversity and the cultural heritage of the Indigenous Purépecha peoples. However, the lake has suffered severe degradation due to the excessive use of fertilizers and pesticides, as well as the discharge of untreated wastewater. The restoration is part of the broader 'Plan Michoacán for Peace and Justice' to support the economic and environmental recovery of the region.
beneficiaries: Indigenous communities, lakeshore town residents, fishing communities, tourism sector workers

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Education in Rwanda has introduced comprehensive guidelines for the management of chemical waste in secondary schools and TVET workshops. These regulations mandate standardized procedures for the procurement, storage, labelling, use, and disposal of laboratory chemicals. Schools are required to maintain detailed records, ensure secure storage, and engage licensed providers for waste collection. The policy aims to protect students, staff, and the environment from the risks associated with hazardous chemical accumulation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was developed following a 2023 national assessment that identified nearly 27 tonnes of expired or unidentified chemicals in 197 secondary schools. A subsequent collection exercise across 574 institutions resulted in the removal of over 63 tonnes of hazardous chemical waste. The government introduced these rules to prevent future unsafe accumulation and to standardize safety protocols across educational and research institutions.

policydecision_details: The Cabinet of Rwanda has approved the Rwanda Development Cooperation Policy 2026–2050, which replaces the 2006 Aid Policy. This new framework shifts the country's approach to development cooperation by moving beyond traditional aid to include all forms of financing aligned with national goals. It emphasizes the participation of diverse stakeholders, including the private sector, civil society, and academia. The policy aims to mobilize and coordinate financing for large-scale, high-impact flagship projects to ensure sustainable development results.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to reflect the evolving global and national development financing landscape. It is designed to better align international and domestic financing sources with Rwanda's long-term development priorities and vision.
decision_making_institution: Cabinet of the Republic of Rwanda

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Government of Rwanda and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) have signed a US$ 24 million grant agreement to fund the third phase of a project to rehabilitate electricity substations and the distribution network. This initiative includes reinforcing the 110KV transmission line and constructing a new substation at Gasogi in the Gasabo district. The project aims to enhance the stability of the power supply, reduce the risk of large-scale outages, and support the growing electricity demand in Kigali. By improving infrastructure, the government intends to foster economic growth and improve the delivery of essential services such as health and education.
contextoradditionalinfo: Rwanda has experienced steady economic growth of approximately 7 percent in recent years, leading to an annual increase in power demand of over 10 percent. Kigali accounts for roughly 64% of the country's total power consumption, making infrastructure upgrades critical to preventing outages and supporting foreign direct investment. This agreement represents the third phase of a long-standing collaboration between Rwanda and JICA to modernize the national electricity network.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Belarus and Mongolia signed 17 agreements and memorandums worth $50 million during a bilateral business forum. The deals cover cooperation in sectors including rail transport, construction, agricultural machinery, and food and dairy supplies. Additionally, the two leaders signed a roadmap for cooperation spanning 2027-2029 to strengthen trade and economic relations. These measures aim to create a favorable business environment and provide tangible economic benefits to both nations.
contextoradditionalinfo: The agreements follow bilateral talks between the presidents of Belarus and Mongolia to enhance trade turnover, which stood at $21.5 million in 2025. The cooperation roadmap is intended to expand ties in various sectors including agriculture, heavy and light industry, and science. This initiative is part of a broader effort to improve the well-being of the populations of both countries through increased economic integration.

policydecision_details: The Serbian government has revised the documentation requirements for accelerated value-added tax (VAT) refunds for manufacturers and exporters, effective January 1, 2027. The reform shifts the criteria for establishing 'predominant exporter' status from annual financial statements to VAT accounting records. Qualifying companies will continue to benefit from a preferential 15-day VAT refund deadline, compared to the standard 45-day period. To qualify, companies must demonstrate that exports exceed 50% of total turnover or reach a value of at least €10 million. This measure aims to improve industrial liquidity and streamline the administrative process for tax refunds.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to modernize how companies document their eligibility for accelerated VAT refunds, ensuring that tax reporting is more closely aligned with actual export performance. By providing faster access to liquidity, the government aims to support capital-intensive industries and facilitate investment in production capacity. The change also addresses the need for more consistent financial and VAT documentation in light of increasing compliance demands on Serbian exporters.

policydecision_details: The government of Togo has announced the Medium-Term Revenue Mobilization Strategy (SRMT) for 2027-2031, aiming to increase tax revenue to CFA francs 2,109 billion by 2031. The strategy focuses on broadening the tax base, digitizing revenue collection, and rationalizing tax expenditures. Key measures include the implementation of certified electronic invoicing and the use of online platforms like e-TPU for tax declarations. This fiscal reform is designed to align the country's tax-to-GDP ratio with the regional benchmark of 20%.
contextoradditionalinfo: Togo's tax-to-GDP ratio was estimated at 13.1% in 2025, which is significantly below the regional benchmark of 20%. The government identified this gap as a primary driver for the new fiscal reform agenda, seeking to increase domestic resource mobilization while maintaining private sector competitiveness.
beneficiaries: 2029 and 2031, businesses as the, about 30, applications to translate, businesses, this trajectory, 2027, african institutions and, customs dispute settlement

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: The Luxembourg government has presented its draft 2027 State Budget, totaling €35.8 billion, with a strong focus on purchasing power, social cohesion, and well-being. Key measures include a 3.8% increase in the social minimum wage, a new cost-of-living supplement, and significant investments in affordable housing and childcare. The budget also introduces tax reforms, including a single tax class and reduced corporate income tax for SMEs. Additionally, it allocates substantial funding for digital and energy transitions, research, and infrastructure development to support long-term growth.
contextoradditionalinfo: The budget, titled 'Fir d’Leit. Fir Opschwong' (For the People. For Growth.), was introduced against a backdrop of moderate economic growth to support households and the economy. It aims to strengthen the Luxembourg model by protecting social cohesion and maintaining sound public finances while addressing the rising cost of living and housing. The government intends to use this fiscal framework to navigate uncertain economic times and provide new prospects for citizens and businesses.
beneficiaries: households, low-income individuals, small and medium-sized enterprises, children
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: The Liberia Airport Authority has unveiled a five-year, US$59 million strategic plan (2027–2031) to modernize Roberts International Airport and secondary domestic airports. The plan focuses on critical aviation safety, security, and financial management reforms to establish Liberia as a competitive logistics hub. A key component includes the development of specialized cargo facilities, such as temperature-controlled storage, to support the export of agricultural products and seafood. The strategy aims to improve domestic connectivity and reduce post-harvest losses for Liberian producers through enhanced cold-chain infrastructure.
contextoradditionalinfo: The plan addresses longstanding challenges in the Liberian aviation sector, including outdated navigation systems, inadequate emergency equipment, and weak financial controls. The authority identified a low international aviation audit score of 27 percent as a primary driver for urgent safety and regulatory compliance upgrades. Additionally, the initiative seeks to diversify revenue streams and reduce reliance on government appropriations by fostering public-private partnerships and expanding cargo-handling capacity.

policydecision_details: The Irish government has announced a €1.3485 billion allocation for Budget 2027 to support enterprise growth, innovation, and job creation. Key measures include the establishment of 'Start Up Ireland', a €500 million expansion of the Growth and Sustainability Loan Scheme, and a €1 billion investment programme through the Ireland Strategic Investment Fund. The budget also introduces tax packages for businesses and individuals, including adjustments to the National Minimum Wage and Employer PRSI thresholds. These initiatives aim to strengthen competitiveness, accelerate AI adoption, and provide long-term financial support for SMEs, farmers, and fishers.
contextoradditionalinfo: Budget 2027 was developed to address business cost pressures, enhance national competitiveness, and foster an environment conducive to scaling indigenous firms. It builds upon recommendations from the Cost of Business Advisory Forum and aligns with broader EU initiatives such as the EU AI Act. The funding is intended to ensure economic resilience and support sustainable growth across various sectors, including tourism and high-growth industries.
beneficiaries: SMEs, entrepreneurs, farmers, fishers, small mid-caps

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Chad has secured a $12.625 million grant from the Adaptation Fund to enhance community resilience against climate change. This funding is part of the broader ECOVERSE project, which has a total approved allocation of $25.25 million. The grant aims to support sustainable development initiatives and improve the capacity of local populations to adapt to environmental risks. This decision follows previous climate financing efforts, including a $25 million grant from the Green Climate Fund earlier in 2026.
contextoradditionalinfo: Chad is facing growing environmental pressures and climate-related challenges that threaten local livelihoods. To address these, the government has set a short-term target of mobilizing $100 million in international climate finance. This grant represents a significant step in the country's climate diplomacy and its ongoing efforts to secure resources for sustainable development and climate adaptation.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The French government has announced a roadmap to address grievances raised by protesting students regarding the university admissions platform Parcoursup, school infrastructure, and class sizes. The plan includes immediate measures to be integrated into the 2027 budget and long-term projects to be carried out over the coming months. A two-stage reform of the Parcoursup platform has been proposed, with initial changes scheduled for the 2027 cycle and a full replacement by 2028. Legislative debates regarding the necessary legal changes are set to begin at the Assemblée Nationale on October 28.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced following five weeks of widespread high school and university blockades and demonstrations across France. The government launched an online consultation in early October that gathered over 100,000 contributions, which informed the development of this response to the student movement.

policydecision_details: Mexico has resumed live cattle exports from the Puerto Palomas quarantine station to Columbus, New Mexico, as part of a phased reopening strategy coordinated with the USDA. The resumption allows for an initial daily flow of approximately 750 head of cattle, contributing to a broader average of 3,500 head exported daily through various border ports. This decision follows strict adherence to sanitary measures agreed upon by SENASICA and APHIS to ensure animal health standards are maintained. The reopening is part of a larger effort to restore trade routes that had been temporarily suspended.
contextoradditionalinfo: The reopening of the Columbus crossing is the third in a series of phased restorations of cattle trade between Mexico and the United States, following previous reopenings in Douglas, Arizona, and Santa Teresa, New Mexico. The trade activity is critical for supporting small-scale ranchers and local supply chains in the border region. However, the resumption occurs against the backdrop of ongoing New World screwworm detections in both US livestock and wildlife, necessitating continued vigilance and the construction of a new sterile fly production facility to manage long-term sanitary risks.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development (SADER)
beneficiaries: small-scale ranchers, collectors, transporters, local communities

policydecision_details: Distributed 41 olive harvesters, 41 agricultural ladders and 205 olive-harvesting nets to farmers in Na’alin, Taybeh and Ein Sinya in the occupied West Bank. The equipment was funded by the Occupied Palestinian Territory Humanitarian Fund under an emergency agricultural assistance project targeting vulnerable farmers and livestock keepers. The intervention aims to facilitate olive harvesting, improve operational efficiency, preserve crop quality and reduce the burden on farmers during the harvest season. It also seeks to protect agricultural livelihoods, help Palestinian farmers remain on their land and strengthen household incomes and food security amid ongoing challenges facing the agricultural sector.
decision_making_institution: The Ramallah and Al-Bireh Directorate of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Begun implementing its autumn plan to propagate medicinal and aromatic plants at the Al-Shuhaymiyah forest site in Wasit Governorate. Preparatory activities include land preparation, opening planting rows, installing filtration pipes to regulate irrigation, and applying organic fertilizer to improve soil conditions and support crop growth. The plan will focus on cultivating anise and coriander, aiming to make better use of available agricultural land, increase production and strengthen the programme for propagating medicinal and aromatic plants.

Signed the United Nations Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents, also known as the Accra Convention. This treaty establishes a common legal framework for documents representing goods transported by road, rail, air, or sea. It aims to simplify cargo transactions, reduce paperwork, and enable businesses to use goods in transit as security for financing. The convention will enter into force once 10 states have ratified or acceded to it.
contextoradditionalinfo: Existing maritime shipping documents like bills of lading allow traders to use goods as security for financing while in transit, but these benefits were previously unavailable for road, rail, and air transport. The Accra Convention addresses this gap by introducing negotiable cargo documents that can be used across different modes of transport, facilitating cross-border trade and improving access to finance for businesses.

policy_description: Establishment or modification of food stock
policydecision_details: The government of Belarus has set a target for an apple harvest exceeding 200,000 tonnes for the 2026 season. This initiative supports the expansion of domestic processing capabilities and the enhancement of storage facilities to ensure a year-round supply of apples. Under the national stabilisation-stock programme, 27,000 tonnes of apples are specifically reserved to maintain market stability. The policy also encourages the adoption of intensive orchard practices to improve yields and productivity.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is driven by the need to ensure domestic food security following a challenging agricultural season marked by extreme weather conditions, including a severe winter and spring temperature fluctuations. By focusing on storage and processing, the government aims to mitigate the impact of seasonal production volatility and reduce reliance on imports. The initiative also reflects ongoing efforts to modernize the fruit sector through research into new varieties and the adoption of high-density planting techniques.
policycategory: Establishment or modification of food stock

policydecision_details: Issued a directive urging farmers to adopt early-maturing seed varieties to mitigate the impact of the looming El Niño phenomenon. Farmers are encouraged to capitalize on early rainfall to ensure crops reach maturity before potential dry spells occur. Additionally, the ministry has provided guidance on livestock management, including the use of nutritional supplements and improved water access to protect herds. Farmers are also advised to consider climate-resilient crops like cassava and to practice intercropping to reduce production risks. These measures aim to safeguard agricultural productivity and food security in the face of anticipated adverse weather conditions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to the looming El Niño phenomenon, which threatens agricultural production across the SADC region. The Ministry of Agriculture identified a high risk of prolonged dry spells that could lead to crop failure and livestock health issues. The directive follows discussions on climate resilience held during the Second African Vegetable Forum in Eswatini.

policydecision_details: Ukrainian Railways (UZ) has announced a planned 15% increase in freight tariffs effective from 1 January 2027. This follows a previous 30% tariff hike implemented on 1 August 2026. The decision is driven by the carrier's need to address rising operating costs, industrial inflation, and significant net losses. The iron and steel sector, which relies heavily on rail for exports due to port blockades, is the primary target of these tariff adjustments.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Ukrainian iron and steel sector is facing severe logistical challenges due to the ongoing war, including the blockage of Black Sea ports and damage to railway infrastructure. With over 500 locomotives destroyed or damaged, the sector is struggling with high transport costs and reduced export capacity. Industry stakeholders argue that continuous tariff hikes create a destructive economic spiral and have called for international funding and a moratorium on fare increases.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: The Zambian government has announced a projected 7% increase in spending for the 2027 national budget, with total expenditure expected to reach approximately $13.8 billion. To address the projected revenue shortfall of $11.1 billion, the government plans to secure $2.3 billion in new loans, primarily from the domestic market. This fiscal strategy aims to support national economic growth and infrastructure development. The budget planning process includes public hearings to finalize the allocation of resources.
contextoradditionalinfo: The budget announcement follows a period of economic adjustment where the Zambian economy is forecast to grow by 5.3% in 2026. The government is also banking on a significant increase in copper production, which is expected to rise to 1.08 million tonnes in 2027, to bolster national revenues. The current borrowing plan is higher than the $1.8 billion projected for the previous year, reflecting the government's fiscal requirements.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Türkiye Climate Action Acceleration Program (TCAAP) is a multi-sectoral initiative designed to operationalize the country's Climate Law and Second Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0). The program focuses on three pillars: establishing a carbon market and green finance regulatory architecture, accelerating sectoral decarbonization, and institutionalizing climate adaptation across water, nature, and health systems. It is supported by $1.6 billion in financing from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB). The program aims to translate legislative commitments into measurable climate outcomes through institutional and policy reforms.
contextoradditionalinfo: Türkiye's economic growth model remains structurally dependent on fossil fuel imports, which drives current account deficits and external vulnerability. As a major greenhouse gas emitter, the country faces pressure from the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and physical climate risks affecting water, ecosystems, and health. The TCAAP was developed to address the gap in the regulatory and institutional architecture needed to channel capital toward climate targets and mitigate these economic and environmental risks.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Palli Karma-Sahayak Foundation (PKSF) and the Institute of Architects Bangladesh (IAB) are launching a design competition for climate-smart houses. This initiative aims to promote innovative and resilient housing solutions suitable for the climate challenges faced by the poor and disadvantaged populations in Bangladesh. The competition is part of PKSF's broader mandate to foster development and build resilience among vulnerable communities. By engaging with architectural experts, the organization seeks to improve living conditions and long-term sustainability for its beneficiaries.
contextoradditionalinfo: PKSF is an apex development organization established by the Government of Bangladesh in 1989 to alleviate poverty through employment generation. The organization works with over 223 partner organizations to provide financial and institutional support to the poor, small farmers, and micro-entrepreneurs. Given the increasing impact of climate change on vulnerable populations, PKSF is shifting its focus toward climate-resilient interventions to ensure sustainable development results.
beneficiaries: micro-entrepreneurs, small and marginal farmers, extremely poor
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Distributed agricultural supplies to farmers in Tubas and the Northern Jordan Valley through its government-funded emergency response programme, aiming to sustain agricultural production and help farmers maintain access to and use of their land amid displacement, land confiscation, property destruction and movement restrictions. The assistance included 600 three-year-old olive seedlings, 6 tonnes of wheat seeds, 76 water tanks, 53 tarpaulins and 26.5 tonnes of straw to support crop production, water storage and livestock farming. The intervention seeks to ease farmers’ financial burdens, address water shortages, protect productive assets and sustain rural household livelihoods. It also forms part of wider efforts to safeguard agricultural resources, maintain local production and strengthen Palestinian food security.

Established 78 one-stop shops nationwide to support farmers during the 2026–2027 plowing and sowing campaign by simplifying administrative and financing procedures and improving access to seeds and fertilisers. Farmers can obtain financing through the Bank of Agriculture and Rural Development (BADR) under the Rfig credit scheme, while supplier credit supports farmers affected by climatic hazards or fires who face difficulties accessing bank loans. The campaign requires an estimated 2.5 million quintals of cereal seeds, while available stocks amount to 3.5 million quintals. The OAIC is also strengthening production capacity through 20 new seed-processing stations equipped with optical sorting technology, modern agricultural machinery and technical support from 700 agricultural engineers and technicians. Storage infrastructure includes 350 local storage centres, alongside 35 planned grain silos, 30 of which are under construction, and 16 metal silos.

Unveiled the Dubai Food Security Strategy 2030, aligned with the UAE National Food Security Strategy 2051. The strategy focuses on five pillars: food availability, affordability, quality and safety, sustainability and resilience, and industry empowerment. Its five strategic initiatives aim to increase sustainable local food production through fisheries, livestock development and small-scale farmer cooperatives; strengthen supply-chain resilience by diversifying food import sources and engaging strategic commodity importers; promote healthy diets and reduce food loss and waste; improve food-system governance and attract investment in agricultural technology; and develop resilient infrastructure and international research partnerships. Implementation will be coordinated by DECCA’s Food Security Department with local and federal government entities and private-sector stakeholders.
decision_making_institution: The Dubai Environment and Climate Change Authority (DECCA)

policydecision_details: The Parliament of Türkiye has approved legislation to provide interim payments of up to 1 million Turkish Liras to investors affected by troubled funds currently under liquidation. The measure applies to funds ordered into liquidation by the Capital Markets Board (SPK) on September 17, 2026, and includes investors whose redemption orders were blocked due to fund defaults. Payments are calculated based on net cash deposits and will be deducted from final settlements. The legislation also establishes a framework for the Savings Deposit Insurance Fund (TMSF) to pursue asset recovery from responsible portfolio management companies and individuals.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to the collapse and subsequent liquidation of several investment funds, which left many investors unable to access their capital. The government aims to mitigate financial losses for these investors while holding management companies accountable for the fund failures.
budget: 1 million Turkish Liras per eligible investor

policydecision_details: Uzbekistan and Egypt signed a memorandum of cooperation to strengthen agricultural ties, focusing on livestock farming, veterinary medicine, and scientific research. The agreement facilitates the exchange of best practices in food security, water resource management, and environmental protection. Specific initiatives include improving the efficiency of livestock farms, enhancing the quality of dairy and meat products, and developing sheep farming. The parties also aim to increase animal productivity and reproduction rates while collaborating on veterinary disease prevention and medicine supply.
contextoradditionalinfo: The memorandum was established following a meeting between Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Economy and Finance and an Egyptian delegation led by the president of the Egyptian Agricultural Research Centre. The collaboration seeks to leverage Egyptian expertise to modernize Uzbekistan's livestock sector, expand pastureland in the Kashkadarya Region, and bring unused land into agricultural production.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Economy and Finance of Uzbekistan

policydecision_details: The Greek government has unveiled a comprehensive package of housing measures to alleviate rent pressures, including the launch of the €2 billion My Home III programme in January 2027. The initiative features renovation subsidies for older homes, tax incentives for long-term rentals, and restrictions on new short-term rental registrations in major cities. Additionally, the government is expanding rent refunds for eligible recipients and introducing new social housing projects through the renovation of public buildings and military camps. A new tax bill will be submitted to Parliament in November to formalize these arrangements and adjust property tax exemptions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to address long-term housing needs, rising rent costs, and the market distortion caused by the shift of residential properties into short-term accommodation sectors like Airbnb. By incentivizing long-term leasing and increasing the supply of energy-efficient housing, the government aims to stabilize the housing market and improve affordability for households.
beneficiaries: households, tenants, property owners, doctors and nurses, public-school teachers, uniformed personnel

policydecision_details: Adopted a package of measures to support the olive oil sector and ensure the smooth implementation of the 2026–2027 season. The plan allocates TND 150 million through public and private banks to the National Olive Oil Office (ONH) to purchase domestic production and provides TND 20 million in preferential loans to small farmers through the Tunisian Solidarity Bank (BTS). Additional support includes priority subsidies for mechanical harvesting equipment, a proposed TND 100 million financing line for 2027–2030, and a storage programme covering up to 60,000 tonnes of olive oil, supported by incentives. To strengthen exports, transport subsidies for olive oil exporters will increase from 50% to 60%, while targeted programmes will promote packaged and organic olive oil, support young exporting companies, and explore new international markets. The measures also include enhanced farmer training in quality, pruning, disease control and mechanization, improved access to bank financing and debt rescheduling, and plans to restructure the ONH and develop a long-term strategy for the sector.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Strengthened the capacity of 111,508 farmers to cope with climate risks and provided agricultural services and assets to 63,812 farmers. The programme has developed more than 2.24 million cubic metres of rainwater harvesting and storage capacity, improved water availability for livestock for 10,650 households in Badia areas, and trained 3,313 farmers in climate-smart agriculture. It has also distributed 852,000 drought-resistant seedlings and supported the rehabilitation of agricultural nurseries and veterinary service centres. Despite satisfactory progress toward its development objectives, several components remain behind their targets, particularly agricultural traceability, export development, digital extension services and access to financing for water-saving technologies. With total financing of USD 241 million and implementation planned through 2030, the programme aims to strengthen climate resilience, improve agricultural productivity and develop agricultural value chains in Jordan.
decision_making_institution: The Agriculture Resilience, Value Chain Development and Innovation Program (Ardi)
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Launched the Protection and Security Plan for the 2026/2027 coffee harvest to ensure the stability and safety of the production cycle. The plan involves the deployment of the Nicaraguan Army and the National Police to provide security for producers, transporters, and exporters across 60 coffee-growing municipalities. It emphasizes the importance of maintaining peace and stability to facilitate investment and efficient trade. The initiative also includes ongoing technical assistance, training through coffee schools, and infrastructure support to enhance the quality and competitiveness of Nicaraguan coffee.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is introduced to address the need for security in the coffee sector, which is a fundamental pillar of the Nicaraguan economy, involving over 55,000 families and generating significant employment. The government aims to mitigate risks associated with climate change and market volatility by ensuring that production and logistics remain uninterrupted. This plan builds on previous successful harvest protection efforts to maintain economic growth and support the livelihoods of rural populations.
beneficiaries: coffee producers, coffee workers, rural families

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Government Resolution No. 586 mandates that greenhouse farms in Tashkent and five surrounding districts transition to cleaner energy sources like natural gas, electricity, or solar power. Operators must install continuous emissions monitoring systems and adhere to strict waste management protocols for hazardous byproducts. To facilitate this transition, the government is providing financial support, including 50% cost compensation for equipment and low-interest loans for technology upgrades. Additionally, imports of non-locally manufactured greenhouse modernization equipment are exempt from customs duties until 2030. The policy aims to balance industrial development with environmental protection by reducing air pollution in the capital region.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to address environmental concerns regarding air quality in Tashkent and surrounding districts caused by greenhouse heating systems using solid fuels like coal and biomass. By enforcing stricter environmental standards and providing financial incentives for modernization, the government seeks to promote sustainable agricultural practices and resource efficiency.
budget: 50 million soums per hectare (compensation); 3 billion soums per hectare (loan cap); 350 million soums per station (CEMS funding)
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis has approved a revised Law on Waste in its first reading to overhaul waste management regulations. The bill introduces updated rules for waste collection, transportation, sorting, recycling, and disposal, while establishing a unified waste catalogue with five hazard classes. It mandates stricter oversight of waste transport, including licensing requirements and certification for hazardous waste vehicles. Additionally, the legislation clarifies the responsibilities of government agencies and local administrations regarding waste accounting, digitalization, and infrastructure management.
contextoradditionalinfo: The current waste management law was adopted 24 years ago and has become outdated due to significant increases in production and consumption, the emergence of new waste types, and the development of modern recycling technologies. The sector has faced persistent challenges, including inefficient sorting and recycling, service fee calculation issues, and inadequate handling of construction, industrial, and medical waste. This revision aims to modernize the legal framework to support a circular economy and improve environmental safety.
decision_making_institution: Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis
beneficiaries: waste management operators, municipal authorities, industrial sector

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Bangladesh has issued the Special Solar Power Installation Ordinance, 2026, to facilitate private-sector investment in rooftop solar installations on government and public buildings. The ordinance introduces Opex and Capex models to address regulatory gaps regarding electricity tariffs, rooftop rentals, and maintenance. It covers solar systems up to 5 MW, including applications for irrigation pumps, cold storage, and agrivoltaic systems. Additionally, the policy simplifies procurement by exempting these projects from mandatory Electronic Government Procurement (e-GP) requirements to accelerate deployment.
contextoradditionalinfo: The government aims to add 3 GW to 4 GW of renewable energy capacity before next summer. Previous legislation lacked clear provisions for long-term electricity tariffs and maintenance arrangements, which hindered the deployment of rooftop solar on government-owned buildings.
beneficiaries: government institutions, state-owned companies, private-sector investors, tea garden owners
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The Ministry of National Food Security & Research has inaugurated the upgraded Central Plant Quarantine Laboratory and the Federal Pesticides Testing and Reference Laboratory in Karachi. These facilities are designed to strengthen agricultural biosecurity and improve pesticide quality assurance. The upgrade aims to enhance the diagnostic capabilities for identifying pests and diseases in imported commodities while ensuring that agricultural inputs meet international standards. By providing reliable laboratory results, the government intends to facilitate compliance with phytosanitary requirements and boost the competitiveness of Pakistani agricultural exports.
contextoradditionalinfo: Agriculture is the backbone of Pakistan's economy, and protecting crops from pests and diseases is vital for food security and export growth. The government identified a need for modern scientific infrastructure to meet international standards and ensure the safety and quality of agricultural products. This initiative addresses the requirement for evidence-based regulatory decisions and effective enforcement of agricultural standards to protect domestic crops and facilitate international trade.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of National Food Security & Research

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: The Estonian government has endorsed a proposal to postpone certain verification and reporting requirements under the EU Methane Regulation by one year. This decision aims to provide companies and producers with additional time to establish necessary monitoring and reporting systems. By delaying these requirements, the government seeks to prevent potential supply disruptions and mitigate price pressures on the European energy market. The policy does not suspend the regulation itself but adjusts the implementation timeline to ensure feasibility for market participants.
contextoradditionalinfo: Estonia's gas supply is heavily dependent on international deliveries and the regional market. The government expressed concern that if fuel suppliers are unable to meet the new EU methane reporting requirements by the original deadline, the range of available supplies could shrink, leading to increased costs and reduced availability for Estonian consumers. The decision reflects a balance between environmental objectives and the practical need to maintain energy security and market stability.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: The Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA) has launched two new trade platforms, the Accra Trade House and the Friday Market, to support local businesses in reaching international buyers. The Accra Trade House serves as a permanent showroom and sales center for locally made goods, while the Friday Market provides a monthly event for direct sales to consumers and wholesalers. These initiatives aim to improve product competitiveness and help producers meet international market standards. The ultimate goal is to increase annual nontraditional export earnings to at least $10 billion by 2030.
contextoradditionalinfo: The launch follows a significant 30.7% increase in Ghana's nontraditional export earnings in 2025, reaching $5.006 billion. These initiatives are part of a broader national strategy to strengthen the export industry, support the 24-hour economy program, and leverage opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

policydecision_details: Sudan's Sovereignty Council chairman, Abdelfattah El Burhan, has officially cancelled a previous cabinet decision that banned the importation of 46 specific goods. The Finance Minister, Jibril Ibrahim, stated that this measure was taken to address the urgent needs of consumers facing high prices. The decision aims to improve the availability of essential goods in the market. Traders and consumers have already reported an immediate decrease in the prices of some of these goods following the announcement.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to a severe economic crisis characterized by high inflation (28.29%) and a significant depreciation of the Sudanese Pound, which reached 10,300 SDG against the Dollar. The ongoing conflict has destroyed much of the country's productive base, leading to a heavy reliance on imports and fragmented supply chains. The government is attempting to balance the need for affordable consumer goods with the challenges of a volatile currency and a struggling domestic production sector.

policydecision_details: Somalia and Uganda have signed a bilateral labor agreement to protect over 20,000 Ugandan workers employed in Somalia. The agreement mandates written employment contracts, direct salary payments into bank accounts, and employer-funded insurance and travel expenses. It prohibits forced labor and passport confiscation while ensuring workers' rights to communicate with their families and diplomatic representatives. The policy will remain in force for three years and will take effect following internal ratification by both governments.
contextoradditionalinfo: The agreement follows commitments made during the second session of the Somalia-Uganda Joint Permanent Commission in October 2025 to expand cooperation in labor and migration. It aims to address issues such as unlawful dismissals, unpaid wages, and the exploitation of workers by recruitment agencies.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs (Somalia) and Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development (Uganda)

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: The European Union has introduced Regulation (EU) 2026/2202, which significantly updates air passenger rights starting October 23, 2027. The new rules mandate automatic refunds within seven calendar days for flight cancellations and establish compensation of up to 600 euros for significant delays. It also clarifies obligations for airlines regarding alternative transport, meals, and hotel accommodations. Furthermore, the regulation prohibits the 'no-show' practice and mandates transparency in carry-on luggage policies.
contextoradditionalinfo: The regulation serves as a comprehensive reform of air passenger protection rules that have been in place since 2004. It aims to reduce conflicts between passengers and airlines by providing clearer definitions of extraordinary circumstances and strengthening the burden of proof on airlines. This is particularly relevant for international travelers, including those on routes between Europe and Cuba, ensuring standardized protection regardless of the airline's origin.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policy_description: Public/mutual fund and contingent risk financing
policydecision_details: The government of South Sudan announced it would receive more than $50 million in United Nations emergency funding to prepare for El Niño, as government planning scenarios warn of potential drought and flooding affecting millions of people. The funding will support anticipatory action, including cash assistance for vulnerable families, measures to protect crops and livestock, and moving humanitarian supplies before floods cut off roads and isolate communities.
policycategory: Public/mutual fund and contingent risk financing

policy_description: Public/mutual fund and contingent risk financing
policydecision_details: UN announced the release of millions of dollars from the Central Emergency Response Fund to address the severe impacts of drought linked to the El Niño phenomenon in South Sudan, Zimbabwe, and Chad. The UN noted that six million dollars of this amount will support early action in South Sudan to combat the worsening drought, which Fletcher warned poses a threat to lives and livelihoods. The international organization explained that these resources will help secure food, health, nutrition, protection services, and water and sanitation.
policycategory: Public/mutual fund and contingent risk financing

policydecision_details: Prime Minister has ordered an increase in the monthly minimum wage for workers in the textile, garment, footwear, and travel goods sectors to $212 for 2027. This decision follows negotiations by the National Council on Minimum Wage and includes an additional $2.50 monthly allowance for travel and accommodation. The total effective minimum wage package for these workers will reach $214.50 per month. The government aims to balance workers' living standards with national competitiveness and investment attraction.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decision was made following a period of negotiation between employer and worker representatives, who remained divided on the wage increase. The Prime Minister intervened after a secret ballot by the council resulted in a proposal to keep the wage at $210. This measure is part of the government's broader strategy to support workers' livelihoods while maintaining the country's investment climate.
beneficiaries: textile workers, garment workers, footwear workers, travel goods and bags sector workers

policy_description: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
policydecision_details: Uzbekistan has introduced a new procedure allowing socially significant projects to access government artificial intelligence infrastructure at no cost or at discounted rates.
