Eligible entities, including startups, universities, and research organizations, can receive up to 10 million free tokens per month for large language models for a period of up to six months. Projects exceeding this limit are eligible for a 50% discount on additional allocations of up to 50 million tokens. The infrastructure supports model training, testing, validation, and inference, with beneficiaries selected through a competitive scoring process held twice annually.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of Uzbekistan's broader efforts to foster digital technology and artificial intelligence development. It follows the recent approval of ethical rules for AI-based solutions, which came into force in June 2026, ensuring that AI implementation remains regulated and aligned with human rights and safety standards.
beneficiaries: higher education institutions, scientific organizations, startups, advisers to regional governors
policycategory: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination

policydecision_details: The government has introduced the Municipal Corporations (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which seeks to establish the City of Chaguanas and the Boroughs of Barataria, Couva, St. Augustine, and Sangre Grande. This legislative act includes consequential amendments to several existing laws, including the Representation of the People Act and the Motor Vehicles and Road Traffic Regulations. The bill is currently published for public information as part of the Trinidad and Tobago Gazette. This institutional reform aims to restructure local government administration within the country.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a broader legislative effort to reorganize municipal boundaries and administrative structures in Trinidad and Tobago to improve local governance.

policydecision_details: The Federal Government of Nigeria has launched the Trade Intelligence Tools to provide businesses with critical market data to enhance export competitiveness. This initiative aims to assist MSMEs in identifying global market opportunities, understanding international trade standards, and connecting with potential buyers. By leveraging data-driven insights, the government seeks to accelerate the country's progress toward a $1 trillion economy by 2030. The tools include comprehensive reports on trade and investment performance to support informed commercial decision-making and strategic policymaking.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to address structural barriers to business growth in Nigeria, such as high production costs, limited access to finance, and complex trade procedures. It is part of a broader economic reform agenda intended to translate government policies into tangible outcomes like job creation and industrial expansion. The initiative builds upon a pilot version launched in 2025 to foster a more data-centric approach to trade facilitation and economic development.

policydecision_details: The National Economic Council has endorsed a 90-day economic action plan aimed at mitigating the cost of living crisis in Nigeria. The plan focuses on five priority areas: food affordability, tax harmonization, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks, and regulated household support. It includes specific initiatives such as a joint financing framework for CNG and electric vehicles to reduce transportation costs and efforts to unlock the economic potential of the livestock sector. The policy seeks to translate macroeconomic reforms into tangible benefits for citizens through improved fiscal coordination and targeted interventions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to consolidate the gains of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s economic reform program. It addresses the need to translate national economic objectives into improved living conditions for Nigerians, specifically targeting inflation reduction and the removal of barriers to investment and essential services.

policydecision_details: The Council of Ministers of Cuba has approved a training and job placement program for youth aged 18 to 30 who are neither studying nor working. Participants will undergo training courses lasting one to six months, during which they will receive a monthly income equivalent to the minimum wage of 3,210 Cuban pesos. The program aims to reintegrate these individuals into the educational, productive, and service systems to enhance their employability. Beneficiaries must meet attendance and performance requirements to maintain their income, and the program is managed by municipal offices of Labor and Social Security.
contextoradditionalinfo: Youth disconnection has been a persistent issue in Cuba, with official data from 2023 estimating approximately 800,000 young people neither studying nor working. The government has been implementing various labor and salary transformations to address this, following previous initiatives that incorporated thousands of young people into the workforce. This specific program was announced in June 2026 as part of a broader effort to improve labor market participation and social inclusion.

policydecision_details: The measure provides emergency support to the road haulage, agriculture, and fishing sectors to cushion the impact of rising fuel prices, preserve business liquidity, and maintain the functioning of critical supply chains. It allocates approximately $50.6 million (€45.2 million) in diesel tax credits for road haulage companies for fuel expenses incurred between March and August 2026, followed by a further $67.2 million (€60 million) for expenses incurred between 1 September and 5 October 2026. In addition, the government has postponed the implementation of the customs contribution on low-value shipments by one month, from 1 December 2026 to 1 January 2027. The package also includes up to $67.2 million (€60 million) in non-repayable grants for eligible agricultural businesses, administered through direct payments by AGEA, to partially compensate fuel costs incurred between 1 June and 15 October 2026, up to €0.45 per litre. In total, the measures provide around $185 million (€165.2 million) in support to mitigate the effects of energy price volatility.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to the rising costs of fuel, which threatened the operational viability of critical sectors including road transport, agriculture, and fishing. By providing liquidity support, the government aims to prevent market disruptions and ensure the continued supply of essential goods.
beneficiaries: road haulage operators, agricultural businesses, fishing sector businesses

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: Signed the law 'On aquaculture (fish farming)' to establish a comprehensive regulatory framework for the sector. The law introduces new legal definitions for aquaculture systems and sets foundations for the economic and organizational operation of production facilities. Additionally, the President signed laws amending land reclamation regulations and improving the identification, registration, and traceability of farm animals. These measures aim to protect the rights of industry entities and enhance the quality and supply of domestic fish and animal products. The legislation is intended to bring existing practices into compliance with current regulatory standards.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to fill a gap in the legal framework governing the aquaculture sector and to modernize regulations regarding land reclamation and animal traceability. By formalizing these sectors, the government aims to foster development in new production facilities and ensure the domestic market is better supplied with high-quality, locally produced food.
decision_making_institution: President of the Republic of Belarus
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policydecision_details: Costa Rica has officially opened international bidding for a $770 million highway expansion project connecting San José and San Ramón. The project involves upgrading 55.6 kilometers of Route 1, including the addition of traffic lanes, bridge improvements, and the construction of a new connecting road. The initiative aims to alleviate chronic traffic congestion that has impacted the region for decades. The government has secured international financing from the Central American Bank for Economic Integration and the OPEC Fund for International Development to support the construction. Bidding remains open until April 2027, with the goal of completing the expanded highway by the end of 2031.
contextoradditionalinfo: The San José–San Ramón highway is a critical transportation corridor for commuters, delivery trucks, and tourists, serving approximately 170,000 motorists daily. The project has faced years of delays and abandoned private concession plans, leading the government to adopt a publicly financed model to finally address the severe traffic congestion affecting the Central Valley and surrounding areas.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MOPT)

policydecision_details: The Government of Japan has committed E21 million to provide emergency food assistance for 27,500 orphans and vulnerable children in Eswatini. Implemented through the World Food Programme, the grant ensures children at Neighbourhood Care Points receive at least one hot meal five days a week. The aid package includes canned fish, white maize, beans, and vegetable oil. This initiative aims to support early childhood development and improve nutritional security for vulnerable populations.
contextoradditionalinfo: Eswatini is currently facing challenges related to persistent poverty, high youth unemployment, climate change, and the lingering effects of the HIV epidemic. These factors have exacerbated food insecurity, necessitating external support to protect vulnerable children and invest in human capital. The project aligns with the national Neighbourhood Care Point Strategy for 2023–2027.

policydecision_details: The Albanian Council of Ministers has adopted new secondary legislation to regulate the medical cannabis market, building upon Law No. 61/2023. The measures establish a comprehensive framework for the licensing, traceability, registration, and supervision of medical cannabis activities. A central electronic database, the National Register of Licensed and Authorised Cannabis Activities, has been created to monitor operators and compliance. The National Agency for Cannabis Control is empowered to oversee the entire supply chain, from cultivation to export or destruction. These regulations provide specific criteria for corporate, technical, and security standards that businesses must meet to operate in the sector.
contextoradditionalinfo: Following the enactment of Law No. 61/2023, which legalized the cultivation and processing of cannabis for medical and industrial purposes, the government needed to establish detailed secondary legislation to operationalize the market. The new framework aims to provide regulatory certainty for domestic and international investors while ensuring strict oversight and traceability of cannabis products.

policydecision_details: The Agricultural Bank of Senegal (LBA) has initiated a $54.2 million agricultural program supported by the Green Climate Fund. The program provides a credit line and technical assistance to help farmers access financing for climate-resilient agricultural practices. This initiative aims to strengthen the agricultural sector, which is vital to the national economy and employs a large portion of the population. The project includes both loans and grants to facilitate the transition toward sustainable and low-emission farming methods.
contextoradditionalinfo: Agriculture accounts for approximately 15.5% of Senegal's GDP and engages nearly 60% of the active population. To address the challenges of climate change and improve the resilience of the agricultural sector, the government and international partners have mobilized climate finance to support farmers through improved access to credit and technical expertise.

policy_description: Sanitary, phytosanitary and technical standards improvements
policydecision_details: The Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC) has launched new packaging and compliance strategies aimed at boosting non-oil exports in the Niger Delta region. The initiative includes capacity-building workshops to educate exporters on international packaging standards, regulations, and quality control. By improving packaging, the NEPC aims to enhance the competitiveness, shelf life, and marketability of regional products like palm oil and cassava in international markets. The program emphasizes that proper packaging is essential for protecting product integrity and building buyer confidence globally.
contextoradditionalinfo: Exporters in the Niger Delta region have faced significant challenges regarding product packaging, which has hindered their ability to compete effectively in international markets. Despite high demand for regional products, poor packaging has led to damage, contamination, and deterioration, resulting in lost market opportunities. The NEPC launched this intervention to address these technical barriers and ensure that products meet the rigorous standards required for global trade.
policycategory: Sanitary, phytosanitary and technical standards improvements

policydecision_details: The Government of The Gambia and the European Union have launched the National Early Warning and Response Policy (2026-2035) to strengthen national early warning systems. This policy provides a comprehensive framework for monitoring risks across health, security, crime, governance, and environmental sectors. It aims to shift the national approach from a culture of reaction to one of anticipation, prevention, and preparedness. The policy serves as the official reference document for all national and partner interventions regarding early warning and response mechanisms.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was developed to address increasingly complex and interconnected societal risks that threaten national peace and human security. It aligns with ECOWAS regional frameworks and international best practices to ensure coherence in crisis preparedness. The initiative was supported by the EU Support to ECOWAS in Peace, Security and Governance Project, reflecting a collaborative effort to enhance institutional capacity for crisis prevention.
decision_making_institution: National Early Warning and Response Mechanism Coordinating Centre (NCCRM)
beneficiaries: government institutions, civil society, local authorities, communities

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Centre for Economic Research and Reforms (CERR) has presented a long-term study on decarbonizing Uzbekistan’s agriculture, forestry, and land use sectors through 2070. The study proposes strategic measures to improve water resource management, reduce food losses, and increase the efficiency of agricultural land use. It outlines three scenarios for the sector, ranging from current trends to the introduction of additional measures to boost productivity and reduce emissions. These findings serve as a basis for expert discussions on the long-term prospects for the country's agrifood systems. The initiative aims to align climate objectives with food security and agricultural efficiency.
contextoradditionalinfo: Agriculture accounts for 17.5% of Uzbekistan’s total greenhouse gas emissions, with livestock farming being a primary contributor. Despite recent gains in crop yields and water-saving technology adoption between 2017 and 2025, significant challenges remain, including high water loss in irrigation canals and widespread soil salinization. The study was conducted to address these inefficiencies and provide a roadmap for sustainable development in the face of climate change.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The President of Uzbekistan reviewed the operations of a new US$8.5 million food processing plant in the Kashkadarya Free Economic Zone. The facility, Wosune Food Ingredients Karshi, specializes in the deep processing of locally grown fruits and vegetables using advanced convection drying technology. This project aims to add value to agricultural raw materials and create 150 permanent jobs. The company plans to establish direct partnerships with local farms to ensure a stable supply chain for its production of dried ingredients.
contextoradditionalinfo: The investment is part of Uzbekistan's broader strategy to enhance its agro-industrial sector, increase the value of agricultural exports, and improve the processing capacity of locally grown produce. By integrating modern technology and creating direct links with local farmers, the government seeks to boost economic productivity and industrialization in the region.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: The government of Bangladesh is restructuring the Annual Development Programme (ADP) for the 2026-27 fiscal year to tighten fiscal discipline. This decision involves scrapping nine development projects, consolidating 32 ongoing projects into 16 integrated schemes, and dropping 185 unapproved proposals. The move aims to reduce administrative overhead, prevent wasteful spending, and align national expenditure with current economic priorities. Funds from cancelled projects may be redirected toward higher-priority national development activities.
contextoradditionalinfo: The restructuring was driven by the need to contain budget deficits and address concerns regarding the financial and economic viability of various development projects. Many of the cancelled or merged projects had stalled for years with negligible physical progress, while others were deemed redundant or inefficient due to overlapping scopes in similar administrative zones.
beneficiaries: renovating level crossings, years, the army and, titas gas, accommodation and training, major ongoing national, rural development, cancellation, installing prepaid gas, corruption
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: The Chinese government has announced a new National Food Safety Standard for milk protein. This regulatory measure establishes updated safety and quality requirements for milk protein products within the domestic market. The standard aims to ensure product consistency and safety for consumers. It reflects ongoing efforts to modernize food safety regulations in the dairy sector.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of China's broader initiative to update and harmonize national food safety standards with international best practices. By defining specific requirements for milk protein, the government seeks to enhance regulatory oversight of dairy ingredients. This is intended to protect public health and improve the quality of processed food products containing milk derivatives.
decision_making_institution: National Health Commission of the People's Republic of China

policydecision_details: Sudan has officially authorized the import of various Brazilian poultry products, including day-old chicks, hatching eggs, poultry meat, processed meat products, and offal. This decision expands the range of poultry products that Brazilian exporters can supply to the Sudanese market. The move is part of a broader trend of Brazil gaining access to additional African markets for its poultry exports throughout 2026. The authorization aims to diversify the sources of poultry products available within Sudan.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decision follows Brazil's strategic efforts to open new markets in Africa, particularly as the country faces restrictions on its poultry exports to the European Union due to sanitary concerns regarding antimicrobial use. Brazil has seen a significant increase in chicken exports to Africa, exceeding 1 million tons in 2025, and is actively seeking to consolidate its position in the region as an alternative to traditional EU markets.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Foreign Ministries

policydecision_details: Launched an initiative to plant 10,000 seedlings along Al-Baha Pass in Saudi Arabia, in collaboration with the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture and the Ministry of Transport and Logistic Services. The initiative aims to expand vegetation cover, combat desertification, enhance the natural landscape and promote sustainable management of natural resources. It also encourages community participation in environmental conservation and supports the objectives of the Saudi Green Initiative.
decision_making_institution: The National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification (NCVC)

policydecision_details: Signed a memorandum of understanding with the Islamic Organization for Food Security (IOFS) to establish a framework for strategic cooperation in agriculture, livestock production and food security, aligned with the organization’s 2031 vision. The agreement covers plant and animal genetic resources, grain and livestock value chains, fisheries development, technical cooperation and the exchange of expertise. Both parties also agreed to establish a joint working group to prepare an action plan for 2026–2028, identifying priority projects, cooperation areas and technical studies to support sustainable agricultural development and strengthen Libya’s food security.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock

policydecision_details: Approved the export of a shipment of yellow corn silage to international markets following a field inspection assessing production capacity, processing operations and preparation standards. The initiative aims to support domestic production, develop the animal feed industry, expand export opportunities, generate foreign currency and diversify non-oil revenues. The ministry will continue monitoring production activities and strengthening integration between the agricultural and livestock sectors.

Reaffirmed a complete ban on leasing agricultural land for any purpose, including farming, warning that both landowners and tenants may face legal consequences for violations. The Committee for the Removal of Violations in Agricultural Areas clarified that rental agreements involving agricultural land have no legal recognition, including private contracts, and that enforcement measures may include warnings, violation notices, utility disconnections and potential withdrawal of the land by the government. The regulation aims to ensure compliance with the emirate’s agricultural land rules.
decision_making_institution: The Committee for the Removal of Violations in Agricultural Areas

policydecision_details: Launched the “Nama” Initiative to revitalise underutilised farms in Al Ain and transform them into sustainable agricultural, tourism and commercial destinations. The initiative will provide eligible farm owners with technical and field consultations, farm management training, digital empowerment, financial management support and guidance on developing agricultural, cultural and heritage tourism experiences. Through a pilot phase involving selected farms, the initiative aims to improve farm utilisation, generate sustainable income, create employment opportunities, strengthen food security and contribute to Abu Dhabi’s economic diversification and sustainable development.
decision_making_institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

policydecision_details: The Central Bank of Cuba has issued new regulations (Resolution 118/2026) governing the opening of bank accounts and the management of financing for Local Development Projects (PDP). The policy defines eligible account holders, operational procedures, and authorized funding sources for these projects. It mandates the creation of a Local Development Fund in each municipality to support economic-productive projects through trust funds and bank loans. The regulation also establishes specific interest rates for these loans and provides a framework for managing both local and foreign currency accounts.
contextoradditionalinfo: This policy was introduced to update the legal framework for territorial development in Cuba, following the approval of the 'Strategic Management of Territorial Development' decree on August 20, 2026. The Central Bank was mandated to issue these regulatory provisions to replace outdated banking procedures for managing local development project financing.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: The National Assembly of Cuba has passed Law 187, which regulates the right to adequate housing and a safe habitat. The legislation establishes comprehensive rules for property ownership, buying and selling, inheritance, and construction. It introduces specific protection mechanisms for vulnerable groups, including young people and families in overcrowded conditions. The law also integrates housing policy with territorial planning, climate resilience, and energy efficiency standards. It replaces the previous General Housing Law of 1988 to modernize the legal framework for the housing sector.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to replace the outdated 1988 General Housing Law and to provide a more robust legal framework for housing rights, property management, and social protection in the face of current socioeconomic and environmental challenges. It aims to address issues such as overcrowding and the need for sustainable urban development while formalizing property rights and transactions.
decision_making_institution: National Assembly of People's Power of Cuba
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: The Nigerian Senate has mandated comprehensive health screening for all passengers arriving at international airports, seaports, and land borders to prevent the importation of Ebola. The resolution requires the implementation of health declaration forms, temperature checks, and symptom screening for all arrivals. Additionally, the Senate has called for the release of emergency funds from Service-Wide Votes to bolster the preparedness of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) and Port Health Services. Legislative committees have been tasked with overseeing the enforcement of these measures and ensuring that entry points are adequately equipped with trained personnel and isolation facilities.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to concerns regarding the spread of the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and other African nations. The NCDC has assessed the risk of Ebola importation into Nigeria as high, prompting the Senate to address gaps in existing border surveillance, such as inadequate equipment and outdated quarantine legislation. This proactive measure aims to prevent a repeat of the 2014 Ebola outbreak in Nigeria and protect the national healthcare system from further strain.

policydecision_details: The Nigerian government has established a technical committee to accelerate livestock development and staple crop production nationwide. This committee is tasked with creating a strategic blueprint to improve agricultural sector performance and coordinate interventions across federal, state, and local government levels. The initiative specifically targets wheat production and dry-season farming to enhance national food security. The committee includes representatives from various ministries, financial institutions, and agricultural agencies to ensure a unified approach to sector challenges.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decision follows high-level meetings with President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima regarding the performance of the agricultural sector. There was a recognized need to address existing challenges and bridge the disconnect between different tiers of government to better support farmers and increase food production. The move is part of a broader national effort to achieve all-year-round farming and improve food security across Nigeria.
decision_making_institution: Office of the Vice President of Nigeria

policydecision_details: The Government of Liberia has launched the Presidential Clean Cities Initiative to address urban sanitation challenges. The program targets 1,250 youth to participate in waste management activities across 14 cities and one township. This initiative aims to mitigate issues such as indiscriminate waste dumping, blocked drains, and urban flooding. The project will be implemented in eight counties with the support of 30 community-based organizations.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative is designed to tackle environmental pollution and poor waste management in urban areas, which contribute to health risks and urban flooding. By engaging youth in these sanitation efforts, the government also aims to provide short-term employment opportunities.

policydecision_details: Signed an agreement with the Republic of Jamaica to deploy 400 Nigerian youths to work in the country for an agreed period. The deployment is scheduled to commence in the first quarter of 2027. This initiative aims to create legitimate international employment opportunities for Nigerian youth. The program is part of a broader strategy to reduce unemployment and mitigate the risks associated with irregular migration.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative is part of the Nigerian Technical Aid Corps (NTAC) program, which was established in 1987 as an instrument of Nigeria’s soft-power diplomacy. It serves as a vehicle for sharing Nigerian expertise with developing countries across Africa, the Caribbean, and the Pacific. The program is designed to foster South-South Cooperation and contribute to global development and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.

policydecision_details: Announced an increase in the national minimum wage to 970 euros for the year 2027. This decision is part of the proposed State Budget for 2027 and follows consultations with social partners. The current minimum wage stands at 920 euros. This adjustment reflects the government's ongoing commitment to wage appreciation as outlined in the tripartite agreement on wage growth and economic expansion.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a broader framework for wage appreciation and economic growth in Portugal. While trade unions have advocated for higher increases due to inflation, the government has maintained the current trajectory established in the tripartite agreement signed in 2024. The government aims to reach a gross monthly minimum wage of 1,100 euros by 2029.

policydecision_details: India and New Zealand have implemented a bilateral free trade agreement effective October 20, 2026, to boost trade and investment. The agreement provides duty-free access for Indian exporters across all tariff lines in New Zealand, including zero tariffs on engineering goods, textiles, leather, and footwear. It also streamlines Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) and Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT) procedures to reduce compliance costs for businesses. Industry leaders are encouraging MSMEs to leverage this agreement to access New Zealand and broader Oceania markets.
contextoradditionalinfo: The trade agreement aims to strengthen economic ties between India and New Zealand by removing trade barriers and facilitating easier market access for various sectors, including labor-intensive industries and processed foods.
decision_making_institution: Government of India and Government of New Zealand

policydecision_details: Uzbekistan has enacted Law No. ZRU-1183, which modifies the procedure for suspending bank account transactions for taxpayers who challenge tax authority decisions. The law mandates that tax authorities must apply to a court within three days of receiving an objection from a taxpayer to justify the suspension. Bank accounts remain frozen until a court ruling is issued, providing a judicial check on administrative actions. Additionally, the law clarifies the conditions under which suspensions must be lifted, including upon the remedy of violations or a court ruling in favor of the taxpayer.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to reduce the regulatory burden on business entities and to establish a more transparent, judicial procedure for resolving disputes between taxpayers and tax authorities regarding the freezing of bank accounts.

policydecision_details: The Legislative Chamber of Uzbekistan’s Oliy Majlis has approved a bill on a new law 'On Waste' to regulate waste collection, recycling, and disposal. The legislation clarifies the powers of state and local authorities while defining the rights and obligations of individuals and legal entities. It introduces waste classification systems and economic incentives to foster sector development. The law specifically addresses the management of hazardous, medical, biological, and construction waste, alongside setting standards for landfills and transfer stations.
contextoradditionalinfo: The current legislative framework in Uzbekistan lacks clear definitions regarding waste management foundations, property relations, and financing mechanisms. These gaps have hindered the systematic regulation of the sector, necessitating a new, comprehensive law to improve environmental and sanitation standards.
decision_making_institution: Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis
beneficiaries: industrial facilities, sanitation and cleaning service providers, general public

policydecision_details: China's top financial regulators have announced a comprehensive package of measures to stabilize the capital market and enhance financial resilience against global volatility. Key actions include improving long-term performance assessment mechanisms for institutional investors and establishing a liquidity backstop for nonbank financial institutions to prevent systemic stress. The regulators are also expanding market access for foreign institutions, including pilot programs for renminbi trading and foreign exchange settlement. Additionally, the government is encouraging share buybacks by listed companies and reforming monetary policy frameworks to prioritize stability in bond and equity markets.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to rising global volatility and the need to mitigate spillover risks across interconnected global equity, bond, and foreign exchange markets. Regulators aim to strengthen market resilience and facilitate cross-border investment to maintain capital market stability as a top national priority.
decision_making_institution: China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), People's Bank of China (PBOC), National Financial Regulatory Administration (NFRA)
beneficiaries: institutional investors, listed companies, nonbank financial institutions, foreign financial institutions

policydecision_details: The Government of Jamaica has provided free land titles to 139 additional farmers and families in St Elizabeth. This initiative is part of the ongoing Pedro Plains Irrigation Expansion Project, which aims to formalize land ownership for agricultural producers. By granting these titles, the government seeks to enhance land security and encourage greater investment in agricultural ventures. To date, a total of 282 beneficiaries have received titles under this program.
contextoradditionalinfo: Many farmers in the Pedro Plains area lacked registered land titles, which hindered their ability to secure financing and make long-term investments in their properties. The government, in collaboration with the National Land Agency, is implementing systematic land titling to remove these barriers and foster agricultural development. This effort is linked to broader infrastructure improvements, such as the commissioning of solar energy systems at local pump stations.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Mining

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Germany has announced a package of 10 measures to accelerate the national hydrogen market, supported by up to EUR 8.7 billion (USD 9.7 billion) in commitment authorizations. The government will provide EUR 1.5 billion (USD 1.7 billion) in funding through carbon contracts for difference (CCfDs) to compensate companies for the costs of transitioning to climate-friendly production. Additionally, the policy includes support for the technical retrofitting of 4 GW of power plant capacity to hydrogen and EUR 4.2 billion (USD 4.7 billion) for hydrogen transmission infrastructure. The initiative also mandates the use of low-emission steel in offshore wind projects to stimulate market demand.
contextoradditionalinfo: The development of the hydrogen market in Germany has been delayed due to high production costs that exceed the willingness to pay in many application sectors. To overcome these barriers and meet long-term climate goals, the government is intervening to bridge the cost gap and build necessary infrastructure.
decision_making_institution: Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWE)
beneficiaries: energy producers, industrial manufacturers, steel producers
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policy_description: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
policydecision_details: The Mineral Leasing Act, as amended through Public Law 119-134, establishes the regulatory framework for the leasing and extraction of mineral resources on public lands in the United States. It authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to divide lands into leasing tracts and award leases through competitive bidding processes. The act specifies eligibility requirements for citizens and corporations to hold leases for resources such as coal, oil, and gas. It also includes provisions for the reservation of helium rights by the United States government during the extraction process.
contextoradditionalinfo: This document is a compilation of the Mineral Leasing Act of 1920, reflecting amendments up to October 20, 2026. It serves as the governing statute for the disposition of mineral deposits on federal public domain lands, excluding specific protected areas like national parks and certain forest lands. The publication is intended to provide an accessible version of the current federal law for public reference.
policycategory: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources

policydecision_details: Mexico has implemented a suspension on the importation of chicken meat, live birds, and fertile eggs from Brazil. This measure applies to both commercial imports and products brought in by tourists. The decision was taken by the National Service for Agrifood Health, Safety and Quality (Senasica) to prevent the introduction of Newcastle disease into the country. The ban is a precautionary step following confirmed outbreaks of the highly contagious respiratory infection in Brazilian commercial farms.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced following reports of a Newcastle disease outbreak in Brazil, specifically in the municipality of Nova Itaberaba. Newcastle disease is a highly contagious respiratory infection in birds that can cause neurological disorders, reduced egg production, and high mortality rates. Mexico, which was Brazil's seventh-largest poultry buyer in 2025, is taking this action to protect its domestic poultry industry from the spread of the disease.
decision_making_institution: National Service for Agrifood Health, Safety and Quality (Senasica)
beneficiaries: animal health, agrifood health, children shop mnd

policydecision_details: Sgned a framework agreement to strengthen bilateral cooperation in fisheries and aquaculture training, technical expertise and scientific research. The partnership between the El Kala Technical Training School for Fisheries and Aquaculture in Algeria and the Tabarka Fisheries School in Tunisia aims to improve mahi-mahi fishing techniques using fish aggregating devices, develop joint field training and research activities, and exchange scientific data on fish biology and migration. Recommendations also include a pilot project involving national fisheries research institutions, alongside initiatives to enhance the processing, storage, marketing and export of fisheries products, particularly blue crab.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries

policydecision_details: Announced plans to expand cereal cultivation to 65,000 hectares during the 2026–2027 season, compared with approximately 60,000 hectares in the previous season, with a production target exceeding one million quintals following a harvest of more than 880,000 quintals. Support measures include providing seeds and fertilizers, mobilizing agricultural resources, improving farming practices, facilitating access to R'fig credit for input purchases, and offering training on irrigation and cultivation techniques. Authorities also aim to diversify production by promoting rapeseed and sunflower cultivation, with final cereal output depending on the results of the harvest.
decision_making_institution: The Directorate of Agricultural Services of Chlef Province

policydecision_details: Launched an initiative, in partnership with Saudi Reef Academy, to develop practical training packages for farmers, translating agricultural research and scientific expertise into improved farming practices, more efficient water and resource use, and greater adoption of modern agricultural technologies. The initiative also involves expanding regional training and extension services to improve productivity and promote sustainable agriculture. In addition, Estidamah signed cooperation agreements with SABIC Agri-Nutrients Company, NSG Geospatial Services and Saudi Arabian Mining Company (Maaden), as well as a memorandum of understanding with Qassim University, to strengthen applied agricultural research, field trials, geospatial monitoring, technology development and knowledge exchange.
decision_making_institution: The National Research and Development Center for Sustainable Agriculture (Estidamah)

policydecision_details: Belarus plans to expand its network of multibrand centers for machinery in Russia's Far East by the end of 2026. The government is currently identifying the specific region that will host the new center. This initiative aims to showcase the Belarusian industrial sector and strengthen trade ties with the Russian market. There are already 14 such centers currently in operation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The development of a network of multibrand centers for Belarusian machinery abroad is a strategic effort to promote the country's industrial sector. The Russian market is considered a priority for Belarusian goods, and the expansion is supported by joint ventures and products manufactured within the Union State of Belarus and Russia. The minister also noted that the country is navigating logistical challenges and supply route changes to meet its annual targets.

policydecision_details: The Government of Lesotho, in partnership with the UNDP and UNEP, has launched a Waste Characterisation Study and an AI-powered household waste categorisation model. This initiative aims to improve waste management by providing data-driven insights into waste composition and generation patterns. The project supports the development of a national Waste Management Information System to enhance environmental planning and decision-making. By identifying recoverable materials like organic waste and recyclables, the initiative seeks to promote a circular economy and improve waste recovery systems.
contextoradditionalinfo: Lesotho faces challenges in waste management, including limited data on waste streams and inadequate infrastructure for recycling and disposal. The initiative was introduced to address these gaps by leveraging technology and scientific research to create a more effective, evidence-based waste management framework. It also aims to support the livelihoods of waste reclaimers and reduce the environmental impact of poorly managed waste.

policydecision_details: The Economic Coordination Board (EKK) of Türkiye has announced plans to provide interim payments to investors in troubled investment funds. These payments, capped at 1 million Turkish Liras per investor, will be issued once the relevant legislation governing liquidation procedures is enacted. The measure is designed to provide relief to affected investors while ensuring fair and transparent liquidation processes. These interim payments will be deducted from the final entitlements of the beneficiaries once the liquidation is complete.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was developed in response to issues within certain investment funds, aiming to mitigate the impact on the financial system and the wider economy. The government seeks to improve the reliability and efficiency of capital markets through these legal safeguards and financial interventions. The bill was approved by the Plan and Budget Commission on October 14, 2026, as part of a broader effort to maintain financial stability.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The government of Bangladesh, through the state-owned Coal Power Generation Company Bangladesh Ltd. (CPGCBL), plans to develop a 70 MW solar power plant at the existing 1,200 MW Matarbari coal-fired power station. The project will utilize unused land in an ash pond area and is expected to be co-financed by the European Investment Bank (EIB) alongside the government. Construction is aimed at increasing the share of renewable energy in the national mix to meet long-term targets of 20% by 2030 and 30% by 2040. Electricity generation from this facility is projected to commence by December 2028.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project is part of a broader strategy to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and lower greenhouse gas emissions in response to fuel supply shortages affecting the country's electricity supply. The government is actively promoting solar deployment through various measures, including tax reductions on solar equipment and the implementation of a net-metering regime for surplus electricity.
decision_making_institution: Coal Power Generation Company Bangladesh Ltd. (CPGCBL)
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Origin Agritech Ltd. has entered into a three-year Provincial General Distribution Agreement with Jinan Jingkun Trading Co., Ltd. to serve as the exclusive distributor for corn seeds in Shandong Province. The agreement covers the 2026–2029 operating cycles and includes an initial payment of RMB 2.9 million. This partnership aims to expand Origin's commercial distribution infrastructure and improve market reach for its corn seed portfolio. The deal also establishes annual minimum sales commitments and market management protocols to ensure brand control and channel governance.
contextoradditionalinfo: Shandong Province is one of China's most significant corn-producing regions. Origin Agritech is executing a commercial strategy to rebuild its distribution network and improve accountability, following its 'Aoyun 2026' national variety promotion program. The agreement is designed to create a more auditable channel structure and facilitate the introduction of new corn varieties into the Shandong market.

policydecision_details: China has unveiled new guidelines aimed at promoting the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into the commerce sector. The policy includes 18 measures that focus on upgrading consumer goods, services, and commercial distribution through advanced technologies like smart devices, robots, and AI-powered customization. It encourages the digital transformation of wholesale and retail businesses, as well as the development of commercial AI agents for shopping and logistics. The initiative also provides support for technology standards, digital infrastructure, and financing to facilitate these innovations.
contextoradditionalinfo: The guidelines were introduced to upgrade consumption and improve commercial distribution efficiency in China. Recent data indicated that while retail sales of services grew by 5 percent in the first three quarters of 2026, retail sales of goods grew at a slower pace of 1.1 percent. This policy builds upon previous efforts, including guidelines released in June 2026, to further promote 'AI plus consumption' and stimulate economic growth in the retail and service sectors.
beneficiaries: retail businesses, wholesale businesses, service providers

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Ministry of National Food Security & Research has welcomed a cooperation agreement between Star Charge and McDonald’s Pakistan to install electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure at McDonald’s locations across the country. This initiative aims to promote environmentally sustainable transportation and reduce dependence on conventional fuels. The partnership combines Star Charge’s technical expertise with McDonald’s extensive customer network to facilitate the adoption of cleaner energy solutions. The government views this as a significant step toward building modern, green infrastructure and encouraging private-sector participation in sustainable development.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of the Government of Pakistan's broader efforts to encourage electric mobility, strengthen charging infrastructure, and promote a cleaner, greener, and more sustainable future. It addresses the need for innovative public-private partnerships to translate technological advancements into practical benefits for citizens while reducing carbon emissions and improving air quality.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of National Food Security & Research
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The European Commission has selected 77 net-zero technology projects, including a new permanent magnet production line in Estonia, to receive funding from the Innovation Fund. The project, led by Neo Performance Materials, will establish facilities for separation, metallization, and magnet manufacturing in Ida-Viru County. This production line is expected to produce up to 3,000 tons of permanent magnets annually, with one-third designated for EU offshore wind farms. The initiative aims to reduce CO2 emissions by over 3.4 million tons during its first decade of operation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project is part of a broader EU effort to transition to climate neutrality and reduce industrial reliance on raw materials from Russia. Estonia has actively sought this support to strengthen its industrial resilience, create local jobs, and establish the country as a center of expertise for critical raw materials. The funding is sourced from revenues generated by the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS).
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Mexico's Ministry of Health has designated menopause care as a public health priority within the primary care system. The initiative includes an initial investment of MX$18 million to provide hormone treatments for women lacking social security coverage. Additionally, the government is launching a training program for 1,000 health professionals and developing a national technical guideline for menopause care to be finalized in 2026. This strategy aims to integrate comprehensive climacteric care into routine health services to improve quality of life for millions of women.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy addresses the health needs of approximately 23.6 million Mexican women aged 40 and older, noting that 57% currently pay out-of-pocket for menopause-related care. Research indicates that 67% of women report negative impacts on their job performance due to symptoms, highlighting both a health and economic challenge. The initiative aligns with the broader restructuring of Mexico's public health system and the Universal Health Service (SUS) expansion, while also responding to the lack of specialized training for primary care staff.
beneficiaries: women aged 40 and older, women without social security

policydecision_details: Implemented livestock vaccination campaigns against foot-and-mouth disease (SAT-1), peste des petits ruminants, brucellosis and sheep pox. The campaigns administered a total of 4,828 vaccine doses, benefiting 127 livestock breeders. These preventive measures aim to limit the spread of animal diseases, protect livestock health, support breeders’ livelihoods, and maintain sustainable livestock production and food security. -

The Bahamas has officially signed the Multi-Country Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework 2027–2031 with the United Nations. This framework establishes a five-year strategic partnership to guide cooperation between the Government and the UN system. It focuses on four priority areas: economic diversification, resilience to shocks, integrated social services, and resilience to crime and violence. The initiative aims to translate high-level commitments into practical community-level actions to advance the 17 Sustainable Development Goals.
contextoradditionalinfo: The framework was signed during Diplomatic Week to align national priorities with UN development goals. It serves as a collaborative roadmap to address specific challenges in The Bahamas, such as social exclusion and economic vulnerability, by leveraging UN expertise and multi-stakeholder partnerships.

policydecision_details: The Whangarei District Council has announced the upcoming New Zealand Recycling Week, scheduled to take place from 19 to 25 October 2026. The initiative encourages participation from businesses, schools, and community groups through registration for official campaign resources and promotional materials. Participants are invited to engage in workplace challenges, school activities, and community events to promote recycling. This effort aims to raise awareness of the critical role recycling plays in Aotearoa.
contextoradditionalinfo: Recycling Week is a national awareness campaign in New Zealand designed to foster better waste management practices and environmental sustainability. The Whangarei District Council is promoting this event to encourage local community engagement in recycling activities.
beneficiaries: businesses, schools, community groups, recycling organisations

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Bangladesh approved the draft Special Solar Power Installation Ordinance, 2026, establishing a dedicated regulatory framework to accelerate rooftop solar deployment across public institutions and government-owned entities, with the objectives of reducing dependence on imported fossil fuels, lowering power-sector subsidies, strengthening energy security, and supporting the national target of installing 3,000-4,000 MW of rooftop solar capacity.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) of Egypt has approved six fintech companies to provide lending, investment, and other financial services. This initiative aims to expand access to financial services and accelerate digital transformation within the non-bank financial sector. The approvals specifically support technology-based lending for consumers and micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises. By integrating digital tools into capital markets, the regulator seeks to bring more individuals and businesses into the formal financial system.
contextoradditionalinfo: Non-bank finance currently accounts for approximately 54 percent of Egypt's financial system, encompassing capital markets, insurance, and real estate finance. The FRA is working to modernize this sector by licensing companies that utilize financial technology to provide credit and investment opportunities. This move is part of a broader effort to improve financial inclusion and support the growth of small and medium-sized businesses outside of traditional banking channels.

policydecision_details: Supplied modern equipment worth 150,000 shekels to the Livestock Breeding Improvement Centre of the National Agricultural Research Center in Samou, under an European Union-funded programme supporting Palestinian resilience in Area C. The equipment will strengthen research infrastructure, improve livestock genetic breeding programmes and enhance milk production and farm management, supporting livestock productivity, farmers’ livelihoods and Palestinian food security.

policy_description: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
policydecision_details: Oman and Lebanon signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen cooperation in agriculture, fisheries and food security. The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources of Oman and the Ministry of Agriculture of Lebanon will promote the exchange of expertise, technical knowledge and experience to develop productive sectors, support sustainable development and enhance food security through bilateral cooperation.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources
policycategory: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination

policydecision_details: Approved Karbala Governorate’s winter agricultural plan for the 2026–2027 season, covering 271,750 dunums. The plan allocates 233,000 dunums to wheat, 7,000 dunums to barley and 31,750 dunums to other crops, including vegetables and fodder mixtures. Of the approved area, 229,000 dunums will rely on groundwater wells, while 42,750 dunums will be irrigated from rivers and irrigation projects. The plan aims to regulate crop production according to available water resources, support farmers and strengthen domestic production of strategic crops. -

Launched the first phase of a project to cultivate native truffles in Iraq’s western desert. The initiative involves planting truffle spores at selected sites to assess the feasibility of laboratory and field propagation, with results subject to monitoring and evaluation before any expansion. The project aims to make better use of natural resources, strengthen applied agricultural research, increase local production of this economically and nutritionally valuable product, and support sustainable agricultural development.

The Government of Guyana has announced a forthcoming ban on the importation of vapes and vaping products for recreational use. An order will be signed under the Customs Act to restrict these imports, with exceptions only for products approved by the Minister of Health, the National Tobacco Control Council, or the Tobacco Control Board. This measure aims to protect public health by curbing the widespread and unregulated use of vaping products. The policy specifically targets the protection of children and young people from nicotine addiction and potential health risks.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decision was prompted by growing concerns from parents, teachers, and religious leaders regarding the prevalence of vaping among school-aged children. The government noted that vapes are not harmless and can expose users to toxic substances, with potential negative impacts on brain development, pregnancy, and respiratory health. By implementing this ban, the government seeks to exercise its duty to protect public health and ensure that products with potential risks are subject to strict oversight.

policydecision_details: The Somali federal government has introduced a bill aimed at prohibiting female genital mutilation (FGM) and address the severe health, psychological, and social consequences of the practice. The bill seeks to establish legal measures to prevent FGM and strengthen protections for the rights and dignity of Somali girls. The proposal is currently awaiting further parliamentary debate and approval procedures.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of broader national efforts to eliminate harmful traditional practices and safeguard the health and rights of children in Somalia. The Minister highlighted the need for effective legal frameworks to combat the practice, which has long-term negative impacts on the well-being of girls.

policydecision_details: Costa Rica and El Salvador have signed a bilateral security agreement to enhance cooperation in combating transnational organized crime. The agreement focuses on strengthening policing and prison security measures to dismantle criminal organizations involved in drug trafficking and other illicit activities. While the specific operational details remain to be finalized, the partnership aims to improve intelligence sharing and prison management. This initiative reflects a broader effort by the Costa Rican administration to address rising domestic violence and criminal influence.
contextoradditionalinfo: Costa Rica is facing increasing challenges from sophisticated criminal organizations, which have been linked to rising homicide rates and drug trafficking activities. The government is seeking to implement more effective tools for dismantling these groups and improving prison controls to prevent criminal leadership from operating behind bars. By deepening ties with El Salvador, Costa Rica aims to leverage regional experiences in security and prison management to bolster its own national security strategy.

policydecision_details: Togo and China signed 13 agreements focused on economic, trade, and technology cooperation to diversify export markets and expand production capacity. A key component is a protocol establishing phytosanitary requirements for Togolese soybean exports to China, aimed at removing sanitary barriers. The agreements also include cooperation on customs facilitation through the Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) program and technology training for students. These measures are designed to strengthen bilateral trade, which reached $5.43 billion in 2025, and include a memorandum on partial debt relief.
contextoradditionalinfo: Togo is seeking to diversify its export markets and increase the value of its agricultural sector, particularly for soybeans, which saw production exceed 260,000 tons in the 2024-2025 season. While China is the world's largest soybean importer, previous trade was limited by sanitary barriers. The government is balancing these export efforts with a domestic policy of encouraging local processing, supported by an export tax on soybeans introduced in early 2026.

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture has announced a series of infrastructure and production support interventions for farmers in Big Biaboo, Region Five. The government will construct an embankment and rehabilitate farm-to-market roads to improve access and flood protection. Additionally, machinery support will be provided to cash crop farmers to raise planting beds, with an estimated investment of $500,000 per farmer. A coordination committee involving farmers and regional officials has been established to oversee the implementation of these works.
contextoradditionalinfo: The intervention is a response to recurring flooding issues that have historically devastated the agricultural sector in Region Five, particularly following the severe floods of 2021. The government aims to strengthen drainage capacity and infrastructure to safeguard agricultural lands and boost production capacity for crops like corn, soya, onions, and red beans as part of a broader national food security strategy.

policydecision_details: TİKA has provided a Concentrated Feed Formulation Pilot Unit to the Bousalem Field Crops Sectoral Agricultural Vocational Training Center in Tunisia. This unit enables the integration of modern agricultural practices, such as silage production and feed formulation, into the center's vocational training programs. The initiative aims to strengthen local feed production capacity and improve the practical skills of students and local farmers. By facilitating local production, the project seeks to reduce dependence on imported feed and lower production costs for livestock breeders in the region.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Bousalem district in Tunisia is a significant agricultural area, yet it faces challenges due to inadequate modern feed-processing infrastructure. This dependence on imported feed has historically increased production costs and reduced the competitiveness of the local livestock sector. TİKA's intervention is designed to address these structural limitations by enhancing both training capacity and local production infrastructure.

policydecision_details: The Federal Government of Nigeria has approved ₦40.76 billion for the third quarter of 2026 under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF). This allocation represents a significant increase from the previous quarter to strengthen primary healthcare delivery and expand access to essential medical services. Additionally, the government has extended health insurance coverage to approximately 90,000 inmates in correctional facilities nationwide. The initiative also includes reforms to pooled procurement of medicines to improve efficiency and transparency in the health sector.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy aims to address gaps in primary healthcare delivery and improve access to medical services for vulnerable populations, including low-income households and inmates. It follows the 16th meeting of the Ministerial Oversight Committee, which sought to enhance financial management and accountability in the health sector while expanding the number of supported primary healthcare facilities.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: France and Germany have reached a bilateral agreement to support the European automotive sector by relaxing CO2 emission rules for carmakers. The deal includes a public procurement scheme for vehicles that will be restricted to EU countries, with an opt-in provision for partners like Britain and Norway. This pact aims to balance climate goals with the need to maintain industrial production and employment within Europe. The agreement will require further approval from other EU member states and the European Parliament to be fully implemented.
contextoradditionalinfo: The European automotive sector, which employs 13 million people and contributes seven percent of the bloc's GDP, has been struggling due to intense international competition and shifting market conditions. France and Germany had previously held conflicting views on how to revive the sector, with Germany favoring less stringent emissions targets and broader trade definitions, while France prioritized climate ambitions and EU-centric procurement. This deal represents a compromise intended to provide regulatory flexibility and investment incentives to ensure the industry's resilience.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Proposed a 15-month action plan to strengthen the Education Management Information System (EMIS) to enable evidence-based decision-making. The plan aims to improve data quality, reporting timeliness, and coordination across government institutions to better inform resource allocation for schools. Key measures include the introduction of data validation rules, the development of an EMIS dashboard, and the revision of reporting instruments to capture critical information on school infrastructure and learner support. This initiative seeks to transition the Ministry of Education and Training from relying on periodic reports to utilizing routine data analysis for planning teacher deployment and school supplies.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to address significant data gaps and inefficiencies in Eswatini's education sector, where decisions on resource allocation were previously based on outdated or inconsistent information. The initiative builds on existing EMIS norms and standards, incorporating lessons from the 2024 GPE-KIX synthesis report to ensure that education statistics translate into practical, effective interventions for schools and learners.

policy_description: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
policydecision_details: Togo has launched a three-year national initiative titled 'Voix du Togo' to collect voice and text data in local languages, specifically Ewe, Kabye, and Moba. The program aims to gather 50 hours of validated audio recordings, 6,000 translated sentence pairs, and contributions from at least 500 speakers per language. This data will be used to train artificial intelligence models tailored to the country's linguistic realities. The initiative is designed to facilitate access to public services, including healthcare, justice, and administrative procedures, by reducing language barriers for citizens.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative is part of Togo's national artificial intelligence strategy, which seeks to strengthen domestic capabilities to develop and utilize AI technologies. By creating AI tools that understand local languages, the government aims to improve the efficiency and accessibility of public services for the population. The project is supported by the Togo AI Lab, which focuses on applying AI to sectors such as agriculture, healthcare, education, and the environment.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Public Service Efficiency and Digital Transformation
policycategory: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination

policydecision_details: Togo and China have signed a formal protocol establishing plant quarantine and sanitary requirements for the export of Togolese soybeans to the Chinese market. The agreement mandates specific measures to control plant pests to meet Chinese import standards. This protocol aims to facilitate trade and address existing sanitary barriers that have hindered full market access. It follows previous efforts to diversify Togo's export destinations beyond the European market.
contextoradditionalinfo: Togo's soybean industry has experienced significant growth, with production rising from 25,000 tons in 2015 to over 260,000 tons in the 2024-2025 season. While Togo already benefits from Chinese tariff exemptions for least developed countries, sanitary barriers remained a challenge for exporters. The government is simultaneously encouraging domestic processing through export taxes on raw agricultural products, creating a need to balance international market access with local supply requirements.

policydecision_details: The International Financial Services Centres Authority (Good Delivery) Guidelines, 2026, establish a standardized framework for quality and responsible sourcing of gold. These guidelines apply to refiners operating in India, including those in Special Economic Zones and International Financial Services Centres, as well as global refiners seeking accreditation. The policy aims to ensure that gold refined by these entities meets 'Good Delivery' standards to enhance market transparency and credibility. By implementing these rigorous standards, the Authority seeks to position India as a significant price influencer in the global bullion market.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to regulate the bullion market ecosystem, ensuring that gold traded within the International Financial Services Centres meets international quality and ethical sourcing standards. It addresses the need for a transparent and orderly market by defining clear requirements for accredited refiners and mandating compliance with anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing measures.

policydecision_details: Japan's Statement at the 114th Meeting of the Development Committee (October 2026), the ODA priority areas and geographic focus include: Critical minerals and fertilizer supply chain resilience. Climate-resilient infrastructure and disaster risk management. Domestic resource mobilization for agrifood transformation. Pacific Islands resilience. Food, nutrition and health system linkages under the UHC agenda.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Government of Jamaica has announced a $56-million coastal protection project to fortify the Palisadoes Peninsula and Port Royal. The initiative aims to protect critical infrastructure, including the Norman Manley International Airport and the main access road, from coastal erosion and storm surges. Proposed works involve strengthening revetments, rehabilitating dunes and mangroves, and installing coastal monitoring systems. The project has been approved by the Cabinet for inclusion in the National Reconstruction and Resilience Authority's work programme.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project was initiated in response to the threats posed by extreme weather events, specifically Hurricane Melissa, which highlighted the vulnerability of the Palisadoes Peninsula. The government recognized that a closer approach by such storms could sever access to the airport and Port Royal, necessitating proactive infrastructure reinforcement to ensure long-term resilience.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Pprovided dairy-processing equipment, including churns, cheese presses and milk containers, to 72 livestock farmers participating in farmer field schools in Tuqu’, Za’atara and Al-Ubeidiya. The support is delivered through the “My Initiative” project, implemented in partnership with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and funded by the IBSA Fund. The initiative aims to strengthen livestock farmers’ production and dairy-processing capacities, improve product quality, increase the value derived from animal products and improve farmers’ livelihoods. It also supports rural community resilience, sustainable agricultural development and food security.

Mobilized resources to launch Algeria’s 2026–2027 plowing and sowing campaign across several central provinces. In Djelfa, more than 27,000 hectares are planned for cereal cultivation, including barley and durum and soft wheat, supported by seed supplies, farmer assistance and 1,587 tractors and agricultural machines. In Bouira, the campaign targets 73,000 hectares, while in Béjaïa, 4,600 hectares are planned, mainly for durum wheat. The initiative aims to support farmers, strengthen cereal production and contribute to national food security.

Eased agricultural import restrictions to help reduce food prices following the devaluation of the Iraqi dinar. The measures include exempting imported food products and medicines from customs duties, reversing restrictions imposed earlier on 15 crops, including potatoes, tomatoes and onions, to protect domestic producers. The policy shift follows increases in the official exchange rate from 1,320 to 1,520 dinars per US dollar and reported price rises of up to 15.4 percent for some staple foods. The measures aim to ease household costs, improve food affordability and address market speculation while balancing consumer needs with support for domestic agricultural production.

Launched a free nationwide spraying and dipping campaign to control ticks, which transmit Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever, with support from the Iraqi Red Crescent Society. The five-day campaign covers 12 governorates and includes spraying cattle and buffaloes and dipping sheep and goats using approved concentrations of deltamethrin. The initiative forms part of the Veterinary Department’s strategic plan to protect livestock, limit disease transmission and safeguard public health. Veterinary teams and Red Crescent personnel will coordinate field activities, identify infection hotspots and assist livestock keepers during implementation.

Launched emergency measures to contain olive tree tuberculosis following the detection of infections in olive-producing areas of Melloulech, Mahdia Governorate. Caused by the bacterium Pseudomonas savastanoi pv. savastanoi, the disease is being monitored by central and regional technical teams conducting field inspections and assessing the extent of infections. The response includes isolating affected areas, pruning severely infected trees, safely burning contaminated pruning residues and applying preventive treatments to olive trees in the targeted areas. Regional teams have also been established across olive-producing governorates to support early detection and preventive action, while farmers are encouraged to seek technical guidance from the ministry to protect healthy olive groves and limit further spread.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Maritime Fisheries

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Launched a competitive procurement process for the NOOR PV Multisites programme, which will involve developing four to six solar photovoltaic plants with a combined installed capacity of at least 350 MW across five regions. The programme includes the selection of engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractors and operation and maintenance (O&M) providers through a two-stage process. A special purpose company established by a subsidiary of the Moroccan Agency for Sustainable Energy (Masen) will oversee the contracts and sign long-term power purchase agreements with the National Office of Electricity and Drinking Water (ONEE). The initiative supports Morocco’s objective of increasing renewable energy to 52 percent of its installed electricity generation capacity by 2030.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Resumed the production of disinfected and screened seeds in Raqqa after a 14-year interruption caused by damage to its screening equipment. The facility has been supplied with new equipment and included in the 2026–2027 agricultural production plan to prepare and supply the required soft and durum wheat varieties to farmers on schedule. The restart aims to rehabilitate production capacity, improve the availability of essential agricultural inputs, support wheat cultivation and strengthen the stability of agricultural production in the governorate.
decision_making_institution: The General Organization for Seed Multiplication

policydecision_details: Adopted the Water Declaration of Grand Anse 2026 to strengthen regional water security and wastewater management. The declaration emphasizes a holistic approach to water as a pillar for public health, economic growth, and food production. It commits member states to accelerate coordinated action against climate change, drought, and infrastructure degradation. The framework aims to move from policy commitments to measurable delivery through strategic investment and regional partnerships.
contextoradditionalinfo: The declaration was adopted during the 35th Annual Caribbean Water & Wastewater Association Conference in Grenada.
