The document identifies the following strategic priorities (i) economic growth through industrialization and investment; (ii) infrastructure development (energy, transport, ICT, hospitals, education); (iii) agricultural transformation and food security; (iv) human capital development (education and skills). The Policy Statement addresses several key sectors, among others (i) Climate change: Eswatini aims to mitigate climate impacts through its National Adaptation and Resilience Strategies while pursuing economic growth. The 2020–2030 NDC Implementation Plan, covering 12 priority areas from agriculture to disaster risk reduction, is stakeholder-driven and will be continuously updated online to ensure inclusive climate action and support global efforts to limit warming; (ii) Energy: The country seeks to transition to a green economy by expanding renewable energy generation via solar, geothermal, and hydropower, supplemented by gas imports from friendly neighbors. Simultaneously, abundant mineral resources will be harnessed to provide affordable baseload energy, supporting industrial growth and energy security; (iii) Disaster risk reduction: In response to increasing natural hazards, the government will prioritize disaster risk management by strengthening institutions and securing funding. A comprehensive framework will be established, including a disaster risk finance strategy, dedicated fund, resilience strategy, and new disaster management law, making Eswatini resilient to common hazards; (iv) Agriculture: Agriculture will be leveraged to create wealth, generate youth employment, and elevate it as a high-return profession through commercialization, mechanization, and strong market systems. The sector will be climate-resilient to ensure food security and sovereignty, supported by government-led production on state farms and policies that empower farmers. The Agricultural Extension Policy will be updated, strategies for sustainable, healthy food production will be developed, and GMO regulations strengthened to maintain an organic, green economy.

policy_description: Opinions of the General Office of the CPC Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council on Strengthening Farmland Protection, Improving Farmland Quality, and Perfecting the Farmland Occupation-Supplement Balance System.
policydecision_details: The Opinions on Strengthening Cultivated Land Protection, Improving Farmland Quality, and Enhancing the Balance between Farmland Occupation and Replenishment, issued by the General Offices of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council on 5 February 2024 and published on 24 September 2024, establish a national policy framework to safeguard agricultural land, improve soil quality, and strengthen national food security. The policy sets minimum protection targets of 124.3 million hectares of cultivated land and 103.1 million hectares of permanent basic farmland. The policy focuses on farmland conservation, sustainable soil management, irrigation development, and agricultural productivity. Key priorities include preventing the conversion of agricultural land to non-agricultural uses, upgrading high-standard farmland, modernizing irrigation and drainage infrastructure, restoring degraded and saline soils, and increasing soil organic matter through improved farming practices and organic fertilizers. It also strengthens land compensation mechanisms, requiring cultivated land converted to other uses to be offset by farmland of equivalent quantity and quality. Additional measures include agricultural subsidies, crop insurance, incentives for grain producers, and stronger monitoring and enforcement mechanisms to ensure sustainable land use and food production.

policy_description: Opinions of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs on Implementing the Feed Grain-Saving Initiative in Animal Husbandry Sector.
policydecision_details: The Opinions on Implementing Grain-Saving Measures in the Livestock and Aquaculture Sectors, issued by China's Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs on 31 December 2024, establish a national policy framework to improve feed efficiency, reduce grain consumption in animal production, and strengthen national food security. The policy aims to promote resource-efficient, environmentally sustainable, and cost-effective livestock and aquaculture systems. By 2030, it targets a reduction of more than 7% in average feed consumption per unit of animal product compared with 2023 levels in standardized large-scale farming operations. The policy focuses on improving feed conversion efficiency, diversifying feed resources, optimizing livestock production structures, and promoting technological innovation. Key priorities include adopting precision feeding and low-protein feed formulations, expanding the use of alternative feed ingredients such as agricultural by-products, microbial proteins, and insect-based proteins, and developing high-quality forage production. It also promotes improved animal breeding, smart farming technologies, disease prevention, and integrated crop-livestock production systems. Implementation is supported by scientific research, technical assistance to producers, and coordination between national and provincial agricultural authorities.

policy_description: No.1 Central Document for 2024 - Opinions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council on Learning from and Applying the Experience of the “Thousand-Village Demonstration and Ten-Thousand-Village Renovation” Project to Vigorously and Effectively Promote Comprehensive Rural Revitalization.
policydecision_details: The 2024 Central No. 1 Document – Opinions of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council on Learning from the “Thousand Villages Demonstration and Ten Thousand Villages Renovation” Project to Effectively Promote Comprehensive Rural Revitalization, issued by the Government of China in 2024, establishes a national policy framework to strengthen food security, prevent rural poverty, modernize agriculture, and promote comprehensive rural revitalization. The document builds on the experience of the Green Rural Revival Programme and emphasizes agricultural modernization, rural development, and improved living standards for rural populations. The policy focuses on food security, agricultural productivity, rural poverty prevention, sustainable resource management, and rural infrastructure development. Key priorities include maintaining grain production above 650 million tonnes, strengthening agricultural subsidies and insurance schemes, protecting cultivated land, expanding irrigation infrastructure, and promoting agricultural mechanization and technological innovation. It also supports smallholder farmers, agricultural cooperatives, rural employment, agro-processing, and agricultural value chains. Environmental priorities include reducing fertilizer and pesticide use, improving water-use efficiency, restoring degraded ecosystems, and strengthening climate and disaster resilience. Additional measures promote rural healthcare, education, sanitation, digital infrastructure, and institutional reforms to support sustainable rural development.

policy_description: Climate and Environmental Action Programme in Cape Verde
policydecision_details: The Climate and Environmental Action Programme of Cabo Verde (Programa de Ação Climática e Ambiental, 2025–2027), approved by the Government of Cabo Verde through Resolution No. 119/2025 of 5 November 2025, establishes a national framework to strengthen climate resilience, promote environmental sustainability, and improve food and water security, particularly among vulnerable rural and coastal communities. The programme focuses on climate change adaptation, sustainable land and water management, biodiversity conservation, and resilient agricultural and fisheries systems. Key priorities include soil and water conservation, construction and rehabilitation of irrigation and water storage infrastructure, reforestation, sustainable forest management, restoration of protected areas, and conservation of terrestrial and marine biodiversity. It also supports sustainable fisheries, climate-resilient infrastructure for fishing communities, and environmental education. The programme aims to directly engage approximately 8,000 community members, including smallholder farmers, women, and young people. Implementation is supported by an estimated budget of CVE 750 million for 2025–2027, with strong emphasis on institutional coordination, community participation, and monitoring.

The 2024 National Hydrogen Strategy sets out Australia’s plan to become a global leader in renewable hydrogen production, use, and export as part of its legislated commitment to achieve net zero emissions by 2050. The strategy identifies hydrogen as a critical complement to electrification for decarbonising hard-to-abate sectors such as heavy transport, industrial processes, and power generation. It outlines a vision for a clean, safe, and competitive hydrogen industry that delivers economic benefits, supports regional communities, and strengthens Australia’s role in global energy markets. Key objectives include achieving cost-competitive hydrogen supply, stimulating demand in priority sectors, ensuring community benefits, and establishing large-scale trade and investment partnerships. Australia targets producing at least 15 million tonnes of renewable hydrogen annually by 2050, with a stretch potential of 30 million tonnes, and aims to export up to 1.2 million tonnes per year by 2030. Measures to achieve these goals include the Hydrogen Production Tax Incentive, the Hydrogen Headstart program, concessional finance, and investment in hydrogen hubs and infrastructure. The strategy prioritises hydrogen use in green metals, ammonia, and low-carbon fuels, while promoting research, innovation, and workforce development. It addresses regulatory reforms, safety standards, and water resource planning to ensure sustainable industry growth. International engagement through bilateral and multilateral partnerships, certification schemes, and co-investment mechanisms is central to securing Australia’s position in emerging global hydrogen markets. Regular monitoring through annual State of Hydrogen reports and five-yearly reviews will track progress against production and export milestones.

policy_description: Stratégie nationale de lutte contre la criminalité liée aux espèces sauvages (2024 – 2030)
policydecision_details: The National Strategy to Combat Wildlife Crime 2024–2030 (Stratégie Nationale de Lutte contre la Criminalité liée aux Espèces Sauvages), developed by the Government of Côte d’Ivoire in June 2024, establishes a national framework to combat wildlife trafficking, illegal poaching, and the unlawful exploitation of protected animal and plant species. The strategy aligns with the ECOWAS Wildlife Crime Strategy adopted in 2020 and aims to strengthen biodiversity conservation, environmental governance, and international. The strategy focuses on wildlife protection, combating illegal trade, strengthening law enforcement, and preventing organized environmental crime. Its six strategic objectives include preventing wildlife crime, strengthening legal frameworks and enforcement mechanisms, improving the operational capacities of law enforcement agencies, enhancing national and international cooperation, combating corruption and money laundering associated with wildlife trafficking, and mobilizing financial resources. Particular attention is given to protecting threatened species, including elephants, pangolins, primates, and endangered timber species, while strengthening border controls, intelligence sharing, investigations, and prosecution. Implementation is supported by a national coordination mechanism, specialized enforcement teams, monitoring and evaluation arrangements, and a costed action plan for 2024–2030.

policy_description: National One Health Strategy Against Antimicrobial Resistance (2024-2033)
policydecision_details: The National One Health Strategy Against Antimicrobial Resistance 2024–2033 sets out Norway’s comprehensive, cross-sectoral plan to address antimicrobial resistance (AMR) over the next decade. It frames AMR as a major health, environmental, and societal threat affecting humans, animals, plants, and ecosystems, requiring coordinated action across ministries and agencies. The strategy builds on earlier national plans and international commitments, integrating lessons from COVID-19, climate-related infectious disease trends, and global drivers of resistance. A One Health perspective underpins all initiatives, acknowledging interdependencies between public health, animal health, agriculture, and environmental stewardship. The strategy identifies six main goals: strengthening cross-sectoral collaboration, enhancing the prevention of AMR, ensuring prudent antimicrobial use, securing access to essential antimicrobial agents, increasing and applying new knowledge, and contributing to global AMR efforts. To reduce the development and spread of AMR, the strategy outlines numerous preventive and regulatory measures. These include improving infection prevention and control in healthcare; maintaining low antibiotic use through better prescribing practices, updated treatment guidelines, and public awareness campaigns; and expanding surveillance of resistant microbes in humans, animals, plants, food systems, and the environment. Norway commits to reducing healthcare-associated infections by at least 10% from 2019 levels and strengthening monitoring of antifungal and antiviral resistance. Preventive measures—such as promoting good animal husbandry, plant health, environmental monitoring, and social policies addressing living conditions and chronic disease—are emphasized as essential to reducing infection pressure and antimicrobial use. The strategy also addresses the lack of new antimicrobial classes, promoting research and development incentives, exploring Nordic and EU joint procurement mechanisms, and ensuring continued access to older narrow-spectrum antibiotics. Finally, the strategy positions Norway as an active global contributor to combating AMR. It outlines support for multilateral efforts led by WHO, FAO, WOAH, and UNEP, and Norway’s participation in European and international collaborations such as the Joint Action on AMR and Healthcare-Associated Infections, TATFAR, and CEPI. Recognising that resistance spreads across borders through travel, trade, and environmental pathways, Norway commits to strengthening global surveillance, infection prevention capacities, and equitable access to diagnostics, vaccines, and effective medicines—particularly in low- and middle-income countries. The strategy calls for expanding cross-sectoral partnerships, considering new governance mechanisms (e.g., a national AMR coordinator), and ensuring that sector-specific action plans translate this framework into measurable, implementable goals across all relevant ministries.

policy_description: National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance (NAP AMR) (2024-2029)
policydecision_details: This Maldives’ National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance (2024–2029) outlines a strengthened One Health strategy to address rising antimicrobial resistance across human health, animal health, food production, and the environment. The Plan builds on the first NAP (2017–2022), which aligned with the WHO Global Action Plan but faced challenges such as weak governance structures, limited surveillance capacity, and inadequate coordination. The 2024–2029 Plan introduces new priorities, including establishing a National AMR Coordination Unit, forming a high-level multi-sectoral steering committee, and enhancing regulatory systems to ensure proper antimicrobial oversight. The Plan identifies persistent gaps—such as poor AMR surveillance across sectors, insufficient trained personnel, and low awareness of environmental AMR risks—and proposes targeted improvements. These include digitalizing reporting systems, integrating AMR activities into existing health and agricultural programs, strengthening infection prevention and control, and improving antimicrobial stewardship. The document emphasizes sustained political commitment, cross-sector collaboration, and investment in research, innovation, and monitoring to mitigate AMR risks and protect public health in the Maldives.

The Health National Adaptation Plan II (HNAP-II) for Ethiopia (2024–2028) provides a strategic framework to address the health impacts of climate change and strengthen the resilience of the health system. Ethiopia is highly vulnerable to climate-related hazards such as droughts, floods, heatwaves, and disease outbreaks, which exacerbate public health challenges including vector-borne diseases, respiratory illnesses, diarrheal diseases, undernutrition, and mental health disorders. The plan builds on the previous HNAP (2017–2020) and aligns with national policies such as the Climate Resilient Green Economy strategy and the National Adaptation Plan. It emphasizes multi-sectoral collaboration, gender sensitivity, and equitable implementation. The overarching goal is to protect human health from climate risks by reducing morbidity and mortality, enhancing early warning systems, ensuring universal health coverage, and promoting climate-informed health workforce development. Strategic objectives include strengthening governance, integrating climate considerations into health programs, improving surveillance and research, and mainstreaming climate resilience across sectors. Key interventions focus on leadership, capacity building, climate risk monitoring, vulnerability assessments, health and climate research, management of environmental determinants, climate-resilient infrastructure, public awareness, and sustainable financing. Implementation will involve national and sub-national actors, universities, civil society, and development partners, supported by a robust monitoring and evaluation framework. The plan prioritizes evidence-based decision-making, community engagement, and resource mobilization through mechanisms such as Green Health Financing.

policy_description: Plan d’Action National de la Resistance aux Antimicrobiens (2024-2028)
policydecision_details: The National Action Plan to Combat Antimicrobial Resistance 2024–2028 (Plan d’Action National de Lutte contre la Résistance aux Antimicrobiens – PAN-RAM), developed by the Government of Cameroon in March 2024, establishes a multisectoral framework to prevent and control antimicrobial resistance (AMR) through a One Health approach, integrating human, animal, plant, and environmental health. The plan builds on the previous 2018–2020 strategy and aligns with the Global Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance. The plan focuses on responsible antimicrobial use, disease prevention, surveillance, and institutional capacity building. Its five strategic objectives include raising awareness through education and training, strengthening research and surveillance systems, reducing infections through improved sanitation and hygiene, optimizing antimicrobial use across human health, livestock, agriculture, and environmental sectors, and reinforcing governance and regulatory frameworks. Particular attention is given to antimicrobial and pesticide use in agricultural production, veterinary services, laboratory capacities, and coordination among government institutions. Implementation is supported by a costed action plan and a monitoring and evaluation framework.

policy_description: Future Drought Fund (Drought Resilience Funding Plan 2024-2028)
policydecision_details: The Future Drought Fund (Drought Resilience Funding Plan 2024–2028) Determination 2024 sets out the statutory framework for the Australian Government’s approach to enhancing drought resilience. It replaces the previous 2020–2024 plan and is made under the Future Drought Fund Act 2019. The Plan acknowledges the increasing severity and frequency of droughts, compounded by climate change and other natural disasters. It recognises the unique role of First Nations peoples in land and water management and promotes inclusive collaboration with a wide range of stakeholders, including farmers, industry groups, research institutions, and regional communities. The Plan provides a principles-based framework for funding decisions under sections 21 and 22 of the Act. It does not prescribe specific programs or delivery partners but is supported by a separate Investment Strategy that outlines priorities and implementation details for the 2024–2028 period. The Plan articulates a vision for an innovative and profitable agricultural sector, a sustainable environment, and adaptable communities that are resilient to drought and climate change. Its aim is to build resilience for the public good, ensuring that benefits are broadly accessible and not limited to private commercial interests. Three strategic objectives underpin the Plan: economic resilience through increased productivity and self-reliance; environmental resilience through improved landscape management; and social resilience through strengthened wellbeing and connectedness in rural and remote communities. These objectives are intended to be pursued holistically rather than through equal funding distribution. Funding principles are divided into two categories. Fund-wide principles guide the design of programs to ensure they are inclusive, scalable, and capable of delivering enduring outcomes. They emphasise co-investment, robust governance, and community-led approaches. Principles specific to arrangements and grants ensure alignment with the Plan’s objectives, delivery of public good, exclusion of in-drought hardship assistance, and promotion of transparency, efficiency, and knowledge sharing.

This Health National Adaptation Plan (HNAP) 2024–2027 outlines New Zealand’s strategic response to the increasing health impacts of climate change. It recognises climate change as a major threat to public health and sets a national framework to build climate-resilient health systems while ensuring equitable outcomes for all communities. The plan emphasises integration of climate adaptation into health policy, strong governance, and the development of local climate health action plans. The HNAP identifies five focus areas: leadership and governance, social and environmental determinants of health, knowledge and risk assessment, health service resilience, and community and whānau leadership. It highlights the heightened vulnerability of Māori, Pacific peoples, rural populations, disabled people, and those facing socio-economic deprivation, underscoring the need for equity-focused adaptation. The plan stresses cross-sector collaboration, prioritising housing, transport, urban development, and food systems.

The Research and Innovation Strategy 2024-2026 serves as a strategic framework to modernize the Cypriot economy and enhance its international competitiveness by fostering a robust, interconnected research and innovation ecosystem. The strategy is structured around four pillars: developing world-class research organizations and infrastructure, strengthening the link between research and business to boost entrepreneurial success, cultivating human capital as a growth driver, and positioning Cyprus as a regional leader in research and innovation. The policy identifies specific thematic priorities including digital technologies and advanced materials, with a focus on key sectors such as agri-food, shipping, renewable energy, space, health, and the environment. Implementation involves optimizing funding tools, promoting scientific excellence, and establishing a robust mechanism for measuring performance and socioeconomic impact. The strategy aims to attract global talent, research centers, and multinational investments, ensuring the country remains an attractive business destination while transitioning to a more resilient and sustainable economic model.
contextoradditionalinfo: Following Cyprus's classification as a 'Strong Innovator' in the 2023 European Innovation Scoreboard, this strategy aims to leverage recent progress to transition to the next level of development, focusing on infrastructure utilization, outward-looking approaches, and the integration of research into the productive fabric of the economy.

policydecision_details: This Strategy defines the priorities of the Republic of Cyprus for research and innovation for the period up to 2030, with the aim of strengthening competitiveness, economic diversification and the transition towards a knowledge-based economy. Building on the previous Smart Specialisation Strategy, it identifies areas where Cyprus has existing or emerging research, technological and economic capabilities. The Strategy establishes two technological priorities—Digital Technologies and Advanced Materials—and three main economic ecosystems: Agrifood, Maritime and Shipping, and Renewable Energy. Space is identified as an emerging ecosystem, while Health and Environment are considered enabling areas supporting economic and societal development. Across these priorities, particular emphasis is placed on digitalisation, sustainability, climate resilience, technological innovation and the development of higher-value economic activities.
policycategory: Enterprise development| Science| technology and innovation

policy_description: National Policy for Open Science Practices
policydecision_details: This National Policy analyses the vision, the goals and the benefits of implementing Open Science practices in the production of research work, specifies the provisions and the tools for its implementation, and revises the existing “National Open Access Policy on Scientific Information in the Republic of Cyprus” approved in 2016. Based on European Union Law establishing Horizon Europe, the Framework Programme for Research and Innovation, this Policy covers the field of access to preservation and re-use of scientific information and specifically: the open access to scientific publications; the management of research data, including open access; the use of infrastructures, tools and services for open science; and the uptake of other open science practices. The Policy applies to all research stakeholders active in the Republic of Cyprus. The Policy concerns the following matters: research funding; open access to scientific publications; metadata publication; management of research data, including open access; promotion of optimal utilisation of the national investments to fund research infrastructures; national open access repository; rights, responsibilities and duties; research assessment and evaluation; training and education; monitoring.
policycategory: Science| technology and innovation| Enterprise development

policydecision_details: The Bioeconomy 2.0 Promotion Plan is a comprehensive strategic framework designed to establish the Republic of Korea as a global leader in the bioeconomy by 2030, targeting 100 trillion won in production and 50 billion dollars in exports. The plan is structured around four primary pillars plus a foundational infrastructure component: achieving global leadership in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, revitalizing the bio-new materials industry, commercializing bioenergy, and building a digital bio innovation ecosystem. Implementation priorities include supporting 15 trillion won in private investment for biopharmaceuticals, increasing domestic bio-naphtha production to 200,000 tons, raising the Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) ratio to 8 percent, and commercializing 50 digital healthcare services. The government will support these goals through tax credits, infrastructure development such as bio-clusters and a national bio-foundry, and regulatory reform. A public-private 'Bioeconomy Alliance' has been established to oversee the execution of these missions, ensuring coordination between government ministries, industry associations, and research institutions.
contextoradditionalinfo: In response to global economic challenges such as low growth and climate change, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy developed this plan to evolve from the previous 'Bioeconomy 1.0' (focused on pharmaceuticals) to a broader 'Bioeconomy 2.0' that integrates bio-new materials, bioenergy, and digital bio-technologies.

policydecision_details: Haiti’s National Climate Change Adaptation Plan (2022) establishes a framework to strengthen climate resilience, reduce vulnerability to climate-related disasters and integrate adaptation into national and local development planning. Covering 2022–2030, the plan prioritizes four sectors: agriculture, water resources, health and infrastructure, identifying 340 adaptation actions, including 21 high-priority interventions. Key measures include climate-smart agriculture, irrigation infrastructure development, integrated water resource management, reforestation and agroforestry, watershed rehabilitation, climate-resilient infrastructure and disease prevention. The plan also aims to develop local adaptation plans for at least half of Haiti’s municipalities, strengthen institutional capacities and promote gender-responsive adaptation. Implementation is coordinated by the Ministry of Environment and the Ministry of Planning and External Cooperation, with an estimated USD 980 million required for the 21 high-priority actions, to be mobilized through national and international financing mechanisms. The plan includes monitoring and evaluation arrangements, an interim review in 2026, and updates scheduled through 2030.

policy_description: Cyprus’ Long-term low GHG emission development strategy
policydecision_details: Cyprus’s Long-Term Climate Strategy (2022) establishes a roadmap towards climate neutrality by 2050, supporting the European Union’s climate objectives through energy transition, emissions reduction and sustainable economic development. It evaluates several decarbonization scenarios, including an ambitious pathway to net-zero emissions by 2050, while the additional-measures scenario projects a 63% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2050 compared with 1990 levels. Key 2030 commitments include reducing non-ETS emissions by 24% compared with 2005, with a proposed increase to 32%, alongside the EU-wide target of reducing net emissions by at least 55% compared with 1990. Priority measures include renewable energy expansion, energy efficiency, sustainable transport, industrial decarbonization, improved agricultural practices, forest carbon sequestration and carbon capture technologies. Implementation spans 2022–2050, coordinated through the National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP), with continuous monitoring and strategy updates envisaged at least every five years.

policy_description: Plan Stratégique Gabon Emergent. Stratégie Nationale d’Industrialisation Déclinaison du Gabon Industriel
policydecision_details: The National Industrialization Strategy (Stratégie Nationale d’Industrialisation), developed by the Government of Gabon in May 2013 under the Emerging Gabon Strategic Plan (Plan Stratégique Gabon Émergent), establishes a framework for transforming Gabon from a predominantly raw-material-exporting economy into a diversified, competitive, and industrialized economy by 2025. The strategy aims to increase domestic value addition, reduce dependence on oil exports, attract investment, and generate employment through the development of strategic industrial sectors, particularly mining, timber processing, agriculture, fisheries, and agro-industry. The strategy focuses on economic diversification, agro-industrial development, sustainable natural resource management, infrastructure modernization, and industrial competitiveness. Key priorities include expanding domestic processing of agricultural and fishery products, developing competitive agricultural value chains, strengthening the timber-processing industry, increasing local mineral transformation, and promoting sustainable fisheries and aquaculture. It also emphasizes the creation of integrated industrial zones, improved transport and energy infrastructure, technical and vocational training, and stronger public-private partnerships. The strategy envisages mobilizing approximately FCFA 17 trillion in investment, creating 325,000 jobs, supporting 13,000 small and medium-sized enterprises, and increasing exports fivefold.

policy_description: Implementation Opinions of the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, National Development and Reform Commission for Promoting Synergy and Efficiency of Wastewater Treatment in Pollution and Carbon Emission Reduction (No.1714〔2023〕).
policydecision_details: The Implementation Opinions on Promoting Synergies between Pollution Reduction and Carbon Emission Reduction in Wastewater Treatment, issued by China's National Development and Reform Commission, Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, and Ministry of Ecology and Environment on 12 December 2023 (Document No. 1714/2023), establish a national framework to improve wastewater treatment efficiency while reducing greenhouse gas emissions and promoting sustainable water resource management. The policy focuses on water conservation, wastewater recycling, energy efficiency, greenhouse gas emission reductions, and resource recovery from sewage sludge. Key priorities include upgrading wastewater collection and treatment infrastructure, promoting renewable energy use in treatment facilities, reducing methane and nitrous oxide emissions, expanding reclaimed water applications, and recovering energy and nutrients from sludge. It establishes targets to achieve at least 25% reclaimed water utilization in water-scarce cities at prefecture level and above and develop 100 green, low-carbon wastewater treatment demonstration plants by 2025. Implementation is supported by technological innovation, improved regulatory standards, green financing mechanisms, and institutional coordination.

policy_description: Charte de gestion locale des espaces agro-pastoraux du département de Mangalmé
policydecision_details: The Local Charter for the Management of Agropastoral Areas in the Department of Mangalmé (Charte de Gestion Locale des Espaces Agro-Pastoraux), developed in Chad in June 2023, establishes a participatory framework for the sustainable management of natural resources, agricultural land, and pastoral areas in the Mangalmé Department of Guéra Province. The charter covers approximately 693,300 hectares and is designed for a five-year implementation period.The charter focuses on sustainable agropastoral development, equitable access to water and grazing resources, conflict prevention, and ecosystem protection. Key priorities include regulating livestock mobility and transhumance corridors, protecting agricultural fields from livestock damage, improving pasture and water management, restoring degraded ecosystems through reforestation, and strengthening animal health services. It also establishes mechanisms for resolving conflicts between farmers and pastoralists, promotes community participation in natural resource governance, and supports capacity building for rural producer organizations. Implementation is coordinated through local management, surveillance, and monitoring committees.

policy_description: Plan Nacional para el Manejo de Bosques con Ganadería Integrada (MBGI)
policydecision_details: The National Plan for Integrated Forest and Livestock Management (Plan Nacional para el Manejo de Bosques con Ganadería Integrada – MBGI), approved by the Government of Argentina through Joint Resolution No. 3/2023 of 3 July 2023, establishes a national framework to promote the sustainable management of native forests while integrating livestock production and forest conservation. The plan aims to reduce deforestation, preserve biodiversity, mitigate climate change, and promote sustainable livestock production through integrated forest and grazing management practices. Key priorities include strengthening institutional coordination, supporting small and medium-sized livestock producers, promoting sustainable forest-based value chains, improving access to financing, and developing monitoring systems. It also establishes a target of bringing at least 300,000 additional hectares under integrated forest and livestock management by 2027, alongside technical assistance, capacity building, and improved provincial regulations.

policy_description: National Plan to Combat Antimicrobial Resistance PAN (2023-2025)
policydecision_details: The National Action Plan to Combat Antimicrobial Resistance 2023–2025 (Plano Nacional de Luta Contra a Resistência aos Antimicrobianos – PAN 2023–2025), developed by the Ministry of Health and Social Affairs of São Tomé and Príncipe and validated on 28 November 2022, establishes a multisectoral framework to prevent, detect, and reduce antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Developed with technical and financial support from the World Health Organization (WHO), the plan adopts a One Health approach, recognizing the interconnections between human, animal, agricultural, and environmental health. Its main objective is to strengthen national capacities to combat antimicrobial resistance by promoting responsible antimicrobial use, improving infection prevention, and establishing coordinated surveillance and research systems. The plan aligns with the WHO Global Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance and international recommendations from FAO and the World Organisation for Animal Health. The plan focuses on four strategic objectives: awareness and education, infection prevention and control, responsible antimicrobial use, and surveillance and research. Key interventions include strengthening laboratory diagnostic capacities, establishing integrated AMR surveillance systems, improving hygiene and sanitation in healthcare facilities and communities, and reinforcing pharmaceutical regulation and inspection. Particular attention is given to veterinary antimicrobial stewardship, animal health, agricultural production, and food safety, including professional training in veterinary medicine, agriculture, food processing, and environmental management. Additional measures promote animal welfare and biosecurity practices to reduce antimicrobial use, voluntary reductions in critically important antimicrobials, improved pesticide management, and stronger regulation of antimicrobial distribution and sales. Implementation involves coordinated action among health, agriculture, livestock, and environmental authorities, supported by WHO, research institutions, professional associations, and civil society organizations.

policy_description: Management of the spread of invasive species on the slopes of amelioration ditches Program for (2023-2027)
policydecision_details: The Order Approving the Implementation Rules for the Intervention “Management of the Spread of Invasive Species on Drainage Ditch Slopes” under Lithuania’s CAP Strategic Plan 2023–2027, adopted by the Lithuanian Minister of Agriculture on 9 April 2025 (Order No. 3D-208), establishes the regulatory framework for providing agricultural support to control invasive plant species along drainage ditches and regulated watercourses. The intervention aims to halt biodiversity loss, improve ecosystem functions, and preserve agricultural habitats and landscapes, contributing to the environmental objectives of Lithuania’s Common Agricultural Policy Strategic Plan 2023–2027. The measure provides annual financial support for removing invasive vegetation through mowing, excavation, or other approved eradication methods. Eligible applicants must be active farmers managing at least 0.1 hectares of designated land, either individually or in partnership with other landholders, drainage system associations, or municipalities. Beneficiaries undertake five-year commitments, including annual treatment of the same areas, removal of invasive plants from drainage ditch slopes and adjacent three-metre maintenance strips, and compliance with species-specific eradication requirements. The use of mineral and organic fertilizers and livestock grazing on treated slopes is prohibited. Farmers must also provide photographic evidence of completed interventions and demonstrate the elimination of invasive species by the end of the commitment period. Implementation and compliance monitoring are administered by Lithuania’s National Paying Agency.

policy_description: Strategic Plan for the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) (2023-2027)
policydecision_details: The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) Strategic Plan of Greece 2023–2027, approved by the European Commission on 21 November 2022 through Decision C(2022)8270, establishes the national framework for implementing the European Union’s Common Agricultural Policy during 2023–2027. The plan aims to strengthen agricultural competitiveness, ensure viable farm incomes, improve food security, promote environmental sustainability, and support the socioeconomic development of rural areas. It is financed through the European Agricultural Guarantee Fund (EAGF) and the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD). The plan focuses on farm income support, agricultural modernization, environmental sustainability, generational renewal, and rural development. Key interventions include basic and redistributive income support, coupled payments for selected agricultural sectors, additional assistance for young farmers, and investment support to improve farm competitiveness. Environmental measures include eco-schemes promoting climate-resilient crops, soil cover, biodiversity protection, and sustainable farming practices, alongside support for organic agriculture, water and soil conservation, and animal welfare. The plan also promotes producer cooperation, agricultural knowledge and innovation systems, digitalization, risk management, and rural employment and entrepreneurship. These interventions seek to strengthen farmers' position in agrifood value chains while supporting Greece's transition towards a more competitive and environmentally sustainable agricultural sector.

The Afforestation Scheme 2023-2027 provides a comprehensive framework for the establishment of new forests in Ireland. Its primary objectives are to promote sustainable forest management, enhance carbon sequestration, and support biodiversity through various forest types, including native forests, agroforestry, and continuous cover forestry. The scheme outlines detailed eligibility criteria, grant and premium rates, and application procedures, including requirements for environmental impact assessments and appropriate assessments for sensitive sites. It establishes clear interactions with other agricultural support mechanisms, such as the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) and the Agri-Climate Rural Environment Scheme (ACRES), to ensure land use reconciliation. Implementation is managed by the Forestry Division of the Department of Agriculture, Food & the Marine, which oversees technical approvals, site notice placements, and payment schedules. The scheme is subject to periodic reviews and amendments to reflect evolving policy needs, such as the mid-term review updates regarding fencing rates and the introduction of agroforestry pilots.
contextoradditionalinfo: This document serves as the operational scheme for afforestation in Ireland for the 2023-2027 period, detailing the terms, conditions, and technical requirements for applicants seeking financial support for planting.

policydecision_details: The Forest Strategy Implementation Plan 2023-2030 provides a comprehensive framework for the development of Ireland's forestry sector. It is structured around strategic enablers and five core value areas: Forests for Climate, Forests for Wood, Forests for Nature, Forests for People, and Forests for Economy and Rural Development. The plan details specific actions for each area, including timelines, lead organizations, and key stakeholders. The Forestry Divisions of the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) are responsible for the coordination, monitoring, and reporting of these actions. The strategy aims to maximize the sector's contribution to national socio-economic well-being through sustainable forest management, increased carbon sequestration, support for the bioeconomy, and the enhancement of biodiversity and public access to forests. Implementation is supported by outcome-based indicators to track progress and ensure effective delivery across all government departments and stakeholder groups.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine is responsible for ensuring the development of forestry within Ireland in a manner and to a scale that maximises its contribution to national socio-economic well-being on a sustainable basis that is compatible with the protection of the environment.

policy_description: Mid-century, Long-term Low Greenhouse Gas Emission Development Strategy
policydecision_details: Thailand’s Long-Term Low Greenhouse Gas Emission Development Strategy (LT-LEDS), submitted to the UNFCCC in October 2021, establishes a national framework for transitioning towards a low-carbon economy, aiming to peak greenhouse gas emissions at approximately 370 MtCO₂e by 2030, reduce net emissions to around 200 MtCO₂e by 2050, achieve carbon neutrality by 2065, and reach net-zero greenhouse gas emissions as early as possible in the second half of the century. Priority measures include renewable energy expansion, energy efficiency improvements, transport electrification, industrial decarbonization, carbon capture and storage, and enhanced carbon sequestration through sustainable forestry and land-use management. Key quantitative objectives include ensuring that renewables account for at least 50% of new electricity generation capacity by 2050 and electric vehicles represent at least 69% of new vehicle sales by 2035. In agriculture and land use, the strategy promotes emissions reductions, improved resource efficiency, forest conservation and increased carbon removals. Implementation extends through 2065 and beyond, supported by national energy and climate policies, technological innovation, private investment and international cooperation. The strategy does not establish a consolidated implementation budget, instead identifying substantial financing, technology transfer and capacity-building needs to support the transition.

policy_description: Roadmap – Costa Rica towards Sustainable Food Systems opportunities and challenges from production to consumption
policydecision_details: Costa Rica’s Roadmap towards Sustainable Food Systems (2022) aims to transform agrifood systems by promoting sustainable production and consumption, food and nutrition security, environmental conservation and climate resilience. Developed through four national dialogues involving more than 500 stakeholders, it identifies nine priority areas and four cross-cutting pillars, emphasizing agricultural innovation, sustainable resource management, healthy diets, food traceability, local markets and inclusive governance. Key measures include expanding climate-smart and organic agriculture, strengthening low-emission practices in livestock, coffee, sugarcane, rice and banana production, reducing food losses and waste, and improving access to affordable and nutritious food. Implementation relies on existing institutional budgets, particularly those of the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock, alongside public–private partnerships and improved financing mechanisms. The roadmap proposes semiannual progress reviews, annual stakeholder workshops and biennial national dialogues, but does not establish a fixed implementation deadline, dedicated budget or binding quantitative outcome targets.

Austria’s Biodiversity Strategy 2030+ aims to halt biodiversity loss, restore degraded ecosystems and integrate biodiversity conservation across economic sectors. It establishes 300 measures targeting species and habitat protection, sustainable agriculture and forestry, ecosystem restoration, reduced land consumption and improved environmental governance. Key targets by 2030 include protecting 30% of national territory, improving the conservation status of 30% of endangered species and habitats, reversing pollinator decline and reducing daily land consumption to 2.5 hectares. Implementation is supported by public and private financing, EU programmes and Austria’s Biodiversity Fund, with immediate measures scheduled by 2026 and medium-term actions by 2030. A mid-term implementation report is planned for 2026, followed by a final report in 2030, contributing to the country's long-term biodiversity vision for 2050.

Malawi’s National Social Protection Policy (2024-2029) provides a comprehensive framework for coordinating and implementing social protection interventions across the country. Building on the 2012 National Social Support Policy, it aims to reduce poverty and vulnerability, protect individuals throughout their life cycle, and empower vulnerable populations to participate in productive economic activities. The policy broadens the scope of social protection to include social assistance, social insurance, social welfare services, and labour market measures. Aligned with the Malawi 2063 vision, it seeks to improve coordination, reduce fragmentation, enhance resilience, and promote inclusive and sustainable socio-economic development.
contextoradditionalinfo: Through this Policy, Malawi reaffirms its commitment to creating a more inclusive and resilient society, where every citizen has the opportunity to thrive.

policy_description: Malawi Social Cash Transfer Programme Strategic Plan 2022-2027
policydecision_details: The Malawi Social Cash Transfer Programme (SCTP) Strategic Plan 2022–2027 serves as a comprehensive roadmap for reducing ultra-poverty and building resilience among labor-constrained, vulnerable populations. Managed by the Ministry of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare, the plan aims to increase program coverage to 15 percent while enhancing the quality of life and wellbeing of beneficiaries. Key objectives include improving targeting mechanisms, strengthening domestic financing, and leveraging innovation and technology for countrywide delivery. The strategy emphasizes shock-sensitive social protection to mitigate the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic, climate-related events, and rising commodity prices. Implementation involves a multi-stakeholder approach, coordinating with entities such as UNICEF, the International Labour Organisation, the World Bank, and the European Union to ensure the sustainability and effectiveness of these safety nets. The plan also focuses on strengthening institutional arrangements, human capacity, and monitoring and evaluation systems to ensure the program remains a catalytic and transformative vehicle for poverty reduction in line with the Malawi 2063 vision.
contextoradditionalinfo: The plan was developed to address persistent poverty and vulnerability in Malawi, exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, climate shocks, and global commodity price increases, building upon the foundation of the SCTP established in 2006.

policydecision_details: The Development Document for the National Programme for Rural Areas (Ontwikkeldocument Nationaal Programma Landelijk Gebied – NPLG), published by the Government of the Netherlands on 25 November 2022, establishes a strategic and operational framework for the sustainable transformation of rural areas. Building on the NPLG's initial policy document of June 2022, it seeks to address interconnected challenges related to nitrogen pollution, biodiversity loss, water quality, climate change, and agricultural sustainability. Its overarching objective is to develop resilient and economically viable rural areas by integrating environmental protection with sustainable agricultural production and rural livelihoods. The document provides guidance for provincial authorities to prepare integrated territorial programmes, aligning national environmental commitments with regional development priorities and the long-term objective of achieving climate neutrality by 2050.The programme focuses on nitrogen emission reduction, nature restoration, sustainable agriculture, water and soil management, and climate mitigation. Key priorities include reducing nitrogen deposition in sensitive Natura 2000 areas, restoring degraded habitats and biodiversity, improving surface water and groundwater quality, and reducing greenhouse gas emissions from livestock farming, agricultural soils, and peatlands. Agricultural interventions promote the transition towards sustainable and circular farming systems, improved nutrient management, environmentally compatible land use, and agricultural practices adapted to local ecological conditions. Additional measures include expanding green-blue ecological networks, restoring wetlands, improving water retention to address drought and flooding, and integrating water and soil considerations into spatial planning. Implementation relies on provincial area-based programmes, developed in cooperation with municipalities, water authorities, farmers, businesses, and civil society, supported by national coordination, financial instruments, monitoring, and adaptive planning mechanisms.

policy_description: Towards a Strong and Sustainable EU Algae Sector
policydecision_details: This Communication highlights the potential of algae within the EU and outlines a cohesive strategy—featuring targeted measures—to scale up regenerative algae cultivation and production across the region, while fostering the development and integration of markets for both food and non-food algae-based products. The key objectives of this Communication are: (i) to unlock the potential of algae as a sustainable resource for food, feed, bio-based products, and energy, (ii) to promote regenerative algae cultivation throughout the EU to support environmental and economic goals, and (iii) to develop and mainstream the markets for food and non-food algae applications. This Communication sets out 23 actions for the purposes of improving the governance framework and legislation, improving the business environment, closing knowledge, research, technological and innovation gaps, and increasing social awareness and market acceptance of algae and algae-based products in the EU. This Communication explores the role of algae in advancing the blue carbon economy and highlights its capacity to support the EU’s goals in decarbonization, pollution reduction, circularity, biodiversity conservation and restoration, ecosystem protection, and the expansion of environmental services. It emphasizes that cultivating and processing algae and other emerging marine biomass resources can contribute to the sustainable production of food and feed, as well as pharmaceuticals, nutraceuticals, fertilizers, bio-based packaging, cosmetics, biofuels, and various other non-food products. Coherent and streamlined governance will be enabled for the algae sector throughout the EU in order to place on the market sustainably sourced and safe biomass algae-based products. New algae farmers’ toolkit will be developed for algae cultivation in the Member States, tailored to the cultivation conditions in different sea basins. The Member States will be encouraged to facilitate access to marine space, identify optimal sites for seaweed farming and include seaweed farming and sea multi-use in maritime spatial plans. The monitoring and quality framework will be strengthened by developing standard testing, quantification and extraction methods for algae ingredients and contaminants. Algae biofuel standards and a certification methodology for algae-biofuel products will be developed to be used in various transport sectors, particularly maritime transport. The market potential, efficiency and safety of algae-based materials will be assessed when used in fertilising products. The procedures as regards national licensing and governance for algae cultivation will be simplified. Market-stimulating mechanisms will be developed to support and promote the transfer of technology from research to algae market. Specific guidance will be given to promote replacing fish-based feed with algae-based feed. Valid and safe alternatives will be identified to the use of nutrients and CO2 from various sources for microalgae cultivation and organic certification. The life cycle assessment of the environmental and climate impact of algae cultivation and production will be promoted by considering the development of monitoring methodologies and indicators to measure the environmental impact and sustainability of seaweed cultivation. Targeted support will be enhanced for innovative SMEs and projects in the algae sector. The Commission will take actions for closing knowledge, research, technological and innovation gaps. Algae sector knowledge will be integrated into the EU aquaculture assistance mechanism. Studies will be conducted to deepen the knowledge of seaweed climate change mitigation opportunities and the role of seaweed as blue carbon sinks. The maximum levels for contaminants will be established and thus a new monitoring Recommendation will be adopted for algae species for which insufficient occurrence data for contaminants are available. New and improved algae processing systems and novel production methods for high-value compounds traditionally sourced from algae will be developed. Better and scalable algae cultivation systems will be developed for dealing with the current technical constraints of macroalgae and microalgae production systems. Algae biofuel-specific technological and systemic challenges will be addressed and market take-up measures will be identified in the context of Horizon Europe. The awareness of EU consumers and citizens will be raised on the benefits of algae cultivation and algae-based products, ranging from regenerating marine ecosystems to creating low-carbon products and generating blue economy jobs. The sustainability profile of algae-based products will be raised in the EU sustainable food labelling framework, including in marketing standards for fisheries and aquaculture products and green public procurement initiatives envisaged as part of the Farm to Fork Strategy. Furthermore, the Commission will promote awareness-raising actions for schools and universities on the blue bioeconomy and innovative solutions for regenerative aquaculture.

policy_description: Politique Nationale des Laboratoires du Cameroun
policydecision_details: The National Laboratory Policy of Cameroon (Politique Nationale des Laboratoires du Cameroun, 2022), developed by the Ministry of Public Health, establishes a national framework to strengthen laboratory services, improve diagnostic capacity, and enhance public health surveillance. The policy aims to establish an efficient, accessible, and reliable laboratory system that supports disease prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and progress towards universal health coverage.The policy focuses on laboratory infrastructure, quality assurance, biosafety and biosecurity, disease surveillance, and institutional capacity building. Key priorities include modernizing laboratory facilities and equipment, strengthening laboratory networks, improving professional training, establishing quality management and accreditation systems, and developing integrated laboratory information systems. It also promotes a One Health approach, encouraging multisectoral collaboration across human, animal, and environmental health, particularly for infectious disease surveillance and antimicrobial resistance monitoring. Implementation is supported by institutional coordination, financing mechanisms, and monitoring and evaluation arrangements.

The National Mining Policy 2050 (Política Nacional Minera 2050), approved by the Government of Chile through Decree No. 2 of 2 March 2022 and published on 28 January 2023, establishes a long-term framework to promote a competitive, inclusive, and environmentally sustainable mining sector. The policy aims to strengthen Chile's position as a leading producer of copper, lithium, and other strategic minerals while contributing to economic development, the energy transition, and national climate commitments. The policy focuses on sustainable mineral extraction, climate change mitigation, water resource management, biodiversity conservation, and responsible mining governance. Key priorities include reducing greenhouse gas emissions, improving water-use efficiency, promoting renewable energy and circular economy practices, managing mining waste and environmental liabilities, and protecting ecosystems affected by mining activities. It also emphasizes technological innovation, occupational health and safety, gender equality, community participation, and stronger institutional coordination to balance mining development with environmental protection and territorial sustainability.

The National Social Protection Strategy 2022–2032 of Nauru is a comprehensive framework aimed at strengthening the island nation's social protection system to reduce poverty, vulnerability, and inequality while promoting social inclusion and resilience. The strategy centers on adopting a life cycle approach, gender responsiveness, needs- and evidence-based programming, shock responsiveness, and good governance, with key goals including expanding coverage, improving program targeting and administration, promoting employment, and ensuring financial sustainability. The strategy outlines six integrated priority areas: (1) Strengthening leadership, multisectoral collaboration, and governance by designating a lead agency and coordinating efforts; (2) Enhancing targeting and administration through building human capacity, developing unique beneficiary identifiers, digital delivery systems, grievance mechanisms, and increasing awareness; (3) Establishing needs-based and evidence-based programs supported by robust monitoring, evaluation, and a management information system; (4) Expanding and improving social protection programs with a particular focus on poor working-age adults and alignment of benefits with inflation; (5) Promoting employment and labor market integration via upskilling, livelihood support, especially for women, and labor mobility; and (6) Ensuring sustainable financing through fiscal space analysis and long-term budget planning. The plan includes a 10-year detailed implementation roadmap and a monitoring and evaluation framework to assess progress and impact, guided by gender and equity principles to support Nauru's broader sustainable development goals and social welfare objectives.

The National Gender Equality Action Plan (GEAP) 2022–2026 aims to operationalize the Maldives’ Gender Equality Act and fulfill international commitments under CEDAW and the Sustainable Development Goals. Its overarching objective is to create a society that guarantees gender equality, equal opportunity, and justice for all. The plan provides a strategic framework for government institutions, private sector actors, and civil society to translate policy into actionable measures, focusing on leadership, economic empowerment, institutional mainstreaming, elimination of gender-based violence, and access to justice. The first core objective is to ensure equitable participation and representation of women and men in governance and leadership roles. This includes setting targets for women’s representation in parliament, local councils, and managerial positions, alongside measures to promote shared parental responsibilities and review electoral laws to remove barriers to women’s political participation. The second objective emphasizes economic empowerment, aiming to increase women’s participation in the labor force, reduce unemployment and informal work, and enhance access to property ownership, financial resources, and entrepreneurship opportunities, particularly for vulnerable groups such as persons with disabilities and victims of gender-based violence. The third major objective focuses on strengthening institutional mechanisms for gender mainstreaming and accountability. This involves establishing gender-responsive systems, complaint mechanisms, and gender-responsive budgeting across state institutions, as well as integrating gender equality into education curricula and civil service training. Complementing these efforts, the plan seeks to eliminate gender-based violence through legislative reforms, improved health sector responses, and expanded support services, while ensuring equal access to justice through legal empowerment, protection measures, and increased female representation in the judiciary. Collectively, these objectives aim to foster a more inclusive, secure, and equitable society in the Maldives.

policy_description: Climate Change Adaptation Program in the Water Resources Sector (2022-2026)
policydecision_details: The Climate Change Adaptation Programme in the Water Resources Sector 2022–2026, approved by the Government of Armenia through Decision No. 1692-L of 3 November 2022, establishes a national framework to strengthen the resilience of water resources and water management systems to climate change. The programme addresses increasing temperatures, declining precipitation, drought risks, and growing pressures on water availability and quality. The programme focuses on sustainable water resources management, climate resilience, and improved water security. Key priorities include strengthening climate risk assessments, improving hydrometeorological monitoring, integrating adaptation measures into water management policies and river basin plans, and protecting aquatic ecosystems. It also emphasizes efficient water use, reliable water supply, institutional coordination, capacity building, and mobilization of financial resources. Implementation is supported by an action plan for 2022–2026, with monitoring and reporting mechanisms to assess progress.

Slovenia’s Long-Term Climate Strategy, adopted on 13 July 2021, establishes a national framework to achieve climate neutrality by 2050, targeting an 80–90% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions compared with 2005 levels, with remaining emissions balanced by carbon sinks and removals. It sets strategic sectoral objectives for 2040 and 2050, promoting a transition towards a low-carbon, circular and climate-resilient economy. Priority areas include renewable and low-carbon energy, energy efficiency, sustainable mobility, industrial decarbonization, sustainable construction, waste reduction and improved resource efficiency. In agriculture and land use, the strategy emphasizes sustainable farming practices, reduced agricultural emissions, forest conservation, improved land management and enhanced carbon sequestration, while protecting biodiversity and strengthening adaptation to climate change. Implementation extends through 2050, with the National Energy and Climate Plan serving as the operational framework for measures up to 2030, supported by sectoral policies, technological innovation, public-private investment and monitoring mechanisms. The strategy does not establish a single consolidated implementation budget, instead providing long-term strategic guidance and investment scenarios rather than a fully costed action plan.

policy_description: Aotearoa New Zealand’s Long-Term Low-Emissions Development Strategy
policydecision_details: New Zealand’s Long-Term Low-Emissions Development Strategy (2021), Transitioning to a Low-Emissions and Climate-Resilient Future, establishes a national framework to achieve net-zero emissions of all greenhouse gases except biogenic methane by 2050, while reducing biogenic methane emissions by 10% by 2030 and 24–47% by 2050 compared with 2017 levels. It aims to support a productive, sustainable and inclusive economy through decarbonization, climate resilience and a just transition. Priority measures include renewable energy expansion, transport electrification, energy efficiency, sustainable agriculture, agricultural methane reduction, forestry expansion, biodiversity conservation and nature-based solutions. Implementation is structured around successive five-year emissions budgets and emissions reduction plans, beginning in 2022–2025 and continuing through 2050, supported by the New Zealand Emissions Trading Scheme, public and private investment, and independent oversight by the Climate Change Commission. The strategy emphasizes Māori participation, regional development and equitable economic transformation. It does not establish a single consolidated implementation budget, with detailed policies and financing arrangements to be developed through subsequent emissions reduction plans.

Malta’s Low Carbon Development Strategy (2021) establishes a long-term roadmap to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050, supporting the European Union’s climate objectives and strengthening national resilience to climate change. It addresses the country’s commitment, under the Effort Sharing Regulation applicable at the time, to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in non-ETS sectors by 19% by 2030 compared with 2005 levels. The strategy identifies mitigation measures across seven sectors: energy, transport, buildings, industry, waste, water, and agriculture and land use (LULUCF). Key priorities include renewable energy expansion, energy efficiency, transport electrification, sustainable mobility, improved waste management, water conservation and sustainable agricultural practices. Quantitative objectives include deploying approximately 65,000 electric vehicles and 6,500 charging points by 2030, alongside electrification of public transport. Adaptation measures address coastal vulnerability, water scarcity, infrastructure resilience, agriculture, biodiversity and public health. Implementation covers 2021–2050, with strategy updates envisaged every four years. Financing relies on national resources, EU funding instruments and private investment, with sector-specific investment estimates rather than a single allocated implementation budget.

policy_description: CANADA’S 2021 NATIONALLY DETERMINED CONTRIBUTION UNDER THE PARIS AGREEMENT
policydecision_details: Canada’s Enhanced Nationally Determined Contribution (2021) aims to accelerate the transition towards a low-carbon, climate-resilient economy while achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. It establishes a national target to reduce GHG emissions by 40–45% by 2030 compared with 2005 levels, strengthening its previous commitment of a 30% reduction. Key sectoral targets include reducing fertilizer-related emissions by 30% below 2020 levels by 2030, achieving 100% zero-emission sales of new light-duty vehicles and passenger trucks by 2035, and planting 2 billion trees over 10 years. Priority measures include clean energy deployment, industrial decarbonization, sustainable agriculture, improved nitrogen management, cover cropping, ecosystem restoration and carbon sequestration. Implementation focuses on 2021–2030, supported by federal and provincial climate policies, clean technology investments, agricultural climate programmes and the Canadian Net-Zero Emissions Accountability Act, which establishes five-year emissions reduction planning cycles towards 2050.

The Programme Implementation Manual (PIM) for Ethiopia’s Productive Safety Net Programme Phase 5 (PSNP5) serves as the authoritative guide for programme design, objectives, principles, and operational procedures. It is legally binding under the Financing Agreement between the Government of Ethiopia and the International Development Association and requires annual review and World Bank approval for any amendments. PSNP5 builds on previous phases to address persistent rural poverty and vulnerability to shocks. It shifts focus from chronic food insecurity to extreme poverty, aligning with Ethiopia’s Ten-Year Development Plan, the Social Protection Policy, Disaster Risk Management Policy, and other national strategies. The programme also supports the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those related to poverty reduction, food security, gender equality, and climate resilience. The overarching goal is to contribute to reducing extreme poverty in rural Ethiopia, while its core outcome is enhancing resilience of poor and vulnerable households to idiosyncratic and covariate shocks. This is pursued through six outputs: timely and adequate transfers; shock-responsive assistance; public works that promote livelihoods and climate adaptation; linkages to social services; tailored livelihood options; and strengthened management and capacity. PSNP5 operates under mandatory principles, including fairness in targeting, predictability of transfers, prioritization of cash over food where markets function, gender equity, nutrition sensitivity, and integration into local systems. It emphasizes scalable safety nets, productive public works, and livelihood pathways tailored to household capacity and context. Environmental and social safeguards are integral to implementation. The Environmental and Social Management Framework governs risk mitigation for public works and livelihood activities, while additional standards address labor conditions, resource efficiency, biodiversity, cultural heritage, and stakeholder engagement. Gender equity measures include childcare support, exemptions for pregnant and lactating women, and quotas for women in livelihood grants. Institutional arrangements span federal, regional, woreda, and kebele levels, with the Ministry of Agriculture as lead agency supported by other ministries and development partners. Governance relies on formal accountability mechanisms, performance-based conditionalities, and multi-tiered committees to ensure transparency and adaptive management. It integrates linkages to health, education, and nutrition services, promotes climate-smart public works, and strengthens financial inclusion and job creation, particularly for women and youth. The programme adopts a systems-based approach to ensure sustainability, resilience, and measurable contributions to Ethiopia’s poverty reduction and development objectives.

policy_description: Project Ireland 2040 National Marine Planning Framework
policydecision_details: The National Marine Planning Framework (NMPF) sets out Ireland’s first comprehensive marine spatial plan, integrating environmental, economic and social objectives to guide sustainable development across the country’s maritime area. It establishes a unified framework for managing marine activities, balancing ecological protection with economic opportunity and community engagement. The NMPF is grounded in EU directives, national legislation and international conventions. It introduces a structured planning system comprising overarching policies and sector-specific guidance, supported by environmental assessments and stakeholder consultation. It emphasizes climate action, biodiversity conservation, and alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals. Environmental policies focus on maintaining ocean health through targets for biodiversity, water quality, marine litter, underwater noise, and climate resilience. Social policies promote public access, heritage protection, and support for coastal and island communities. Economic policies encourage co-existence of marine activities and infrastructure development, particularly in aquaculture, ports, and offshore renewable energy. The framework is supported by the Maritime Area Planning Bill, which establishes a new regulatory authority and enables regional marine plans. Implementation involves monitoring, public engagement, and coordination across government departments, local authorities, and marine stakeholders.

policy_description: National Climate Change Adaptation Action Program and the List of Activities for (2021-2025)
policydecision_details: The National Adaptation Programme on Climate Change and Action Plan for 2021–2025, approved by the Government of Armenia through Decision No. 749-L of 13 May 2021, establishes a national framework to strengthen climate resilience and integrate climate change adaptation into sectoral policies, regional development strategies, and national planning processes. The programme focuses on reducing vulnerability to climate-related hazards, strengthening adaptive capacity, and promoting sustainable management of natural resources. Key priorities include addressing climate risks affecting agriculture, water resources, ecosystems, public health, and infrastructure, particularly in vulnerable rural communities. It emphasizes institutional coordination, climate risk assessments, improved data collection and monitoring, capacity building, and mobilization of financial resources for adaptation. The programme also establishes implementation and reporting mechanisms to support Armenia's commitments under the Paris Agreement.

policy_description: National Development Strategy of the Republic of Croatia until 2030
policydecision_details: The National Development Strategy of the Republic of Croatia until 2030, adopted on 5 February 2021 and published in the Official Gazette (13/2021), establishes a comprehensive framework for Croatia’s sustainable economic, social, and environmental development. The strategy aims to transform Croatia into a competitive, innovative, and resilient economy while improving living standards, reducing inequalities, and preserving natural resources. It aligns national development priorities with the European Green Deal, the EU Territorial Agenda 2030, and the Sustainable Development Goals. The strategy is structured around four development directions: sustainable economy and society, strengthening resilience to crises, green and digital transition, and balanced regional development. Key priorities include increasing productivity and innovation, strengthening healthcare and social protection, promoting renewable energy and decarbonization, developing a circular economy, and protecting biodiversity and ecosystems. In the agrifood sector, it emphasizes food production self-sufficiency, sustainable agriculture, bioeconomy development, and rural revitalization. Additional measures promote digital infrastructure, improved public administration, regional competitiveness, and targeted support for disadvantaged, mountainous, and island areas.

policy_description: Rural Development Programme under the Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance of the Republic of Albania (2021-2027)
policydecision_details: The Rural Development Programme under the Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance (IPARD III programme) addresses the identified needs and is in full compliance with the Strategy on Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries 2021-2027 (SARDF 2021-2017). The general objectives of the IPARD III programme are: (I) reinforcing a sustainable and competitive agri-food sector; (II) strengthening environmental protection and climate actions; and (III) strengthening the socio-economic fabric of rural areas. The timeframe of the programme is 7 years between 2021 and 2027.
