The identified main needs are described, as follows: (i) to increase investments in physical assets in agricultural holdings; (ii) to improve access and quality of advisory services to farmers; (iii) to improve irrigation and drainage infrastructure; (iv) to improve competitiveness of agri-processing industry; (v) to upgrade physical capital in agri-processing and food industry to comply with EU standards; (vi) to enhance cooperation among the main actors in the agri-food chain; (vii) to improve management of natural resources, resource use efficiency and climate change resilience; (viii) to diversify activities and sources of income for farmers; (ix) to develop non-agricultural sectors of rural economy; (x) to improve rural infrastructure, access and quality of basic services in rural areas; (xi) to improve local governance and develop capacity for the implementation of LEADER approach. The overall performance of agricultural holdings will be improved in the production of primary agricultural products, in order to be consistent with EU Standards as regards environmental protection and animal welfare, for the milk, meat, fruit, vegetables, olive trees, medical and aromatic plants (MAPs) and vineyards sectors. Investments will be promoted to ensure resource efficiency and support the shift towards a low carbon and climate resilient economy in agriculture, food and forestry sectors. The physical assets of selected priority food processing sectors will be modernized in order to improve competitiveness and to gradually align with Union standards in the fields of environmental protection, food safety and public health, animal welfare, renewable energy, circular economy and occupational safety. Measures will be taken to reduce the post-harvest loses and improve storage techniques and capacities in fruits and vegetables, olives, MAPs and grapes; strengthen the supply chain and integration between processors and agriculture producers; strengthen food safety, quality systems and traceability; and to improve treatment and handling of waste and use of by-products. Awareness will be raised amongst different stakeholders and groups of stakeholders from public authorities to local farmers on how the agricultural practices and sustainable use of resources can contribute to nature conservation and protection of the environment. The agri-environment management will be strengthened to conserve soil quality by introducing organic farming practices; conserve genetic resources, local breeds and support organic production of medical and aromatic plants; and to reduce biodiversity loss. The LEADER approach will be implemented to improve community development, enhance the social capital and to contribute to economic, social, cultural and environmental improvements of local areas, by engaging a wide range of multi-sectoral private and public partners and valorising community resources at the local level. The private-public partnerships will be created to improve social capital and local governance. The participation of young people and women will be encouraged. Actions will be undertaken to facilitate business and community development, growth and employment in rural areas. Rural activities will be diversified and developed, through support for investments in farm diversification and development of non-agricultural activities, such as rural tourism. Rural infrastructure will be developed to improve the living conditions of residents in rural areas. Forest conservation and management will be strengthened to improve the access to forest for performing supported activities related to afforestation, economic use of forests, and protecting forests against fire and diseases etc. To provide environmental services, forest cover or area of other wooded land, whether on agricultural, degraded or other land, will be expanded.

policy_description: National Action Plan for Gender Equality (2021-2025)
policydecision_details: The National Action Plan for Gender Equality (ESDIF) 2021–2025 sets out a comprehensive framework to promote substantive gender equality across all sectors of Greek society. Its overarching aim is to eliminate gender-based discrimination and ensure equal rights, opportunities, and participation for women and men. The plan responds to persistent inequalities in employment, decision-making, and social inclusion, while addressing the exacerbation of gender gaps during the COVID-19 pandemic. It aligns with international and European commitments, including the Istanbul Convention and the EU Gender Equality Strategy, and emphasizes coordinated action among ministries, local authorities, and civil society. The strategy is structured around four priority axes: preventing and combating gender-based and domestic violence; promoting equal participation of women in the labour market; increasing women’s representation in decision-making and leadership; and mainstreaming the gender perspective into all sectoral policies. These axes translate into specific objectives such as implementing legislative reforms, strengthening institutional mechanisms, reducing the gender pay gap, fostering female entrepreneurship, and integrating gender equality into education, health, culture, and sport. Special attention is given to vulnerable groups, including migrant women, women with disabilities, and those at risk of poverty or social exclusion. To achieve these objectives, the plan introduces targeted actions like gender-responsive budgeting, awareness campaigns, training programmes, and digital tools for monitoring progress. It also establishes mechanisms for evaluation and accountability through the Gender Equality Observatory and local equality committees. By promoting systemic change and empowering women in all spheres of life, the ESDIF aims to enhance social justice, economic growth, and democratic governance, contributing to Greece’s convergence with European standards of equality and inclusion.

policy_description: Program of Activities of the Government (2021-2025)
policydecision_details: The Government Action Programme of the Republic of Belarus until 2025, approved through Resolution No. 758 of 24 December 2020, establishes a comprehensive framework for implementing the country's socioeconomic development priorities for 2021–2025. Its overarching objective is to promote sustainable economic growth, improve living standards, strengthen economic independence, and enhance public welfare. The programme focuses on economic diversification, employment creation, social protection, healthcare, education, and infrastructure development. Key priorities include increasing household incomes, improving labour market efficiency, strengthening social assistance, modernizing public services, and promoting technological innovation. It establishes measurable targets, identifies responsible government institutions, and provides for annual monitoring and evaluation of implementation.

policy_description: Recycling and Waste Reduction (Export—Waste Plastic) Rules 2021
policydecision_details: The Recycling and Waste Reduction (Export—Waste Plastic) Rules 2021 establish a regulatory framework under the Recycling and Waste Reduction Act 2020 for the export of waste plastic from Australia. These rules define waste plastic as material discarded or surplus from various activities, including processed engineered fuel, and designate it as regulated waste material subject to export controls. Export of regulated waste plastic is prohibited unless specific conditions are met. These include holding a valid export licence, submitting export declarations, or meeting criteria listed in the Waste Plastic Exports List. Export licences require applicants to nominate specifications for the plastic and demonstrate compliance with processing standards. The Minister assesses licence applications based on factors such as intended use, specification appropriateness, contamination thresholds, and the applicant’s compliance history. Separate provisions apply to processed engineered fuel, with additional requirements concerning packaging, combustion safety, and environmental risk mitigation. Licence holders must maintain commercial relationships with suppliers and importers and notify the Minister of changes in these relationships. Licences may be suspended or revoked for non-compliance, and exemptions may be granted for trade samples intended for market testing, subject to similar scrutiny. Record-keeping obligations require licence holders to retain detailed documentation, including photographs and export declarations, for at least five years. Records must remain unaltered except for standard notations, and any changes must be documented. The rules also outline circumstances under which Commonwealth liabilities are considered paid, including through accepted payment undertakings.

policy_description: Sweden’s long-term strategy for reducing greenhouse gas emissions
policydecision_details: Sweden’s Long-Term Strategy for Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions (2020) establishes a national framework to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2045 at the latest, followed by net-negative emissions thereafter, targeting a reduction of at least 85% in territorial emissions compared with 1990 levels, with remaining emissions offset through supplementary measures such as enhanced carbon sequestration, international emissions reductions and bioenergy with carbon capture and storage (BECCS). The strategy establishes intermediate targets for sectors outside the EU Emissions Trading System of at least 63% emissions reduction by 2030 and 75% by 2040 compared with 1990 levels, alongside a 70% reduction in domestic transport emissions by 2030 compared with 2010 levels. Priority measures include renewable energy expansion, industrial decarbonization, transport electrification, energy efficiency, carbon taxation, emissions trading and circular economy practices. In agriculture and land use, the strategy emphasizes sustainable agricultural practices, biogas production from manure, forest conservation, sustainable forestry and enhanced carbon sinks. Implementation extends through 2045 and beyond, supported by Sweden’s Climate Act, national climate action plans, annual climate reporting and independent monitoring by the Climate Policy Council. The strategy does not establish a consolidated implementation budget, relying instead on existing and evolving national and EU policy instruments, public investment programmes and private-sector financing.

policy_description: Low-Carbon Development Strategy of the Slovak Republic
policydecision_details: The Republic of Korea’s 2050 Carbon Neutral Strategy (2020) establishes a long-term national framework to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050, promoting a transition towards a low-carbon, climate-resilient economy through technological innovation, sustainable development and green investment. It identifies five strategic directions: expanding clean electricity and hydrogen, improving energy efficiency, accelerating technological innovation, promoting a circular economy, and strengthening natural carbon sinks. Priority measures include renewable energy deployment, transport electrification, industrial decarbonization, carbon capture technologies, sustainable agriculture and livestock management, forest conservation and enhanced carbon sequestration. Implementation extends through 2050, supported by the national emissions trading scheme, green finance, research and development, and cooperation between government, industry and civil society. The strategy does not establish a consolidated implementation budget, with financing and detailed implementation measures to be developed through subsequent national and sectoral policies.

France’s Second National Low-Carbon Strategy (2020) establishes a national roadmap to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050 and reduce greenhouse gas emissions by at least 40% by 2030 compared with 1990 levels. It aims to reduce gross emissions approximately sixfold by 2050 while strengthening natural carbon sinks and reducing the national carbon footprint. The strategy establishes three successive carbon budgets, limiting average annual emissions to 422 MtCO₂e for 2019–2023, 359 MtCO₂e for 2024–2028 and 300 MtCO₂e for 2029–2033. Priority measures include decarbonizing transport and energy production, improving building efficiency, transforming industrial processes, promoting agroecological practices, reducing agricultural emissions, strengthening forest carbon sequestration and advancing circular economy approaches. Adopted by decree on 21 April 2020, the strategy guides national and territorial public policies through 2050, with monitoring indicators, periodic evaluations and mandatory five-year revisions. It does not establish a single consolidated implementation budget.

policy_description: Finland’s long-term low greenhouse gas emission development strategy
policydecision_details: Finland’s Long-Term Low Greenhouse Gas Emission Development Strategy (2020) outlines pathways to achieve carbon neutrality by 2035 and carbon negativity thereafter, supporting the transition towards a low-carbon economy by 2050. The strategy assesses three scenarios: With Existing Measures, Continuous Growth and Savings. The two low-emission scenarios project greenhouse gas emission reductions of 87.5% and 90%, respectively, by 2050 compared with 1990 levels, excluding the land-use sector, while both achieve carbon neutrality by 2035. Priority areas include renewable energy expansion, energy efficiency, industrial decarbonization, sustainable transport, agricultural emissions reduction, sustainable forestry and strengthening carbon sinks. Implementation is envisaged through national energy and climate strategies, sectoral roadmaps and land-use policies, with specific measures to be determined through subsequent planning processes. The strategy covers the period 2020–2050 and provides scenario-based assessments of investment needs and socioeconomic impacts rather than a consolidated implementation budget.

Spain’s Long-Term Decarbonisation Strategy (ELP 2050), approved on 3 November 2020, establishes a national roadmap to achieve climate neutrality by 2050, targeting a 90% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions compared with 1990 levels, with the remaining 10% offset by natural carbon sinks, expected to absorb approximately 37 MtCO₂e annually by 2050. The strategy aims to transform Spain into a competitive, climate-resilient and low-carbon economy, with intermediate milestones for 2030 and 2040. Priority measures include expanding renewable energy, achieving an almost entirely renewable energy system, improving energy efficiency, electrifying transport, decarbonizing industry and buildings, and promoting circular economy practices. In agriculture and land use, the strategy emphasizes reducing livestock and fertilizer-related emissions, improving agricultural practices, sustainable forest management, ecosystem restoration and strengthening natural carbon sinks, while addressing climate risks such as drought, desertification and biodiversity loss. Implementation covers 2021–2050, supported by the National Integrated Energy and Climate Plan (PNIEC), the Just Transition Strategy, sectoral policies, technological innovation and public-private investment. The strategy does not establish a consolidated implementation budget, instead providing long-term investment scenarios and strategic guidance for financing the transition.

policy_description: 2050 Carbon Neutral Strategy Of The Republic Of Korea
policydecision_details: The Republic of Korea’s 2050 Carbon Neutral Strategy (2020) establishes a long-term national framework to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050, promoting sustainable economic growth, technological innovation and a transition towards a low-carbon society. It builds on the country’s 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), which, at the time of submission, targeted a 24.4% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030 compared with 2017 levels. Priority measures include expanding renewable energy, phasing down fossil fuel dependence, improving energy efficiency, promoting hydrogen technologies, electrifying transport, decarbonizing energy-intensive industries and developing carbon capture, utilization and storage technologies. The strategy also emphasizes climate-smart agriculture, sustainable livestock management, forest conservation, afforestation and enhanced carbon sequestration, alongside circular economy practices and waste reduction. Implementation extends through 2050, supported by green finance, carbon pricing, the national emissions trading scheme, research and development, and institutional coordination across government and industry. The strategy promotes a just transition and greater public participation while identifying technological innovation and private investment as essential enablers. It does not establish a consolidated implementation budget, with detailed investment requirements and financing mechanisms to be developed through subsequent policies and sectoral plans.

Belgium’s Long-Term Climate Strategy 2050 aims to support the transition towards climate neutrality through coordinated federal and regional policies, focusing on renewable energy, energy efficiency, sustainable transport, industrial decarbonization and low-emission agriculture. Key targets include Wallonia’s 95% greenhouse gas emission reduction by 2050 compared with 1990 and Flanders’ 85% reduction in non-ETS emissions compared with 2005, while Brussels aims to approach EU climate neutrality. Regional projections indicate a 85–87% reduction in non-ETS emissions by 2050, including a 45–51% reduction in agricultural emissions compared with 2005. Priority measures include sustainable land management, circular economy practices, electrification, renewable energy deployment and low-carbon technologies. Implementation follows regional pathways towards 2050, supported by Belgium’s National Energy and Climate Plan and cooperation between federal and regional authorities.

Austria’s Long-Term Strategy 2050 aims to achieve climate neutrality by 2050 through substantial greenhouse gas emission reductions, renewable energy expansion, energy efficiency improvements and the strengthening of carbon sinks. It promotes the decarbonization of transport, industry, buildings and agriculture, alongside sustainable land management, technological innovation and circular economy practices. Key targets for 2030 include reducing non-ETS greenhouse gas emissions by 36% compared with 2005, increasing renewable energy to 46–50% of gross final energy consumption, covering 100% of domestic electricity consumption with renewables on a national net basis, and improving primary energy intensity by 25–30% compared with 2015. The strategy also emphasizes sustainable forestry, agricultural emissions reduction, climate adaptation and a socially just transition. Its implementation follows a long-term pathway through 2050, supported by national energy and climate planning, sectoral policies, investment and stakeholder coordination.

policy_description: Actualización de la Contribución Determinada a Nivel Nacional de Colombia (NDC)
policydecision_details: Colombia’s Updated Nationally Determined Contribution, approved in December 2020, aims to strengthen climate mitigation and adaptation while promoting low-carbon development, ecosystem conservation, sustainable agriculture and climate resilience. It establishes a national target to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 51% by 2030 compared with the business-as-usual scenario, limiting emissions to 169.44 MtCO₂e, alongside a 40% reduction in black carbon emissions compared with 2014. Key targets include reducing annual deforestation to 50,000 hectares by 2030, with a complementary ambition of achieving net-zero natural forest deforestation, and integrating climate risk management, adaptation and mitigation into 50% of social protection programmes by 2030. Priority measures include renewable energy expansion, sustainable livestock production, forest restoration, climate-smart agriculture and improved water management. Implementation covers 2020–2030, coordinated through national, sectoral and territorial climate plans, supported by carbon budgeting, monitoring mechanisms, climate finance and international cooperation.

The Politique Nationale de Protection Sociale (PNPS) 2020-2030 establishes a comprehensive strategic framework to mitigate social vulnerabilities in Cameroon through four primary pillars: strengthening non-contributory social transfers, expanding contributory social insurance schemes, providing targeted social services for vulnerable groups, and promoting the economic inclusion of marginalized populations. The policy aims to improve the national social protection system by reinforcing legislative frameworks, enhancing technical capacities, and developing robust analytical databases to support implementation. It emphasizes a multi-sectoral coordination approach, involving central and decentralized levels, to ensure the effective delivery of social services. The framework also outlines measures for resource mobilization and monitoring and evaluation to ensure the sustainability and impact of social protection interventions over the decade.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was developed to address the socio-demographic and socio-economic challenges identified in the national diagnostic, aiming to transition from fragmented interventions to a more structured and effective national social protection system.

policydecision_details: The National Development Strategy 2020-2030 is a comprehensive framework designed to achieve structural transformation and inclusive development in Cameroon. Its primary objectives include accelerating industrialization through the development of energy, digital technology, and manufacturing sectors, while simultaneously boosting agricultural productivity and competitiveness. The strategy emphasizes the development of productive infrastructure, including energy, transport, telecommunications, and water/sanitation, to support economic growth. It also prioritizes private sector revitalization, regional integration, and trade facilitation. Environmental sustainability and climate change adaptation are integrated into the strategy, alongside a focus on transforming the financial system to increase financial inclusion and local investment. Implementation is coordinated by the Ministry of Economy, Planning and Regional Development, with contributions from various ministries and development partners, utilizing a results-based management approach to ensure progress toward the 2030 goals.
contextoradditionalinfo: The NDS30 was formulated to address national development challenges and build upon the foundations of previous growth and employment strategies, with the participation of development partners including the UNDP.

policy_description: National School Nutrition Programme (NSNP) Food Specifications
policydecision_details: The National School Nutrition Programme (NSNP) Food Specifications is a sub-sectoral document intended for all the stakeholders, such as manufacturers, service providers, Provincial Education Departments, Districts, Circuits, schools, and the public. It accompaignes and completes the National School Nutrition Programme (NSNP) which is a sectoral document aiming to enhance the learning capacity and give access to education for learners from poor households based on the following: it (i) helps learners arrive at school alert, punctual, and ready to learn, improving concentration and attendance; (ii) encourages healthy eating habits through nutrition education; (iii) promotes food security through school vegetable gardens managed with parents, learners, and communities. Given that, the rationale behind the Food Specifications is to (i) maintain food standards to ensure food safety and quality; (ii) improve the quality of nutrition in meals served to learners; (iii) minimize hygiene-related risks to learners; (iv) make information on quality control measures available to role players e.g. manufacturers and service providers on the requirements of the NSNP standards. To be approved for use, food items must meet strict general requirements for safety, quality, and labeling. This includes a valid Certificate of Acceptability for handling food, a certified Quality Management System (like HACCP), and compliance with all national and local regulations. The manufacturer is responsible for all necessary examinations, tests, and quality control. All packaging and labeling must be clear, legible, and compliant with regulations, including providing a product name, manufacturer's information, net weight, dates, and a list of ingredients. All containers must be durable and protect the food from contamination. The delivery process must follow a strict schedule and quantity limits, with schools not obligated to accept excess stock. All products must undergo regular microbiological, sensory, and shelf-life testing to ensure they are free from pathogens, maintain their quality, and meet specific shelf-life requirements. The document also recommends using locally produced and fresh foods to support the South African economy and provide optimal nutrition. Lastly, it clarifies that the National School Nutrition Programme (NSNP) does not provide specialized diets for specific health conditions, as its mandate is to ensure access to basic, quality nutrition for all learners. For each food item, the National School Nutrition Programme (NSNP) Food Specifications document indicates the required compliance rules, quality standards, nutritional requirements, and properties for human consumption, as well as packaging, labeling, and storage requirements.

The National Sanitation and Hygiene Policy provides a holistic and clear policy direction for the sanitation and hygiene sector in Bhutan. The mission of the Policy is to attain sustainable sanitation infrastructure and services with safe hygienic practices. The five policy objectives laid down are: 1. Achieve universal coverage and access to sustainable services for all; 2. Adopt appropriate technology for sustainable sanitation systems; 3. Develop sustainable and efficient financing mechanism for safe sanitation and hygiene services; 4. Strengthen capabilities including behaviour change communication at all levels; and 5. Institutionalize mechanism for effective and efficient coordination and service delivery. Policy statements are provided under each of the policy objectives. The policies and legal framework relevant for sanitation and hygiene are also described. The strategy for monitoring and evaluation of Policy implementation is provided, which includes the responsibilities of the concerned agencies.

The goal of this strategy is to create conditions whereby the urban population in Bangladesh has the opportunity to reach and maintain the highest attainable level of health. The objectives laid down include improved access to quality and equitable healthcare; strengthening governance and stewardship of public, local government and private sectors; institutional development for improved performance; equitable access to health, population and nutrition care of urban population; strengthening the capacities of city corporations and municipalities; building a robust evidence base for decision making; and promoting healthy lifestyle choices, healthy environment and early healthcare seeking. The strategies for urban health are provided along with the roles and responsibilities of various stakeholders.

policy_description: Plan de Acción Nacional para la Contención de Resistencia Antimicrobiana (2020-2024)
policydecision_details: The National Action Plan for the Containment of Antimicrobial Resistance 2020–2024 (Plan de Acción Nacional para la Contención de Resistencia Antimicrobiana – PANCRAM), developed by the Government of Nicaragua, establishes a multisectoral framework to prevent and control antimicrobial resistance (AMR) through a One Health approach. Aligned with the WHO Global Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance and international guidance from FAO and the World Organisation for Animal Health (OIE), the plan aims to reduce the emergence and spread of resistant microorganisms while preserving the effectiveness of antimicrobial medicines. It addresses risks to human, animal, plant and environmental health, recognizing antimicrobial resistance as a major threat to public health, food safety, agricultural production and sustainable development. The plan covers 2020–2024 and is aligned with Nicaragua's National Human Development Programme 2018–2021. The plan is structured around five strategic priorities: awareness and education, surveillance and research, infection prevention and control, responsible antimicrobial use, and sustainable financing. Key interventions include strengthening national antimicrobial resistance surveillance systems, improving laboratory and research capacities, implementing infection prevention and hygiene measures, and promoting the prudent use of antimicrobials in healthcare, livestock production, plant health and food systems. Particular attention is given to veterinary antimicrobial use, food safety, and monitoring resistant microorganisms in animals and animal-derived products, reflecting Nicaragua's important livestock production and export sector. Additional measures promote professional training, public awareness campaigns, stronger regulatory frameworks and interinstitutional coordination. Implementation involves the Ministry of Health (MINSA), the Institute for Agricultural Protection and Health (IPSA), the Ministry of Agriculture (MAG), environmental authorities, universities and other public institutions, supported by monitoring and evaluation mechanisms.

policy_description: Plan d’Aménagement et de Gestion du Parc National du Banc d’Arguin (PNBA) pour (2020-2024)
policydecision_details: The Management and Development Plan 2020–2024 for Banc d’Arguin National Park (Plan d’Aménagement et de Gestion du Parc National du Banc d’Arguin), issued by the Government of Mauritania in March 2020, establishes a five-year framework for conserving and sustainably managing one of West Africa’s most important marine and coastal protected areas. Established in 1976 and designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989, Banc d’Arguin National Park covers approximately 12,000 km² and supports internationally significant marine biodiversity, migratory birds, and traditional fishing communities. The plan seeks to preserve the park’s ecological integrity and cultural heritage while strengthening sustainable livelihoods, institutional governance, and resilience to environmental and socioeconomic pressures. The plan is structured around four main components: sustainable development, conservation of natural and cultural heritage, ecosystem knowledge, and governance and resilience. Key interventions include strengthening surveillance against illegal fishing, maintaining restrictions on motorized fishing within the park, protecting sensitive marine species and habitats, and supporting participatory fisheries management with local Imraguen communities. Additional priorities include preserving traditional sailing vessels and fishing practices, improving scientific monitoring of marine ecosystems, managing risks associated with coastal development and offshore activities, addressing waste and pollution, and strengthening climate adaptation and institutional capacities. Implementation emphasizes cooperation among park authorities, fishing communities, research institutions, the Mauritanian Coast Guard, and international conservation partners, alongside sustainable financing and monitoring mechanisms.

The Maldives Health National Adaptation Plan (HNAP) outlines how the country’s health sector will respond to climate change threats, such as the rise of communicable and non-communicable diseases, water- and heat‑related illnesses, and mental health stresses, by strengthening health infrastructure, waste management, and emergency preparedness. It emphasizes cross-sectoral collaboration, research, advocacy, and sustainable financing, aligning with international guidance documents. The plan also sets out a robust monitoring and evaluation framework, building on vulnerabilities identified in water resources, air quality, food security, and the built environment, in order to protect public health amid the Maldives’ acute exposure to climate risks.

The Recycling and Waste Reduction (Fees) Rules 2020 set out the fee structure and related provisions under the Recycling and Waste Reduction Act 2020. These rules govern the financial aspects of product stewardship, particularly in relation to the accreditation of voluntary arrangements. Fees are prescribed for the consideration of applications for accreditation and for variations to existing accreditations. A fixed fee applies to new applications, while a time-based fee is charged for variations. Applications must be accompanied by the relevant fee unless waived. Penalties apply for late payment, calculated as a proportion of the overdue amount based on the number of days delayed. The Minister has discretion to remit or refund fees and penalties, either on their own initiative or upon written request. Decisions to refuse such requests are subject to review, with affected persons identified in the rules.

The National Digital Strategy (2020-2025) provides a comprehensive roadmap for the digital transformation of Cyprus. Its primary objectives include the modernization of public administration through e-government services, the expansion of high-speed broadband infrastructure, and the enhancement of digital skills across the population to ensure inclusive growth. The strategy focuses on creating a robust digital ecosystem that supports innovation, improves the efficiency of public services, and strengthens the competitiveness of the Cypriot economy. Implementation is led by the Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy, which coordinates efforts across various government departments to integrate digital solutions into daily operations. The strategy targets a wide range of beneficiaries, including citizens, private enterprises, and the public workforce, with the expected outcome of establishing a fully digitized, efficient, and resilient society capable of meeting the challenges of the modern digital era.
contextoradditionalinfo: The strategy was developed to address the need for a cohesive digital transformation framework in Cyprus, aiming to bridge the digital divide and align the country with European digital standards and the Digital Single Market.

policy_description: National Plan for Adaptation to Climate Variability and Change for the Agricultural Sector of Uruguay
policydecision_details: Uruguay’s National Adaptation Plan to Climate Variability and Change for Agriculture (PNA-Agro), published in September 2019, establishes a comprehensive framework to strengthen the climate resilience of agricultural production systems, reduce vulnerability to climate variability and extreme weather events, and promote sustainable rural development. The plan combines a long-term strategy to 2050 with an Action Plan to 2025, structured around four strategic dimensions: production systems, ecosystems and natural resources, rural livelihoods, and institutional capacities. It identifies 66 priority adaptation measures, including climate-resilient agricultural practices, sustainable livestock and crop production, improved water and soil management, agricultural research and technology transfer, climate information systems, agricultural insurance, resilient infrastructure and strengthened farmers’ organizations. The plan also promotes biodiversity conservation, ecosystem services and improved institutional coordination. Implementation is led by the Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries (MGAP), in coordination with the National Climate Change Response System (SNRCC), with technical support from FAO and UNDP. The Action Plan identifies responsible institutions, beneficiaries, objectives, financing requirements and implementation barriers for individual measures, supported by monitoring and evaluation mechanisms. It does not establish a single consolidated implementation budget, instead identifying financing needs and opportunities for domestic and international support.

Costa Rica’s National Decarbonization Plan 2018–2050 aims to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, transforming the economy through green growth, sustainable development and climate resilience. It establishes 10 strategic transformation axes and 8 cross-cutting strategies, covering sustainable transport, renewable electricity, energy-efficient buildings, low-carbon industry, waste management, sustainable agriculture and livestock production, and forest conservation. Key targets include achieving 100% renewable electricity by 2030, electrifying 25% of the light-duty vehicle fleet by 2035, and transitioning 100% of buses and taxis to zero-emission technologies by 2050. Agricultural priorities include improving production efficiency, reducing livestock emissions, promoting low-carbon agrifood systems and strengthening carbon sequestration through sustainable land management. Implementation spans 2018–2050, structured into three phases: initial actions (2018–2022), transformation and consolidation (2023–2030), and large-scale deployment (2031–2050), supported by institutional reforms, green fiscal policies, investment and monitoring mechanisms.

Portugal’s Roadmap for Carbon Neutrality 2050 (RNC2050), approved in June 2019, establishes a long-term strategy to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, through an 85–90% reduction in emissions compared with 2005 levels, complemented by carbon sequestration from forests and land use. It defines intermediate emission reduction trajectories of 45–55% by 2030 and 65–75% by 2040, alongside an estimated carbon sink capacity of 9–13 MtCO₂ annually by 2050. Priority measures include expanding renewable energy, fully decarbonizing electricity generation by 2050, improving energy efficiency, electrifying transport and industry, promoting circular economy practices, and reducing emissions from agriculture, livestock and waste management. The strategy emphasizes sustainable agricultural production, precision farming, improved manure and fertilizer management, afforestation, forest restoration and biodiversity conservation, while strengthening resilience to droughts, wildfires and desertification. Implementation extends through 2050, supported by the National Energy and Climate Plan, sectoral policies, sustainable finance mechanisms and public-private investment. The roadmap estimates approximately EUR 85 billion in additional investment requirements for carbon neutrality over 2016–2050, equivalent to EUR 2.1–2.5 billion annually, primarily within the energy system. This represents modelled investment needs rather than an approved government implementation budget.

policy_description: Strategy of Latvia for the Achievement of Climate Neutrality by 2050
policydecision_details: Latvia’s Long-Term Climate Strategy, adopted in January 2020, establishes a national roadmap to achieve climate neutrality by 2050, combining greenhouse gas emission reductions with increased carbon removals through land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF). It sets intermediate targets to reduce GHG emissions by 65% by 2030 and 85% by 2040 compared with 1990 levels, excluding LULUCF, alongside net emission reductions of 38% by 2030 and 76% by 2040, including LULUCF. Priority measures include renewable energy expansion, energy efficiency, sustainable transport, low-carbon technologies, sustainable agriculture and forestry, circular economy practices and climate-neutral urban development. Implementation covers 2020–2050, with specific measures defined through successive National Energy and Climate Plans and sectoral policies. Indicative additional investment requirements are estimated at approximately EUR 16 billion (2020–2050), with additional net costs of EUR 13.5 billion, both expressed in constant 2010 prices. The strategy provides for progress monitoring and reviews by 2029 and every ten years thereafter.

The National Action Plan to Counteract Antibiotic Resistance 2000–2004 (Tiltak for å motvirke antibiotikaresistens 2000–2004), issued by the Norwegian Ministry of Health and Social Affairs in 2000, establishes a coordinated national framework to prevent and control antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The plan recognizes that excessive and inappropriate antibiotic use in human and veterinary medicine, together with the spread of resistant microorganisms through healthcare, food production and international travel, threatens the effectiveness of antimicrobial treatments. Its overarching objective is to preserve antibiotics as effective medicines by reducing unnecessary consumption, preventing the spread of resistant microorganisms, and improving knowledge of antimicrobial resistance in humans, animals, food products and the environment. The plan adopts a multisectoral approach involving health, agriculture, fisheries and environmental authorities. The plan identifies eight priority areas, including antimicrobial resistance surveillance, monitoring antibiotic consumption, responsible prescribing practices, public awareness, infection prevention, microbiological diagnostics, regulatory improvements and research. Key interventions include strengthening national surveillance systems, notably the Norwegian Monitoring Programme for Antimicrobial Resistance (NORM), improving monitoring of resistant microorganisms in humans, animals and food products, and promoting appropriate antibiotic use among physicians, veterinarians and dentists. Particular attention is given to veterinary antibiotic stewardship, food safety, animal health and infection control in agricultural and aquaculture production systems. Additional measures include improving hygiene standards, strengthening regulations governing antibiotic approval and marketing, expanding professional training and public education, and supporting research into resistance mechanisms and alternative treatments. Implementation relies on interministerial cooperation, public health institutions, veterinary authorities, healthcare providers and research organizations.

This Cottage and Small Industry (CSI) Policy is a nation wide setoral policy document. The CSI Policy sets out the overall policy framework for CSI development until 2030. The overall objective of the policy is to promote establishment of new CSIs and improve the performance and competitiveness of existing CSIs to enhance their participation and contribution to the Bhutanese economy. As the mission of the Policy states, the CSI Policy seeks to enhance CSIs contribution to employment generation and alleviation of poverty, especially in rural areas. Development of a culture of entrepreneurship at all levels of the education system and all spheres of economic activity will reinforce the importance of entrepreneurship and its contribution to socio-economic development of the nation. There is also a need to develop and enhance a deep and diverse talent pool of CSIs that matches labour market demand, with an emphasis on gender equality. The Royal Government of Bhutan shall: 1.Ensure collaborative and synchronized efforts amongst agencies in providing skills development training with a focus to encourage women and youth entrepreneurship; 2. Promote women entrepreneurship in CSIs to maximize the economic contribution of both genders through provision of preferential business development services; 3. Promote entrepreneurship amongst vulnerable groups in CSIs to improve their livelihoods through provision of preferential business development services. The CSI Policy seeks to enable more inclusive and efficient agricultural and food systems. The objectives of CSI Policy 2019 comprise of six strategic domains of entrepreneurship ecosystems namely: i) Policy and Legislative Framework; ii) Entrepreneurship Culture and Human Capital Development; iii) Business Development Support and Infrastructure; iv) Enhancing Access to Finance and Incentives; v) Innovation and Technology Adoption; vi) Access to Market. The measures proposed in the Policy include: 1. Adopt an integrated business licensing system - end to end automation for CSIs to ease doing business; 2. Adopt registration system for cottage scale industries with validity of 3 years for those activities not requiring any sector clearance and those not in the restricted category; 3. Stimulate the development of business cluster and/or value chains to increase competitiveness of CSI products and services. 4. Facilitate establishment of market infrastructure such as warehouses, cold storage facilities, naturally ventilated store, pack house, etc. for CSI products; 5. Facilitate establishment of market linkages to link producers to market; etc.

policy_description: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (2019-2025)
policydecision_details: The National Strategy and Biodiversity Action Plan 2019-2025 aims to ensure the conservation and sustainable use of Biodiversity components, taking into account the fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from the use of biological resources as well as conservation actions, preservation, protection and restoration of Biodiversity in Angola. The Strategy's Vision is that by 2025, Angolan Biodiversity should be valued, converted, restored and wisely used, maintaining Ecosystem Services, maintaining a healthy and unpolluted environment, and sharing essential benefits for all people. Its General Objective is: Take effective measures to halt biodiversity loss to ensure that by 2025 ecosystems are resilient and continue to provide essential services, thereby contributing to the eradication of extreme poverty and the well-being of our population. The Specific Strategic Goals (SG) for Action to achieve the General Objective until 2025 are: SG1: Reduce pressure on Biodiversity and promote its sustainable use; SG2: Strengthen the network of conservation areas including representations of the different Biomes and Ecosystems in Angola; SG3: Promote scientific research and the dissemination of information on Biodiversity; SG4: Reinforce education and awareness for sustainability; SG5: Reinforce the Implementation of International Biodiversity Agreements; SG6: Reinforce the role of local communities in the management of Biodiversity; SG7: Mobilize Funds for the conservation of Biodiversity; SG8: Restore Biodiversity in cities, towns, villages and neighborhoods in the country; SG9: Strengthen Institutions related to the Environment; SG10: To reinforce the elaboration of specific Legislation and its implementation in harmony with the International and SADC Region Agreements; SG11: Manage, coordinate and monitor Actions for the Conservation of Biodiversity (NBSAP); SG12: Restore degraded Forests and Ecosystem Services: The Strategic Goals lead to the setting of the National Biodiversity Goals that the Country should achieve by 2025, taking into account the international and regional synergies for reaching the Biodiversity Goals, Aíchi 2020 and the Millennium Sustainable Development Goals.

policy_description: Afghanistan Independent Human Rights Commission Strategic Plan (2019-2023).
policydecision_details: The 2019–2023 Strategic Plan defines baselines, targets, and methodologies for implementation, risk management, and evaluation, supported by a detailed budget and SWOT analysis to strengthen institutional effectiveness and ensure sustainability in advancing human rights across Afghanistan. The Afghanistan Independent Human Rights Commission (AIHRC) envisions a just, democratic, and developed Afghanistan where human rights are respected and protected. Its mission focuses on monitoring, promoting, and safeguarding human rights through empowerment, accountability, investigation of abuses, and collaboration with civil society and government institutions. Guided by principles of dignity, justice, equality, freedom, transparency, and gender inclusivity, the Commission works to ensure fairness, participation, and legal protection for all Afghans, especially vulnerable groups. The AIHRC is committed to environmental sustainability by minimizing its ecological footprint and adhering to international standards such as those set by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) and the Paris Agreement. It prioritizes biodiversity preservation, clean air, protection of aquatic ecosystems, prevention of land degradation, and responsible waste management across all its operations. Through eco-friendly practices, sustainable construction, and community advocacy, the Commission ensures its activities support both human rights and environmental protection in Afghanistan.

policy_description: State Program for Veterinary State Control by National Food Agency of Georgia
policydecision_details: of the country's annual framework for veterinary, food safety and phytosanitary controls. Its principal objective is to protect animal health and public health through veterinary surveillance, disease prevention and official controls, while supporting the safety and sustainability of livestock production. The programme focuses on animal disease surveillance, vaccination, veterinary inspections, livestock traceability, and veterinary medicine quality control. Key measures include monitoring and controlling foot-and-mouth disease, anthrax, rabies, lumpy skin disease and other infectious animal diseases; inspecting livestock holdings, live-animal markets and veterinary pharmaceutical establishments; and supervising ante-mortem and post-mortem inspections. It also promotes animal identification and registration, laboratory testing for veterinary drug residues, and the prevention of zoonotic diseases. For 2018, planned activities included foot-and-mouth disease vaccination covering approximately 1.2 million cattle and 1.38 million sheep and goats, rabies vaccination of 260,000 dogs and cats, and inspections of approximately 267 veterinary establishments.

policy_description: State Program for Phytosanitary Control by National Food Agency of Georgia
policydecision_details: The 2018 State Phytosanitary Control Programme of Georgia, approved by the Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture through Order No. 2-22 of 15 January 2018, establishes an annual framework for protecting plant health, preventing the introduction and spread of quarantine pests, and regulating pesticides and agrochemicals. Implemented by the National Food Agency, the programme aims to safeguard agricultural production, improve food safety, protect human health and the environment, and strengthen the export competitiveness of Georgian agricultural products. It constitutes Annex No. 3 of the broader 2018 State Control Programme for Food Safety, Veterinary and Phytosanitary Measures. The programme focuses on plant health surveillance, pest prevention, pesticide quality control, and phytosanitary compliance. Key measures include monitoring quarantine and particularly dangerous pests, conducting laboratory analyses of plant diseases, inspecting pesticide and agrochemical production, storage, labelling and marketing, and supervising the treatment and certification of wood packaging materials. For 2018, it envisages installing 400 pheromone traps, conducting approximately 732 laboratory examinations for plant pests and diseases, and inspecting 150 pesticide and agrochemical retail establishments. It also provides for testing approximately 300 pesticide samples and 48 agrochemical samples to identify counterfeit, unregistered, expired, or otherwise unsuitable products. These interventions aim to reduce crop losses, improve agricultural productivity, and facilitate compliance with international phytosanitary requirements.

policy_description: State Program for Food Safety Control by National Food Agency of Georgia
policydecision_details: The 2018 State Control Programme for Food Safety, Veterinary and Phytosanitary Measures, approved by Georgia’s Ministry of Environmental Protection and Agriculture through Order No. 2-22 of 15 January 2018, establishes an annual regulatory framework for official inspections and monitoring of food safety, animal health, and plant protection. Implemented by the National Food Agency, the programme aims to protect public health and consumer interests, ensure compliance with food safety legislation, strengthen domestic market functioning, and improve the export potential of Georgian agricultural and food products. The programme focuses on food safety inspections, veterinary surveillance, phytosanitary controls, risk-based monitoring, and compliance enforcement. Key measures include scheduled and unannounced inspections of food businesses, laboratory testing for microbiological and chemical contaminants, verification of food labelling and traceability, and monitoring of production, processing, and distribution activities. Particular attention is given to slaughterhouses, dairy processors, agricultural markets, school and kindergarten catering facilities, and exporters of agricultural products. The programme establishes differentiated inspection frequencies, including four annual inspections for slaughterhouses and two for raw-milk heat-treatment facilities, and plans approximately 4,436 food samples for laboratory analysis. Veterinary and phytosanitary components complement these measures through controls aimed at protecting animal and plant health.

policy_description: Plan d'action national pour les élephants (PANE)
policydecision_details: The National Elephant Action Plan 2019–2028 (Plan d’Action National pour l’Éléphant – PANE), developed by the Republic of Congo's Ministry of Forest Economy, establishes a ten-year national framework to protect forest elephants, combat poaching and illegal ivory trafficking, and ensure the long-term conservation of elephant populations and their natural habitats. The plan responds to the significant decline in Central African forest elephant populations and aligns with international conservation commitments, including CITES and the African Elephant Action Plan. FAOLEX The plan focuses on wildlife conservation, anti-poaching enforcement, habitat protection, and sustainable forest management. Its eight strategic objectives include reducing illegal elephant killing and trafficking by 80%, maintaining habitat connectivity across major forest landscapes, mitigating human–elephant conflicts, strengthening public awareness and institutional capacities, promoting cross-border conservation cooperation, and increasing the participation of local and Indigenous communities in wildlife management. Implementation is supported by priority actions, institutional coordination, monitoring mechanisms, and financial resource mobilization.

policy_description: Programme to Support Production, Export Diversification and Import Substitution (PRODESI)
policydecision_details: The Programme to Support Production, Export Diversification and Import Substitution (PRODESI), approved by the Government of Angola through Presidential Decree No. 169/18 of 20 July 2018, establishes a national framework to accelerate economic diversification, reduce dependence on oil revenues, strengthen domestic production, and promote non-oil exports. The programme places particular emphasis on agricultural production, agro-industrial development, and food import substitution, prioritizing strategic value chains such as cereals, soybeans, dairy products, meat, and eggs. It aims to improve domestic competitiveness by facilitating access to finance, attracting private investment, strengthening productive infrastructure, and promoting industrial clusters and public-private partnerships. PRODESI also supports improvements in the business environment, institutional coordination, and monitoring mechanisms to stimulate employment, expand export opportunities, and strengthen national production capacity.

policy_description: National Strategy to accelerate Stunting Prevention (2018-2024)
policydecision_details: The National Strategy to Accelerate Stunting Prevention 2018–2024 (Strategi Nasional Percepatan Pencegahan Stunting), issued by the Government of Indonesia in November 2018, establishes a comprehensive multisectoral framework to reduce childhood stunting and improve maternal and child nutrition. The strategy addresses chronic malnutrition, which affected 30.8% of Indonesian children under five in 2018, and prioritizes interventions during the first 1,000 days of life, from pregnancy to a child's second birthday. Its main objective is to accelerate reductions in stunting prevalence by improving access to essential nutrition, health, food security, water, sanitation, and social protection services, particularly among vulnerable households and communities. The strategy is structured around five pillars: leadership commitment, national awareness campaigns and behavioural change, convergence of national and local programmes, food and nutrition security, and monitoring and evaluation. It combines nutrition-specific interventions, including maternal nutritional support, breastfeeding promotion, complementary feeding, micronutrient supplementation and child healthcare, with nutrition-sensitive interventions addressing household food security, access to nutritious diets, safe drinking water, sanitation, social protection and early childhood development. Particular emphasis is placed on coordinating programmes across ministries, provincial and district governments, and villages to improve service delivery in priority areas. Implementation involves integrated planning and budgeting, community participation, strengthened institutional accountability, and monitoring systems to assess progress in reducing stunting and improving nutritional outcomes.

The Strategic Plan for the Ministry of Agriculture of the Kingdom of Eswatini (2018–2023) aims to address persistent challenges of poverty, unemployment, and food insecurity through agricultural transformation. The plan is aligned with national frameworks such as the National Development Strategy and international commitments including the Malabo Declaration and Sustainable Development Goals. Its vision is to optimize agricultural resources to create wealth, while its mission focuses on modernizing agriculture into a sustainable, diversified, and export-oriented sector. The plan sets three overarching goals: increasing agriculture’s contribution to economic development, reducing rural poverty, and improving food and nutrition security. Specific objectives include enhancing domestic production and productivity of crops and livestock, improving value chains and market access, promoting food safety standards, rationalizing land and water use, and fostering fisheries development. Implementation strategies emphasize knowledge management, infrastructure investment, public-private partnerships, and adoption of modern technologies to build resilience against climate variability. Institutional arrangements involve multiple departments and parastatals under the Ministry, supported by a legislative and policy framework comprising operational laws and pending bills. Sector policies are harmonized with regional and global frameworks such as CAADP and SADC-RAP. The plan identifies structural challenges including fragmented land tenure, low productivity, inadequate research and extension services, and vulnerability to climate change. Strategic interventions target key subsectors: livestock (cattle, goats, pigs, poultry, dairy, fisheries, apiculture), crops and horticulture (sugarcane, maize, legumes, vegetables, fruits, cotton), and land and water resource development. Measures include improving breeding programs, feed production, disease control, irrigation infrastructure, and commercialization models. Food and nutrition security strategies focus on diet diversification, hygiene, and income generation for vulnerable households. Implementation relies on stakeholder engagement, resource mobilization through government and development partners, and capacity building.

policy_description: National Invasive Species and Biosecurity Strategic Action Plan (2018-2022)
policydecision_details: The National Invasive Species and Biosecurity Strategic Action Plan (NISSAP) is a national policy with a timeframe of years covering the period from 2018 to 2022. The goals of the NISSAP are: (I) to increase community awareness and participation and build resilience of communities and ecosystems by increasing capacity and improving the legal and policy frameworks for ongoing management of invasive species at national, state, and community levels; (II) to prevent the introduction and spread of invasive species; (III) to reduce negative impacts of existing invasive species; (IV) to strengthen the effective collaboration, coordination and participation for invasive species prevention and management among community, state, national, regional, and international partners; and (V) to sustain a comprehensive and systematic effort to effectively address invasive species in the long term. Community awareness on the prevention and management of invasive species will be increased. Invasive species information and materials will be integrated into school curricula. Awareness campaigns with a focus on invasive species will be carried out and monitored regularly. The support will be increased for research and training and educational opportunities for local programs related to invasive species, such as Integrated Pest Management (IPM) Program. To improve the fight against invasive species, the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats in communities and all sectors will be identified. Community and sectoral participation in the prevention and management of invasive species will be promoted. A functional framework for invasive species management will be developed and implemented by 2022. Biosecurity measures will be strengthened at all levels in order to prevent the introduction and spread of new species with the potential to become invasive. Early detection and rapid response mechanisms will be developed against new introductions of potentially invasive species. Measures will be taken to prevent or reduce the spread of invasive species within Palau, especially from one island to another. Urgent actions will be undertaken to control and/or eradicate invasive species which are known to be causing serious damage to biodiversity and/or society. Existing invasive species will be assessed, inventoried and prioritized for appropriate management action, including control and/or removal. The Palau National Invasive Species Committee will work closely with communities and partners to support the development of economic and ecosystem restoration plans. Biosecurity legislation and regulations will be developed in compliance with national legislation and regulations. The institutional capacity of the Palau National Invasive Species Committee will be enhanced to ensure its continuity, effectiveness and functionality. A National Invasive Species Office will be established with a mandate and sufficient capacity necessary to lead the implementation of the NISSAP. Adequate and sustainable funding will be allocated for the effective implementation of each of the activities of this plan. Long term efforts to address invasive species will be effectively integrated into existing state and national government procedures, work plans and activities.

The National Development Plan 2018–2022 (Plano de Desenvolvimento Nacional), approved by the Government of Angola through Presidential Decree No. 158/18 of 29 June 2018, establishes a comprehensive framework for promoting sustainable economic growth, social development, and territorial cohesion. Building on the previous National Development Plan 2013–2017, it prioritizes economic diversification, macroeconomic stability, poverty reduction, employment creation, and improved access to essential public services. The plan places particular emphasis on agricultural development, food security, and rural transformation, promoting increased domestic agricultural production, improved productivity, irrigation development, rural infrastructure, and stronger agricultural value chains. It also supports import substitution, agro-industrial development, and greater participation of smallholder farmers in agricultural markets. Additional priorities include education, healthcare, social protection, water and sanitation, environmental sustainability, and institutional capacity building. Implementation is supported by sectoral programmes, public investment priorities, and monitoring and evaluation mechanisms

policy_description: Food Safety and Food Authenticity Strategy 2018-2020
policydecision_details: The Food Safety and Food Authenticity Strategy 2018-2020 establishes a strategic vision for the Department of Agriculture, Food and the Marine (DAFM) to ensure the continued safety and authenticity of food products. The strategy is built upon five core goals: strengthening governance through open and robust official controls; improving communication to foster collaboration between the Department, stakeholders, and the public; enhancing risk management systems using the latest scientific evidence; maximizing the utility of food-based data to support evidence-based policy; and developing a cohesive regulatory framework to safeguard consumers and promote industry compliance. The strategy aims to cultivate a culture of compliance within the agri-food sector, enabling the Department to act as an enabler of best practices while fulfilling its regulatory responsibilities. Implementation involves multi-disciplinary teams working with regulatory partners to deliver improved assurances to consumers both domestically and internationally, ultimately supporting the high-level objectives of the Food Wise 2025 blueprint.
contextoradditionalinfo: The strategy was developed to address the challenges and opportunities facing the Irish agri-food sector, ensuring that the industry's growth is underpinned by high standards of food safety, provenance, and integrity.

country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
policydecision_details: The United Kingdom’s Clean Growth Strategy, published in October 2017 and amended in March 2018, establishes a national framework to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while promoting economic growth, technological innovation and sustainable development. Building on the Climate Change Act 2008, the strategy supports the then-existing target of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by at least 80% by 2050 compared with 1990 levels, alongside legally binding five-year carbon budgets requiring average emissions reductions of 51% during 2023–2027 and 57% during 2028–2032, relative to 1990. Priority measures include renewable energy expansion, energy efficiency in buildings and industry, low-carbon transport, clean electricity generation, waste reduction and green innovation. In agriculture and land use, the strategy promotes environmentally sustainable farming, low-emission fertilizers, agricultural innovation, woodland expansion and improved carbon sequestration, including a commitment to plant 11 million trees in England and support the longer-term ambition of increasing woodland cover to 12% by 2060. Implementation focuses on measures through 2032, within the broader 2050 decarbonization framework, coordinated by the Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy and other government departments. The strategy identifies over GBP 2.5 billion in government investment in low-carbon innovation between 2015 and 2021, alongside sector-specific funding programmes, but does not establish a single consolidated implementation budget.

Haiti’s Intended Nationally Determined Contribution (2015) establishes a national framework to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 31% by 2030 compared with a business-as-usual scenario, while strengthening climate resilience and addressing the country’s high vulnerability to natural disasters. The mitigation target comprises an unconditional reduction of 5% and an additional conditional reduction of 26%, dependent on international financial and technical support. Priority measures include expanding renewable energy to 47% of the electricity mix by 2030, improving energy efficiency, promoting sustainable agriculture and agroforestry, strengthening forest conservation and reforestation, and improving waste management. Adaptation priorities address food security, integrated water resource management, coastal protection, climate-resilient infrastructure and disaster risk reduction. Implementation covers 2016–2030, with estimated financing requirements of USD 25.387 billion, including USD 8.773 billion for mitigation and USD 16.614 billion for adaptation. The contribution emphasizes international cooperation, institutional coordination and capacity building to support implementation.

policy_description: Concept for the improvement and development of housing and communal services (2017-2025)
policydecision_details: The Concept for the Improvement and Development of Housing and Communal Services until 2025, approved by the Government of Belarus through Resolution No. 1037 of 29 December 2017, establishes a national framework to modernize public utilities, improve service quality, and enhance the efficiency and sustainability of housing and communal infrastructure. The concept focuses on improving drinking water supply, wastewater treatment, energy efficiency, and municipal waste management. Key priorities include modernizing water supply and sanitation networks, reducing water and energy losses, upgrading heating systems, promoting waste separation and recycling, and improving housing maintenance. It establishes a target of providing 100% of consumers with quality drinking water by 2025. The concept also promotes affordable utility services, social protection for low-income households, institutional reforms, and increased investment through innovative financing mechanisms, including public-private partnerships.

policy_description: National Strategy of the Republic of Azerbaijan on the conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity (2017-2020)
policydecision_details: The National Strategy for the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Biodiversity 2017–2020, approved by the Government of Azerbaijan through Presidential Order No. 2358 of 3 October 2016, establishes a national framework to protect biodiversity, restore ecosystems, and promote the sustainable use of natural resources, in line with the Convention on Biological Diversity. The strategy focuses on biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration, sustainable land management, and the protection of genetic resources. Key priorities include expanding and improving protected areas, strengthening biodiversity monitoring, restoring degraded forests and ecosystems, and protecting endangered species. Particular attention is given to agricultural biodiversity, including the conservation of traditional crop varieties and livestock breeds, sustainable pasture management, crop rotation, organic farming, and soil restoration. The strategy also promotes environmental education, institutional capacity building, public participation, and improved coordination among government agencies. Implementation is supported by a national action plan identifying responsible institutions and financing mechanisms.

The National Hygiene Promotion Strategy 2017–2020, developed by Afghanistan’s Ministry of Public Health, aims to improve hygiene and sanitation conditions and reduce the incidence of diseases associated with unsafe drinking water and inadequate sanitation facilities. The strategy focuses on promoting appropriate hygiene practices through awareness campaigns, health education, and community engagement. Key priorities include handwashing, safe drinking water management, improved hygiene practices in schools, menstrual hygiene management, and the prevention of waterborne diseases. It also emphasizes coordination among government institutions, non-governmental organizations, and local communities, supported by an implementation plan and a monitoring framework.

Germany’s Climate Action Plan 2050 (2016) establishes a long-term strategy to achieve extensive greenhouse gas neutrality by 2050, with an interim target of reducing emissions by at least 55% by 2030 compared with 1990 levels. It introduces sector-specific emission reduction targets for 2030, including 61–62% for energy, 66–67% for buildings, 40–42% for transport, 49–51% for industry and 31–34% for agriculture, with agricultural emissions limited to 58–61 MtCO₂e annually. Priority measures include expanding renewable energy, improving energy efficiency, decarbonizing transport and industry, reducing agricultural nitrogen surpluses and livestock emissions, protecting peatlands, promoting sustainable land management and strengthening forest carbon sinks. Adopted in November 2016, the plan provides strategic guidance through 2050, with milestones for 2030, sectoral implementation programmes, regular monitoring and periodic revisions. It does not establish a single consolidated implementation budget.

This Agricultural Policy Framework and Strategy provides decisions and measures that impact the growth and development of agricultural sector. The Policy Framework and Strategy identifies the following priority areas: agriculture diversification, based on improved research and development; strengthening of banana industry; enhancement of National food and nutrition security; reduction in the food import bill; agro-processing and agri-business development; internal and foreign market development; development and strengthening of appropriate institutional structures; increasing youth and women involvement in agriculture; effective management and utilisation of fisheries resources; protection, conservation and sustainable utilisation of natural resources of land, water and forestry sectors; disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation. For each priority area, the Policy provides a detailed analysis and targeted objectives and instruments for their achievement.

policy_description: National Action Plan for Gender Equality (2016-2020)
policydecision_details: The National Action Plan for Gender Equality 2016–2020 aims to eliminate gender-based discrimination and promote equal opportunities for women and men across all sectors of society. It builds on previous strategies while addressing new challenges such as the economic crisis and migration flows. The plan emphasizes gender mainstreaming in public policies and legislative reforms, ensuring compliance with international frameworks like CEDAW, the Beijing Platform for Action, and EU directives. Its overarching goal is to foster cultural change toward equality through awareness campaigns, education, and systematic monitoring. The plan’s strategic objectives focus on empowering women and protecting their rights, particularly those belonging to vulnerable groups such as migrants, refugees, Roma, and persons with disabilities. Key priorities include preventing and combating gender-based violence, improving access to health and education, and promoting women’s participation in the labor market and decision-making structures. Measures include legal reforms, support services for victims of violence, gender-sensitive curricula, and initiatives to close pay and pension gaps. Special attention is given to intersectionality, addressing compounded inequalities linked to poverty, ethnicity, and disability. Finally, the plan seeks to enhance women’s representation and leadership in politics, business, and cultural spheres while promoting balanced participation in sports and media. It encourages entrepreneurship, particularly in the social and solidarity economy, and supports family-work balance through improved parental leave policies and campaigns for shared domestic responsibilities. Implementation relies on multi-sectoral partnerships involving government agencies, civil society, and international organizations, supported by gender-disaggregated data collection and annual progress evaluations. Through these coordinated actions, the plan aims to create an inclusive society where gender equality is a fundamental principle.

policy_description: National Action Plan for Mainstreaming Gender in Tunisia (2016–2020)
policydecision_details: The National Action Plan for Mainstreaming and Institutionalizing Gender Equality in Tunisia (2016–2020) establishes a comprehensive national framework for integrating gender equality into public policies, development planning, government institutions and public budgets. Developed under the leadership of the Ministry of Women, Family and Childhood and the Council of Peers for Equality and Equal Opportunities between Women and Men, the plan supports the implementation of Tunisia's constitutional commitments to equality and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, particularly SDG 5. The Council of Peers was established by Government Decree No. 626 of 25 May 2016, while the action plan was formally approved by the Council of Ministers on 21 June 2018. Its main objective is to eliminate gender-based discrimination, strengthen women's participation in economic and political life, and institutionalize gender-responsive governance across public administration. The plan is structured around five strategic outcomes: eliminating discrimination and violence against women, strengthening women's political participation, promoting women's economic and financial empowerment, institutionalizing gender-responsive policies and budgets, and improving public awareness of gender equality. Key interventions include reviewing discriminatory legislation, strengthening mechanisms to prevent and respond to gender-based violence, increasing women's representation in elected bodies and decision-making positions, and expanding access to decent employment, entrepreneurship opportunities and financial resources. Particular attention is given to women's economic empowerment in rural and disadvantaged areas, including improving access to employment, essential services, education and economic opportunities. The plan also promotes gender-responsive budgeting, gender-disaggregated statistics, institutional capacity building and monitoring mechanisms to evaluate progress. It identifies women's participation in the labour market as a priority, with the broader national policy framework targeting an increase in women's economic activity rate from approximately 28% to 35% by 2020. Implementation involves government ministries, public institutions, civil society organizations and development partners, coordinated through the Council of Peers and supported by measurable objectives and performance indicators

policy_description: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (v.2)
