policydecision_details: South Africa’s Second National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP), finalized in July 2015, establishes a ten-year framework to conserve biodiversity, promote sustainable use of natural resources and strengthen biodiversity’s contribution to economic development, rural livelihoods and social well-being, aligned with the Convention on Biological Diversity and the Aichi Biodiversity Targets. The strategy identifies six strategic objectives addressing effective management of biodiversity assets, investment in ecological infrastructure, integration of biodiversity into sectoral policies, public participation, institutional capacity development and improved biodiversity knowledge. Priority measures include expanding and effectively managing protected areas, restoring degraded ecosystems, strengthening ecosystem-based adaptation, promoting biodiversity stewardship on communal and private lands, improving sustainable agriculture, forestry and fisheries, and protecting threatened species. The plan emphasizes biodiversity-related employment, poverty reduction, indigenous knowledge and equitable access to natural resources. Implementation covers 2015–2025, coordinated by the Department of Environmental Affairs with national and provincial institutions, municipalities, conservation organizations and local communities

policy_description: National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (v.2)
policydecision_details: Denmark’s National Biodiversity Strategy, Our Shared Nature (2014), aims to halt biodiversity loss by 2020 and establish a more diverse, resilient and interconnected natural environment by 2050. It identifies three priority areas: expanding and connecting natural habitats, strengthening the protection of wild animals and plants, and improving public access to nature and outdoor recreation. Key quantitative targets for 2020 include creating approximately 25,000 hectares of new natural areas, restoring 8,000 hectares of wetlands, converting 4,500 hectares of carbon-rich agricultural land into natural habitats, establishing 3,400 hectares of new forests, and improving biodiversity management across approximately 125,000 hectares. Implementation relies on the Green Map of Denmark, municipal land-use planning, voluntary agreements with landowners and partnerships with conservation organizations. The strategy provides DKK 20 million for pilot projects, with initial implementation focused on 2014–2020 and progressive habitat connectivity improvements continuing towards 2050.

policy_description: National strategy for integrated coastal zone management of Montenegro
policydecision_details: This National strategy for integrated coastal zone management of Montenegro (also called CAMP) sets basic management and conservation objectives in terms of sustainable and planned management of geographical zones that are classified as marine coastal areas. In order to preserve development potential of the coastal zone of Montenegro and limit growing pressures on its resources, it is here determine that it is necessary to establish an efficient, accountable and adaptable management system that will enable: − protection of productivity and diversity of coastal ecosystems, − improvement in economic efficiency and sustainable use of coastal zone resources, and − improvement in integration and alignment of sectoral management. Basic underlined benefits that are stated in this text are as follows: A more successful resolution of problems where involvement of more sectors is required; − Promotion of management culture based on obligation to achieve measurable results; − Reduction of damages (and related costs) caused to the coast due to natural processes (such as erosion and flooding) and human activities; − Mitigating pollution and reducing the costs it generates (for economy, human health); − Mitigating the over-exploitation of natural resources in the coastal zone; − Enhancing results of economic sectors in the coastal zone; − Preserving unique coastal ecosystems along with their habitats and species; − Preserving cultural heritage, landscapes and geomorphology of coastal zones; − Maximising coastal ecosystem services (such as climate regulation, water conservation, erosion and pollution prevention, food and raw material security and production, etc.); − Maximising economic efficiency (by improving environmental performance of coastal industries, reducing spatial conflicts , preserving coastal landscapes and attractions, maximising benefits from investments and tourism); − Promoting social cohesion and improving the quality of life for coastal communities. This strategy includes terms and aims that regard the preservation of biodiversity and nature among its resources, sustainable and controlled use and development, preservation of natural and cultural heritage, preservation oh habitats and species.

policy_description: “Azerbaijan 2020: Look into the Future” Development Concept
policydecision_details: The Azerbaijan 2020 is a national policy with a multi-sectoral approach. The overall objective of the policy is to achieve sustainable economic growth and high social welfare, effective state management and supremacy of the law, the full ensuring of all human rights and freedoms and the active status of the civil society in the country’s public life. Food security will be ensured through increased production and processing of agricultural products. Environmental protection will be ensured in line with the international and European standards with special emphasis on biodiversity conservation, coastal zone management, waste management, pollution control, disaster risk management, and soil conservation. The capacities of rural population will be enhanced through advanced international experience in the agriculture sector. In addition equipment, fertilizers, seeds and seedlings will be provided to peasants to enable their participation in agricultural production. Equal opportunities for women and men will be created in the labour market and the role of women will be strengthened. All social and public services required in the daily lives of citizens such as communications, Internet, banking services, public utilities, health and education services will be provided to all, even to the most remote villages. National policies on improvement maternal and infant health, preventive examinations, and the early prevention and treatment of childhood disability will be developed. Education system will be developed and modernized in accordance with the best international practice. Social security system will be improved by developing national policies. In order to make Azerbaijan an economically and politically developed and competitive country, highly effective economic system will be formed to have enough competitive power on a global scale. Effective use of the existing economic, social and political resources will be ensured by developing the energy, transport, transit and logistical infrastructure, and by fulfilling development at national and regional level. The mechanism of using oil and gas reserves will be improved by modernization of the systems for the extraction, transportation and refining of oil and gas. A complex consisting of oil and gas refineries and petrochemical factories will be established to make it possible to attract the necessary investments, observe environmental rules, establish a production chain up to the manufacture of the end product, increase the competitiveness of finished products and increase export in this field. Moreover in order to develop non-oil industry the involvement of the country’s natural and economic resources in the economic turnover will expand and the efficiency of their use will increase. The creation of new competitive spheres in the non-oil industry will be supported. The agrarian sector will be developed to increase the productive capability of existing agrarian-processing enterprises through the application of modern technologies and financing. Furthermore the production of eco-friendly agricultural and food products in the country will be stimulated. The land market in the country will be developed and farmers will be encouraged to join farming traditions on a voluntary basis. Melioration and irrigation measures will be strengthened, and measures will be intensified to prevent soil erosion and the salination of irrigated sowing areas and to increase fertility. The provision of agricultural producers with modern equipment, fertilizers, seeds and seedlings will be improved. In the agrarian sphere, it is planned to improve scientific support and staff training in the agrarian sector. In order to increase entrepreneurs’ skills and knowledge the scope of information and advisory services will be expanded, and cooperation with international organizations in the fields of veterinary and phytosanitary will be developed. The restoration and protection of immovable historical and cultural monuments, improvement of activities of historical and cultural reserves and its development will be ensured. State regulation in market relations will be established to maintain macroeconomic stability, improve the business environment in the country, ensure free competition, create favourable conditions for local and foreign investments, implement regulatory measures to improve the structure of the economy, implement investment and large-scale infrastructure projects and effectively organize the social protection of the population. Monopolies in the economy and especially on the consumer market will be restricted to form a fair competitive environment. The protection of consumers’ rights will be improved, effective mechanisms to control the quality of products will be created, national standards of quality control will be prepared and the system of certification will be improved. Measures will be taken to simplify and enhance foreign trade procedures and increase state support for entrepreneurs in increasing their competitiveness in foreign markets. Long-term sustainable economic development will be ensured by forming a knowledge-based economy through increased scientific potential and innovative activity.

policy_description: Unified Water Strategy and its Implementation Plan for the Gulf Cooperation Council Countries (GCC UWS) (2015–2035)
policydecision_details: The GCC Unified Water Strategy 2015–2035 and its Implementation Plan, developed by the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) in November 2015, establishes a regional framework to strengthen water security, promote sustainable water resources management, and address severe water scarcity across Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. The strategy responds to increasing water demand, groundwater depletion, dependence on desalination, and the environmental and economic challenges associated with water supply. The strategy focuses on water resource sustainability, water-use efficiency, agricultural water management, wastewater reuse, and integrated water governance. Its five strategic pillars address water resources development and sustainability, efficient and equitable water use, municipal water supply security, effective governance and public awareness, and economic efficiency and financial sustainability. Key priorities include improving desalination technologies, protecting groundwater resources, expanding wastewater treatment and reuse, modernizing irrigation systems, reducing excessive agricultural water consumption, and strengthening emergency water supply systems. Implementation is supported by a detailed action plan, performance indicators, and regional institutional coordination.

The Intended Nationally Determined Contribution (INDC) of the State of Kuwait (2015), submitted in November 2015 under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), establishes Kuwait’s initial climate mitigation and adaptation commitments for the 2020–2035 period. The document aims to support the transition towards a lower-carbon economy while addressing the country's vulnerability to rising temperatures, water scarcity, desertification, dust storms and sea-level rise. Recognizing Kuwait's substantial dependence on fossil fuels, the INDC emphasizes economic diversification, sustainable development and energy transition. Rather than establishing a quantified national emissions reduction target, it commits to limiting future greenhouse gas emissions growth relative to business-as-usual projections, subject to financial, technical and technological support. The INDC prioritizes renewable energy development, energy efficiency, sustainable transport, waste management, water security and climate adaptation. Mitigation measures include expanding solar and wind energy generation, improving fuel quality and refinery technologies, developing waste-to-energy facilities, introducing public transportation systems, and strengthening railway infrastructure. Adaptation priorities address Kuwait's particularly severe water constraints, including its dependence on seawater desalination, alongside the growing risks associated with extreme heat, declining rainfall, desertification and coastal flooding. The document also emphasizes strengthening national environmental legislation, institutional capacities and international cooperation to support implementation

policy_description: Information to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) on the Intended Nationally Determined Contribution (INDC) of the Republic of Azerbaijan.
policydecision_details: This Information to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) on the Intended Nationally Determined Contribution (INDC) of the Republic of Azerbaijan is a multi-sectoral policy document at national level. The INDC outlines a target: by 2030 the Republic of Azerbaijan targets 35% reduction in the level of greenhouse gas emissions compared to 1990/base year as its contribution to the global climate change efforts. Mitigation measures will be taken in the agricultural sector, including: Collect methane gas from manure of livestock and poultry, use of alternative sources of energy and modern technologies. For the Land Use, Land-Use Change, and Forestry (LULUCF) sector, the INDC proposed the following mitigation measures: plant new forest areas, water and land protecting forest strips (windbreaks), urban and roadside greenery as well as further improve the management of pastures and agricultural lands. In order to reduce vulnerability of Azerbaijan towards climate change impacts, it is considered to develop relevant adaptation measures for decreasing or minimizing the losses that may occur at national, local and community levels per sector.

policy_description: Development Plan for the Herbs, Spice and Condiments Industry in Barbados (2015-2022)
policydecision_details: The Development Plan for the Herbs, Spice and Condiments Industry in Barbados provides for the overarching planning framework that will guide stakeholder actions in the herbs, spice and condiments industry over the short, medium and long term, for the purpose of increasing local production, diversifying the current product offering and enhancing access to the local and international markets for local enterprises. The timeframe of this Plan is seven years covering the period of 2015-2022. The Development Plan specifically focuses on select herbs, spices and condiments namely, onions, hot peppers, thyme, marjoram, parsley, ginger, chives, celery, coriander and basil. The goals of this plan are: (I) to establish a formal institutional mechanism that facilitates appropriate Government policy and public sector support; joint collaboration, action, and investment among private players in the sector; (II) to ensure the availability of relevant and up to date information on the industry; (III) to reduce on- farm and post harvest losses within the sector through the application of modernised technology and systems; (IV) to increase the productive capacity of and application of standards by the various enterprises operating along the value chain; (V) to develop (high end) price competitive and differentiate value added products within the sector; and (VI) to maximize the commercial viability of stakeholders through increased market access to the domestic and international markets. A Public-Private Sector Dialogue and Action Platform will be established as an improved institutional mechanism to support the herbs, spices and condiments Industry. Post-harvest losses will be reduced or prevented by increasing the knowledge and understanding of post harvest systems/practices within the sector; establishing a multipurpose drying, packing, and processing facility; and reducing the impact of praedial larceny within the sector. The application of various systems of protected agricultural will be increased among farmers within the industry. Standards, such as good agricultural practices, health and safety standards and product specifications, will be applied by operators. New value-added products will be developed, including a product line of dried herbs and a high value differentiated product within the herb, spice and condiment industry suitable for both the local and export market. Efforts will be given to increase the consumption of local products within the local market and to increase export of the selected commodities.

The Integrated Approach to Nitrogen Programme 2015–2021 (Programma Aanpak Stikstof – PAS), adopted by the Government of the Netherlands in 2015 and partially revised on 18 December 2017, establishes a national framework to reduce nitrogen deposition, protect biodiversity, and reconcile environmental conservation with economic development. The programme addresses excessive nitrogen pollution affecting nitrogen-sensitive habitats and species within the European Union's Natura 2000 network, particularly from agricultural activities, livestock farming, transport, and industry. Its main objective is to prevent further deterioration of protected ecosystems, progressively restore their ecological condition, and create opportunities for economic activities compatible with nature conservation objectives. The programme covers the period from 1 July 2015 to 1 July 2021 and was developed jointly by national ministries and provincial authorities. The programme combines agricultural ammonia emission reductions, ecological restoration, nitrogen deposition monitoring, and regulated economic development. Agricultural measures include stricter emission standards for livestock housing, improved manure application practices, and voluntary livestock feeding and management measures. These interventions were projected to reduce agricultural ammonia emissions by at least 10 kilotonnes annually by 2030 compared with 2013 levels. Ecological restoration measures include improving hydrological conditions, raising groundwater levels, removing nitrogen-rich vegetation and restoring degraded habitats within Natura 2000 sites. The programme also introduces a system for allocating nitrogen deposition and development space to economic activities, supported by the AERIUS modelling and monitoring system. Implementation involves national ministries, provincial governments, agricultural organizations and environmental authorities, with periodic assessments of nitrogen deposition, ecosystem conditions and compliance.

policy_description: Stratégie nationale de conservation communautaire dans les aires protégées en République démocratique du Congo (2015-2020)
policydecision_details: The National Community Conservation Strategy in Protected Areas of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (2015–2020), revised in 2015 by the Congolese Institute for Nature Conservation (ICCN), establishes a framework for strengthening community participation in biodiversity conservation and sustainable natural resource management. Building on the original 2008 strategy and the 2014 Nature Conservation Law, it aims to reconcile environmental protection with local socioeconomic development, reduce conflicts between protected-area authorities and surrounding communities, and promote equitable access to natural resources and their benefits. The strategy focuses on participatory governance, biodiversity protection, sustainable livelihoods, benefit-sharing, and community empowerment. It identifies five priority programmes: strengthening governance and community participation in protected-area management; improving access to and equitable sharing of benefits from ecosystem services; expanding environmental education, information, and awareness; developing alternative income-generating activities and sustainable natural resource use; and strengthening planning, monitoring, and evaluation. Particular attention is given to recognizing indigenous peoples' traditional knowledge, improving dialogue between conservation authorities and local communities, reducing pressures on protected ecosystems, and supporting community-based development initiatives compatible with conservation objectives.

The policy focuses on the importance of agriculture in economic growth, socio-economic development, and poverty reduction within the Southern African Development Community region. The Policy outlines strategies aimed at enhancing agricultural productivity, improving food security, and promoting sustainable management of natural resources, all of which are critical for rural development. The policy emphasizes sustainable food security and the need to address declining forest resources due to deforestation. It outlines key objectives such as improving regional and international trade access for agricultural products, reducing trade impediments, and supporting farmers and traders to compete in global markets. The document highlights the significance of creating a conducive environment for agriculture and food-related regional trade by harmonizing trade relations with third parties and addressing adjustment costs that may impact specific populations. The policy is structured into four parts: Introduction, Conceptual Policy Framework, Policy and Strategy Statements, and Policy Implementation Mechanisms.

The Agricultural Mechanization Promotion Policy establishes a national policy framework to modernize agricultural production through the adoption of appropriate machinery, equipment, and mechanized farming technologies. The policy addresses low agricultural productivity, increasing production costs, rural labour shortages, and the limited commercialization of Nepalese agriculture. Its main objective is to increase agricultural productivity, competitiveness, and sustainability by promoting mechanization adapted to the country's diverse geographical conditions, particularly the Terai plains, hills, and mountainous areas. It also seeks to reduce women's labour burden, attract young people to agriculture, and support the transition from subsistence farming to commercially oriented agricultural production. The policy prioritizes agricultural technology development, mechanization services, public–private cooperation, institutional capacity building, and inclusive access to agricultural machinery. Key interventions include identifying and promoting affordable machinery suitable for smallholder farmers, strengthening agricultural engineering research and extension services, organizing training programmes and machinery demonstrations, and encouraging private-sector investment in equipment manufacturing, distribution, maintenance, and rental services. Particular attention is given to developing women-friendly and environmentally appropriate agricultural technologies, reducing physically demanding agricultural work, and improving access to mechanization in geographically disadvantaged areas. The policy also promotes cooperation among government institutions, cooperatives, and private enterprises, alongside the development of machinery quality standards, regulatory mechanisms, and institutional arrangements to support agricultural modernization

The objectives of the National Environmental Policy and Strategy are in light with the Ministry of Forestry, Fisheries, and Sustainable Development (MFFSD) vision, with the urgent need to ensure that the country revisit its policy and strategies to be responsive to new environmental challenges and commitments undertaken. Environmental documents are to be used to set policies, priorities, action plans and anticipated results for 2014-2024 based on a clear assessment of existing environmental challenges and resources and institutional framework and capacities to address them. These documents are also intended to be used as an operational/management tool for the mobilization of resources, development of capacity (both institutional and legal), and as guidance for addressing gaps and the improvement in the execution of the Department of Environment’s mandate. It recognizes that these are essential elements of GOB’s strategies to eradicate poverty by looking at these as a replenishable source of “natural capital”, essential in sustaining livelihoods and ensuring food security. It has as its core strategic outcome the “Greening of Belize’s Economy” (3.5.1). The methodology used in the execution of this activity provided the DOE with the opportunity to involve stakeholders (including NGOs), Civil Society, indigenous and local communities, private sector, and the media) in the process and include their inputs in the final documents. The overall objective is to have the DOE, the MFFSD, and stakeholders feel a sense of ownership since the method utilized ensured stakeholders active involvement in the preparation of the documents. The methodology was to organize the tasks into five major groups of activities. These activities were: 1. Background Research; 2. Stakeholder Consultations/Field Research; 3. An Analysis Process; 4. Drafting of Deliverables; and 5. Consultation Workshops including an Inception and a Validation Workshop. The strategic goals and targets for the major environmental issues addressed in this Strategy document and organized around the four strategic clusters, such as: Green, Clean, Resilient and Strong. The clusters pertaining to Green, Clean, and Resilient encompass the traditional issues focusing on environmental impacts; while the cluster pertaining to strong, focuses on the issues related to environmental governance and institutional capacity. This Strategic section focuses on addressing those issues related to the management of the natural resources and has as its long- term objective, a Belize where its natural resources, including land, forests, coastal and marine and water resources, are sustainably managed and conserved to improve the quality of life of present and future generation. The development of the Policy and Strategy Statement must address the above mentioned issues which makes evident the relationship between sustainable practices and economic development and Belize’s efforts to eradicate poverty. Vision: To be leaders in environmental stewardship for sustainable development both nationally and regionally. Mission: To ensure that Belize’s development is sound through effective environmental management for present and future generations. The Strategy is divided into 12 goals, as follows: 1. Degradation of Terrestrial Resources (A new and robust forest policy that aims to the sustainable use the forest and other natural ecosystems); 2. Degradation of Marine Resources (Protection and rational use of marine-coastal ecosystems and strengthen trans-boundary coordination and national actions with a focus on fisheries, tourism and marine areas); 3.Sustainable Land Management (implementation of the 2012 Belize National Land Use Policy); 4. Integrated Water Resources Management (integrated management water resources); 5. Challenges in Transitioning to a Green Economy; 6. Improve Waste Management; 7. Reduce Air Pollution; 8. Reduce Marine Pollution; 9. Integrated Chemicals Management; 10. Disaster Risk Reduction (resilient communities to the effects of natural, technological and environmental hazards and engendering a shift from protection against hazards to risk management); 11. Response to Global Climate Change; 12. Environmental Governance and Institutional Strengthening.

policy_description: Strategic Action Plan on Gender Equality (2014-2017)
policydecision_details: The Strategic Action Plan on Gender Equality 2014–2017 aims to promote equality between men and women across all sectors of Cypriot society. Developed by the Ministry of Justice and Public Order, the plan builds on previous national efforts and responds to evaluations and recommendations from both domestic stakeholders and international bodies like the CEDAW Committee. It recognizes the disproportionate impact of economic crises on women and seeks to address systemic inequalities through targeted, realistic actions within the state’s financial and administrative capacities. Six priority objectives guide the plan: (1) effective promotion of gender equality through administrative reform, (2) modernization of the legislative framework, (3) balanced participation in decision-making positions, (4) elimination and prevention of violence against women, (5) economic empowerment of women and poverty eradication, and (6) elimination of social stereotypes and prejudices. Each objective is supported by interim goals, specific actions, responsible agencies, timelines, and monitoring indicators to ensure accountability and progress. The plan emphasizes interdepartmental coordination and stakeholder engagement, including NGOs, equality bodies, and local authorities. It integrates gender mainstreaming into public administration, strengthens the National Machinery for Women’s Rights, and promotes legal reforms to eliminate discrimination. Special attention is given to vulnerable groups such as migrant women, women with disabilities, and victims of violence, ensuring inclusive and equitable access to justice, employment, and social services. Education and media play a central role in transforming societal attitudes. The plan includes initiatives to integrate gender equality into school curricula, train educators and public officials, and raise awareness through campaigns. By fostering a culture of equality and dismantling patriarchal norms, the Strategic Action Plan seeks to create a more just and inclusive society where both women and men can participate fully and equally in all aspects of life.

policy_description: Gender and Climate Change Strategic Plan Ministry of Women’s Affairs (2013-2023)
policydecision_details: This Gender and Climate Change Strategic Plan of the Ministry of Women’s Affairs (2013-2023) is a sectoral policy document. As a goal, the Royal Government of Cambodia’s (RGC) Ministry of Women’s Affairs (MoWA) seeks to ensure that gender and climate change agendas are fully integrated into public policymaking on climate change within MoWA for Neary Rattanak IV (NRIV), line ministries for sectoral strategic plans, by ensuring that national and sub-national institutional mechanisms for gender mainstreaming are fully charged; GCCC/MoWA and Gender Mainstreaming Action Groups (GMAGs) are fully capacitated and articulating key policy messages and benefits expected by the integration of gender equality and women’s empowerment. Climate Change is relatively new development agenda to Ministry of Women’s Affairs (MoWA). Based on the findings of analyzing economic development from a gender perspective, the Document proposes policy measures covering both adaptation and mitigation, cross-cutting agendas and institutional, organizational and human capacity development, research and development, financing, monitoring and evaluation. Strategic objectives are: 1. Women’s participation in climate change policymaking is increased; 2. The funding rules for gender and climate change initiatives are established and made operational through gender-responsive budget in the current and upcoming projects/programmes/policies (both external and national sources); 3. The level of awareness of public policymakers is increased on the importance of gender equality in climate change adaptation and mitigation, to achieve sectoral goals in climate change; 4. Women’s climate change adaptation and mitigation needs are met by strategic and catalytic initiatives on gender and climate change on a priority basis, following the development of criteria, based on the findings of vulnerability and adaptation analyses; 5. National capacities are enhanced to plan, implement and monitor gender-integrated climate change adaptation and mitigation initiatives; 6. Effective mechanisms for scaling up the proven experiences on gender and climate change are identified; lessons and best practices of gender and climate change are elicited and analysed for sharing and learning in national, regional and global forums.

The National Agricultural Sector Investment Plan 2013–2017 (Plano Nacional de Investimento do Sector Agrário – PNISA), developed by the Ministry of Agriculture of Mozambique, establishes a five-year investment framework to promote agricultural growth, food and nutrition security, poverty reduction, and sustainable natural resource management. The plan operationalizes the country's Strategic Plan for Agricultural Sector Development (PEDSA 2011–2020) and its commitments under the Comprehensive Africa Agriculture Development Programme (CAADP). Its main objective is to develop a prosperous, competitive, equitable, and sustainable agricultural sector by increasing agricultural productivity, strengthening market-oriented production, improving farmers' incomes, and addressing structural constraints affecting agriculture, livestock, fisheries, and rural development. The PNISA is organized around five investment components: agricultural production and productivity, market access, food and nutrition security, natural resource management, and institutional reform and capacity building. Key interventions include improving food and cash crop production, strengthening livestock and fisheries development, expanding agricultural research and extension services, investing in irrigation and mechanization, improving rural roads and post-harvest infrastructure, and facilitating farmers' access to financial services and markets. The plan also promotes access to nutritious foods, sustainable land and forest management, and stronger agricultural institutions. Its estimated investment requirement is approximately USD 4.25 billion, with around 79% of financing needs initially unfunded. Implementation involves government institutions, private-sector stakeholders, development partners, and civil society, supported by coordination, monitoring, and evaluation mechanisms.

policy_description: Belgian action plan to reduce the risks and impacts linked to pesticides (2013-2017)
policydecision_details: This Belgian Action Plan (NAPAN) to reduce the risks and impacts linked to pesticides is composed of the action plans of all involved competent authorities at national, federal and regional level, as follows (I) Federal Program for the Reduction of Pesticides (FPRP); (II) Flemish Action Plan for a Sustainable Use of Pesticides; (III) Walloon Plan for the Reduction of Pesticides; and (IV) Brussels Regional Program for the Reduction of Pesticides. Each of these plans contains specific actions and joint actions that are set up in cooperation with the other members of the NAPAN Task Force (NTF). Being all developed under the Directive 2009/128/EC of 21 October 2009 establishing a framework for Community action to achieve the sustainable use of pesticides, many od the proposed measures are similar. The FPRP aims at reducing, by all means possible, the risks and consequences of the use of Plant Protection Products (ppp), to be understood as pesticides, and biocides (disinfectants, wood preservatives, parasiticides, rodenticides, antifouling products, etc.) for human health and the environment, including a reduction of the use and placement in the market of these products if reduction of such use is the suitable means to realize a reduction of the risk. It intervenes on a series of thematic areas for which it sets objectives. The main ones of these areas are (i) certification of the know-how of professionals working with ppp; (ii) conditions for the sale of products; (iii) informing the general public; (iv) protection of specific areas against ppp; (v) using professional ppp; (vi) bee protection; and (vii) observatory for ppp and biocides. To make agriculture more sustainable, main measures taken by the present Action Plans include (i) the issuance of the Phytolicence for all professional users, sellers and information providers on ppp for professional use; (ii) the provision of well-balanced information, online and not, to non-professional users about the proper conditions of ppp use and the risks for public health and the environment; (iii) extreme care in the management of ppp storage sites; (iv) monitoring the effects of ppp and biocides on bees; (iv) protect water against ppp; (v) create a more efficient monitoring strategy on the ppp use. The Government of Flanders in its Action Plan (i) adds the promotion of the use of alternatives; (ii) explicitly mentions the protection of the aquatic environment (both surface and groundwater) and drinking water; (iii) the protection of particular vulnerable groups, such as children; and (iv) focuses on the importance of the Integrated pest management, suggesting to make general IPM principles mandatory. As for the Walloon Pesticide Reduction Programme (WPRP) it aims at (i) renovate regulations on the management of public areas in order to eliminate the use of plant protection products (zero PPP); (ii) protect vulnerable groups in public and private areas used by the general public; (iii) improve the knowledge and tracking of the acute and chronic effects of pesticide use on applicators and on local inhabitants; (iv) amplify awareness campaigns for professional and amateur users focusing on the dangers of pesticide use; and (v) protect surface water and groundwater to reduce the percentage of cases where the thresholds of standards are exceeded. Brussels Regional Program for the Reduction of Pesticides is a regional program aiming at reducing the health and environmental risks related to pesticide use, in particular by reducing recourse to pesticides and giving priority to alternate methods and techniques by both managers of public areas and private individuals.

The National Development Plan 2013–2017 (Plano Nacional de Desenvolvimento), adopted by the Government of Angola in 2012, establishes a comprehensive framework for promoting economic growth, social development, and structural transformation. Its main priorities include macroeconomic stability, economic diversification beyond the oil sector, employment creation, poverty reduction, and improved access to essential public services. The plan places particular emphasis on agricultural development and food security, promoting agricultural productivity, irrigation infrastructure, agro-industrial development, and stronger domestic food production. It also prioritizes investments in education, healthcare, water and sanitation, transport infrastructure, and social protection. The strategy encourages private sector development, regional economic integration, and more balanced territorial development, supported by public investment programmes and a monitoring and evaluation framework

The Ghana Agriculture Sector Investment Programme (GASIP) aims at providing a framework and institutional basis for a long-term engagement and supplementary financing for scaling up investments in private sector-led pro-poor agricultural value chain development. GASIP will contribute to the realization of Ghana’s Medium Term Agriculture Sector Investment Programme (METASIP), which provides the road map for the CAADP compact in Ghana. In line with the agreed Strategic Framework for IFAD in Ghana (2012 COSOP), GASIP is built along four (4) strategic axis: (i) linking smallholder farmers to agribusinesses to enhance pro-poor growth, (ii) nationwide scaling up of a successful value chain investment approach, (iii) promoting and mainstreaming climate change resilience approaches in Ghana, in particular in the northern regions, financed through the Adaptation for Smallholder Agriculture Programme (ASAP) and (iv) knowledge management, harmonization of intervention approaches and policy optimization. The overall goal of GASIP is to contribute to sustainable poverty reduction in rural Ghana. The Programme Development Objective is: “agribusinesses, including smallholders, have enhanced their profitability and climate change resilience”. Regarding the reduction of rural poverty, GASIP is highly compliant with IFADs Strategic Framework 2011-2015. GASIP has a clear focus on enabling poor rural women and men to overcome poverty. GASIP is aligned to the 5 strategic objectives of the framework, especially: (i) a natural resource and economic asset base for poor rural women and men that is more resilient to climate change, environmental degradation and market transformation; (ii) access for poor rural women and men to services to reduce poverty, improve nutrition, raise incomes and build resilience in a changing environment; (iii) poor rural women and men and their organizations able to manage profitable, sustainable and resilient farm and non-farm enterprises or take advantage of decent work opportunities, (iv) poor rural women and men and their organizations are able to influence policies and institutions that affect their livelihoods. To enable inclusive and efficient agricultural and food systems, GASIP aims to leverage investments in commercial infrastructure and facilities. These will be facilities, owned by a private sector player or a District Assembly, but operated by a private sector entity for the benefit of all value chain participants. In addition, GASIP aims to finance essential public infrastructure for the growth and viability of associated value chains. These are facilities completely operated and maintained by the public sector. Finally, GASIP aims at ensuring increased and systematic access to and use of short and long term financing for value chain businesses. In this context, GASIP will: (i) in collaboration other projects, provide capacity building Rural and Community Banks (RCBs) to improve performance in liquidity management, delinquency management, structured trade finance and savings mobilization, (ii) support universal banks in strategic and operational development for structured trade finance, (iii) promote equity style investments in value chain enterprises including finance leasing and venture capital, (iv) promote equity development in RCBs through direct investment and linkage with larger banks, and (v) through grant mechanisms match high potential, weakly capitalized value chain actors’ equity to leverage finance for investments in equipment and infrastructure. To increase the resilience of livelihoods to threats and crises, GASIP aims at mainstreaming climate change resilience across the selected agricultural value chains through a broad promotion of technologies proven elsewhere. GASIP will focus on three domains. Firstly, commercially valid adaptive trials and demonstrations of modern conservation agriculture techniques under rain fed conditions and in situ rainwater conservation techniques will be undertaken. Secondly, demonstrations of efficient water-use techniques within new and existing irrigation systems will be undertaken. Thirdly, institutional capacity building and enhanced public awareness of private and public value chain actors in the field of climate change resilience will be supported. Initial funding will be provided through the Adaptation for Smallholder Agriculture Programme (ASAP). The demonstrated activities will thereafter be taken up under the financing from the IFAD resources and those of other future co-financiers. In the context of governance, MOFA will have overall responsibility for the implementation of GASIP. A National Programme Steering Committee (NPSC) will orient programme strategy, oversee planning, review progress and ensure linkages with related entities. The Programme Coordination Unit (PCU) will be based in Accra and ensure overall coordination of the Programme, support supervision, Inter-cycle Review and evaluation missions, consolidation of the Annual Work Programme and Budget (AWPB) and progress reports, fiduciary and procurement oversight, and promotion of transversal themes.

policy_description: Programme national de prévention et de lutte contre les zoonoses émergentes et ré-émergentes au Cameroun
policydecision_details: The National Programme for the Prevention and Control of Emerging and Re-emerging Zoonoses (Programme National de Prévention et de Lutte contre les Zoonoses Émergentes et Ré-émergentes), developed by the Government of Cameroon in March 2012, establishes a multisectoral framework to prevent, detect, and control zoonotic diseases through a One Health approach, integrating human, animal, and environmental health. The programme aims to reduce public health risks associated with diseases transmitted between domestic animals, wildlife, and humans, while strengthening national preparedness and response capacities. The programme focuses on epidemiological surveillance, early disease detection, scientific research, and institutional capacity building. Its three main components include strengthening surveillance and outbreak response systems, promoting scientific and operational research on zoonotic diseases, and improving professional training and technical capacities. Particular attention is given to risks associated with livestock production, wildlife exploitation, and human–animal interactions. The programme also promotes interministerial coordination, improved laboratory capacities, information sharing, and stronger regulatory frameworks. Implementation is supported by a national coordination mechanism, resource mobilization arrangements, and monitoring and evaluation systems.

This National Irrigation Policy (Revised 2012) provides strategic direction for Bhutan’s irrigation sub-sector to enhance food self-sufficiency and economic growth. It transitions from a narrow focus on traditional paddy cultivation toward a holistic, multi-sectoral approach that emphasizes sustainable water resource management and integrated river basin planning. The Policy outlines eight core objectives, including accelerating sector investments, diversifing irrigation beyond paddy, promoting alternative water sources, strengthening technical capacity, and empowering beneficiaries through farmer-centered participation. It mandates the creation of an Irrigation Development Master Plan and explores alternative technologies like groundwater harvesting and drip irrigation to diversify crop production beyond paddy. More specifically, the Policy institutionalises monitoring and evaluation through comprehensive irrigation inventories, baseline surveys, and SMART and QQTP indicators. Responsibilities for planning, implementation, and reporting are clearly allocated across national, regional, and local institutions to ensure accountability and sustainable scheme management .

policy_description: Strategy for Agricultural Development in Georgia (2012-2022)
policydecision_details: The Strategy for Agricultural Development in Georgia 2012–2022, approved by the Government of Georgia through Decree No. 566 of 28 March 2012, establishes a long-term framework for modernizing the agricultural sector, increasing competitiveness, and strengthening national food security. Developed by the Ministry of Agriculture, the strategy aims to create an efficient, competitive, and sustainable agrifood sector by improving agricultural productivity, developing value chains, attracting private investment, and strengthening institutional capacities. The strategy focuses on agricultural modernization, farmer competitiveness, agrifood value-chain development, rural infrastructure, and food security. Key priorities include establishing agricultural research stations and extension centres, creating a national farmers' registry, developing agricultural land markets and a land bank, and improving access to credit, leasing, and insurance. It also promotes the introduction of improved crop varieties and modern technologies, agricultural processing and marketing, wholesale markets, and public-private investment in irrigation, machinery, and rural infrastructure. Additional measures aim to strengthen agricultural education and technical training, improve agricultural statistics and market information systems, and establish food security monitoring mechanisms. The strategy emphasizes market-oriented agricultural development and private investment rather than direct production subsidies.

policy_description: Program for the development of production of oilseeds, oilseed production and fat-and-oil products and protein feed for (2012-2015)
policydecision_details: The Programme for the Development of Oilseed Production, Oil and Fat Products, and Protein Feed in Belarus (2012–2015), approved by the Government of Belarus through Resolution No. 799 of 31 August 2012, establishes a national framework to strengthen domestic agricultural production, reduce import dependency, and increase exports of vegetable oils and protein-rich animal feed. The programme focuses on expanding oilseed cultivation, modernizing agro-industrial processing facilities, and strengthening domestic agricultural value chains. Key priorities include increasing the production of rapeseed, sunflower, soybean, and flax seeds; improving processing efficiency; expanding vegetable oil and protein feed production; and enhancing the competitiveness of domestic products. It sets targets of cultivating 536,000 hectares of oilseed crops and producing at least 1 million tonnes of marketable oilseeds annually from 2014. The programme also promotes investments in processing infrastructure, technological innovation, financial support to agricultural producers, and the development of integrated production facilities to strengthen domestic supply and export capacity.

policy_description: State Program “Engineering water management measures to protect populated areas and agricultural land from floods in the most flood-prone areas of Polesie" (2012-2015)
policydecision_details: The State Programme on Engineering Water Management Measures for the Protection of Settlements and Agricultural Land against Flooding in the Most Flood-Prone Areas of Polesia (2011–2015), approved by the Government of Belarus through Resolution No. 1280 of 6 September 2010, establishes a framework to reduce flood risks, protect rural communities, and safeguard agricultural production in flood-prone areas. The programme focuses on flood prevention, water management infrastructure, and agricultural land protection. Key measures include constructing and upgrading flood protection infrastructure, such as embankments, pumping stations, drainage canals, and water regulation systems. It aims to protect 108 settlements, approximately 113,000 inhabitants, and 76,000 hectares of agricultural land, while reducing economic losses and improving agricultural productivity. The programme also incorporates environmental protection measures, including the preservation of riverbank ecosystems and wildlife habitats, and provides for public investment and monitoring of implementation.

policy_description: Mahinda Chintana – Vision for the Future
policydecision_details: This policy aims at the sustainable development of Sri Lanka and particularly to achieve a number of improvements, including the following: (a) sustained economic growth of around 6 percent; (b) reduce unemployment and poverty; (c) raise access to safe drinking water and services such as electricity and road access. The vision envisages a Sri Lanka that has an economy with a green environment and rapid development; aspires to be a stable society with a high quality of life for all of its people having access to decent living, electricity, water, schooling and health facilities; maintains the best of Sri Lankan culture, traditions and long standing global identity; aims to consolidate as an emerging market economy, integrated into the global economy and is competitive internationally. The policy refers to the period from 2010 to 2016 and is composed of the following Chapters: (1) Sri Lanka: The Emerging Wonder of Asia; (2) A Prosperous Country: A Land of Plenty; (3) Enterprises with Strength to Conquer the World; (4) Developed Road Network and Transport System; (5) Focus on Modern Education and Knowledge Systems; (6) A Healthy Society; (7) Comforts, Convenience and Satisfactory Lifestyle; (8) Shared Values and Rapid Development. Eradication of hunger and hard-core poverty is one of the main targets of the Vision. The overall objective is to reach a stable society with a high quality of life for all people having access to decent living, electricity, water, schooling and health facilities. Regarding malnutrition of children, the objective is to reduce rate from a third to 12-15 percent. Further the policy aims to increase access to clean water in urban areas from 65 to 90 percent. As mentioned, the Vision is focused on green economy. It aims to make agriculture, forestry and fisheries more productive and sustainable. The Government’s agricultural policy aims at realizing multiple goals including (a) achieving food security of people, (b) expanding the extent under cultivation, (c) reducing wastage in transit, (d) ensuring environmental conservation, (e) introducing efficient farm management techniques, and (f) using high yielding seeds and improved water management. The policy promotes the promotion of specific crops and boosts crop diversifcation. Regarding fisheries, the policy policy aims at exploiting the country’s fisheries and aquatic resources in a sustainable manner, while conserving the coastal environment. The government is targeting self-sufficiency in the national fish supply and a significant increase in fish exports. The document also seeks to enable more inclusive and efficient agricultural and food systems. In particular it aims at ensuring higher and sustainable income for farmers; remunerative prices for agricultural produce; uninterrupted access to competitive markets both in Sri Lanka and abroad; farm mechanization. Regarding rural employment, the policy seeks to ensure that rural youth acquire the necessary skills to secure highly paid jobs. Special attention is also given to women in rural areas. Particular measures on irrigation and water resources management in relation to agriculture are foreseen as well. Regarding disaster management, a culture of safety of the nation will be created through systematic management of natural, technological and man-made disaster risks. Both public and private sector media will be voluntary bodies to prepare the country for environmental changes. All citizens will be made aware of natural disasters, mitigation and adaptation.

policy_description: Strategic Plan for a New Modern National Agricultural Health and Food Control System in Barbados.
policydecision_details: The Strategic Plan for a New Modern National Agricultural Health and Food Control System is a national policy with a cross-sectoral approach. The main purpose of this Strategic Plan is to improve public health and increase quality and competitiveness of agricultural and fishery products by raising agricultural health and food safety standards to international levels. This Strategic Plan sets forth activities to ensure food safety and quality towards (I) consumer protection, (II) competitiveness of industries, (III) institutional capacity building, and (IV) protection of environment. Legislative and regulatory framework for food safety, veterinary drugs control, animal health, food standards, consumer protection, agricultural health and food control will be improved. A Technical Management Committee will be established to facilitate the cooperation and communication needed for the development and enactment of legislation as well as achievement of other goals, objectives and tasks in this Strategic Plan. National controls will be established for harmful plants and animals, pests and diseases to prevent and control threats to Barbadian plant and animal health, in accordance with international norms. Risk assessment units will be established for animal health, plant health and food safety through the systematic collection, analysis and interpretation of the data in order to evaluate and identify the ten highest risk priority plant diseases or invasive species, and the ten highest risk priority animal diseases. Standards will be developed for plant health, animal health and food safety in accordance with the Codex Alimentarius, Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures, the World Organisation for Animal Health and the International Plant Protection Convention. Food control management systems will be strengthened with a farm-to-fork approach. The monitoring and inspection systems will be developed for the agricultural sector, including HACCP, Good Agricultural Practices, Good Manufacturing Processes, and traceability. Moreover, a traceability and recall system will be developed for the food industry. The quality assurance programmes will be developed for the laboratories and inspection and quarantine facilities at ports of entry. Awareness of industry, consumers and other relevant persons and organisations will be raised through training, access to information, and communication. Food safety emergency response systems will be developed for active surveillance of foodborne diseases and related epidemiologic studies. The National Agricultural Health and Food Control Agency shall be responsible for the monitoring of the implementation and reporting the progress of this Strategic Plan. Moreover, the Agency shall carry out annual evaluations of the National Agricultural Health and Food Control Systems to ascertain progress, accomplishments, issues/problems and future needs.

policy_description: State Program for the Study and Preservation of Glaciers (2010-2030)
policydecision_details: The State Programme for the Study and Conservation of Glaciers of the Republic of Tajikistan for 2010–2030 establishes a 20-year national framework for monitoring, studying and protecting the country's glaciers. The programme responds to the accelerating retreat of glaciers caused by climate change and its implications for freshwater availability, agricultural production, hydropower generation and disaster risks. At the time of adoption, Tajikistan had more than 8,000 glaciers covering approximately 8% of its territory, containing an estimated 550 km³ of freshwater and contributing nearly half of the country's river runoff. Its main objective is to establish an effective national glaciological monitoring system to support water resource management, climate change adaptation and the prevention of hydrometeorological disasters. The programme prioritizes glacier inventories, systematic climate monitoring, scientific research, satellite-based observation and hydrological forecasting. Key interventions include establishing a National Centre for Glaciology and Hydrometeorology, developing a comprehensive glacier catalogue, restoring snow and avalanche observation networks, installing automated monitoring stations in remote mountain areas, and introducing high-resolution satellite technologies to monitor glacier retreat, snow cover and river flows. Additional measures focus on assessing potentially dangerous glacial lakes, improving forecasts of floods, mudflows and avalanches, developing climate impact models, and strengthening scientific cooperation and professional training. Particular attention is given to developing adaptation measures for agriculture and hydropower, as glacier retreat threatens seasonal water availability, especially during summer irrigation periods. The programme also envisages establishing a national glaciological information database, preparing regulatory measures to protect glacier territories, and strengthening cooperation with regional and international research institutions. Implementation is coordinated by the Government of Tajikistan, particularly its Committee for Environmental Protection, in collaboration with international organizations.

The Water Sector Development Programme of the Republic of Tajikistan for 2010–2025 establishes a long-term framework for the sustainable management, development and protection of Tajikistan's water resources. Developed by an interministerial working group with technical assistance from the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), the programme addresses deteriorating water infrastructure, inefficient irrigation systems, inadequate drinking water and sanitation services, and growing pressures associated with climate change and economic development. Its main objective is to improve water-use efficiency, strengthen water governance and ensure the sustainable allocation of water resources across agriculture, hydropower, domestic consumption and environmental protection. It builds on the national Water Code and earlier water-sector strategies, emphasizing the need for coordinated institutional reforms and investment planning. The programme prioritizes irrigation and drainage modernization, integrated water resources management, drinking water supply, wastewater treatment, hydropower development and water-related disaster risk reduction. Key interventions include rehabilitating irrigation canals, pumping stations and drainage networks; improving agricultural water productivity; strengthening water user associations; and introducing more effective water allocation and management mechanisms. Particular attention is given to irrigated agriculture, which represents a major component of national water consumption and is essential for agricultural productivity, rural livelihoods and food security. Additional measures address the rehabilitation of drinking water and sanitation infrastructure, improved monitoring of surface and groundwater resources, protection against water pollution, and the management of floods, mudflows and other hydrological hazards. The programme also promotes institutional decentralization, improved coordination among water-sector authorities, greater participation by water users, and reforms to financing and cost-recovery mechanisms. Implementation requires substantial public and external investment, with priorities to be pursued according to available financial resources.

policy_description: National Policy on Food and Nutrition (2010-2025)
policydecision_details: The National Food and Nutrition Policy (Política Nacional de Alimentação e Nutrição – PNAN), updated by Brazil’s Ministry of Health through Ordinance No. 2,715 of 17 November 2011 and published in 2012, establishes a national framework to improve food, nutrition, and health conditions while ensuring the human right to adequate food and promoting food and nutrition security.The policy focuses on promoting healthy diets, preventing malnutrition and obesity, addressing micronutrient deficiencies, and strengthening nutrition services within the public healthcare system. Key priorities include improving maternal and child nutrition, promoting breastfeeding and healthy complementary feeding, strengthening food and nutrition surveillance, regulating food quality and safety, and encouraging nutrition education. It also emphasizes intersectoral coordination, community participation, professional training, and research to address nutritional inequalities and diet-related non-communicable diseases.

policy_description: Strategy for the implementation of the Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat
policydecision_details: The National Strategy for the Implementation of the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands (2009–2014), approved by the Government of Belarus through Resolution No. 177 of 10 February 2009, establishes a national framework for the conservation, restoration, and sustainable use of wetlands, particularly those of international importance as waterbird habitats. The strategy aims to protect biodiversity, maintain essential ecosystem services, and strengthen Belarus's compliance with the Ramsar Convention. The strategy focuses on wetland conservation, ecosystem restoration, biodiversity protection, and sustainable water and land management. Key priorities include restoring degraded peatlands and natural hydrological regimes, improving wetland inventories and monitoring systems, protecting endangered species, controlling invasive alien species, and expanding the network of internationally important wetlands. It also promotes integrated river basin management, sustainable forestry and land-use planning, environmental education, ecotourism, and transboundary cooperation. Specific conservation objectives cover 30,000 hectares of open lowland mires, 40,000 hectares of floodplain meadows, and 160,000 hectares of raised and transitional bogs.

policy_description: Forestry and Climate Change Framework for Action (2009–2015)
policydecision_details: The Forestry and Climate Change Framework for Action is a national policy, and its timeframe is 7 years covering the period of 2009–2015. The primary goal of this framework is to ensure that the people of Papua New Guinea build their capacity to: (i) ensure ownership of carbon credits; (ii) become resilient to the risks and impacts of climate change; (iii) implement adaptation measures; (iv) contribute to the mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions, (v) improve decision-making and good governance; (vi) enhance understanding of climate change and its effects; (vii) promote education and awareness; and (viii) develop and strengthen partnerships and international cooperation. This goal will be achieved through a strategic, multi-stakeholder, and programmatic approach, coordinated by the national government and supported by the PNG Forest Authority. The framework is designed to guide sustainable development, address economic, environmental, and social opportunities and challenges, and ensure that forests, the environment, and livelihoods are resilient to climate change risks. All natural forest carbon will be owned by the customary landowners and managed by the state. Efforts will be made to ensure efficiency and equity in benefit sharing in any future carbon trading schemes. Landowner will be empowered to participate and own Reduced Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD), REDD+ and Afforestation and Reforestation Clean Development Mechanism (ARCDM) projects. Measures will be taken to prevent marginalization of rural communities which are dependent on forests. Adaptation measures against the impacts of climate change will be developed and implemented at all levels. ARCDM projects on forestry initiatives will be facilitated and developed with communities adaptation funds. Highly vulnerable forestry priority areas will be identified through site-specific baseline data, collection and interpretation and adaptive actions will be developed. Integrated approaches to adaptation will be embedded in national sustainable development plans and budgeting process. Research & development will be directed into forest types and climate impacts. Restoration and rehabilitation will be carried out through forestry enrichment and plantation development with soil protecting species in highly degraded areas. Climate change will be mainstreamed into forestry management plans and policies. Methodologies and research initiatives will be incorporated and streamlined into school curriculum. Agroforestry will be promoted, and important environmental economic and social services will be provided to improve local communities' capacity to cope with adverse climatic events. Effective management of coastal mangrove and littoral forest will be ensured to minimize effects of heavy storms and rising sea level on coastal communities. Demonstration projects such as REDD, and other initiatives will be coordinated and developed in the productive forest areas. Renewable energy efficiency measures and technologies will be promoted and implemented. Timber royalties and compensation fees to landowners will be facilitated. Baseline study on potential Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) will be completed urgently in the sectors of forestry, waste, renewable energy and technology. Greenhouse Gas inventories will be updated and maintained. Climate Change issues and considerations will be integrated into the Forestry Act and National Forest Policy, as well as into national sustainable development strategies, plans or their equivalent. Regulatory and incentive-based approaches will be developed and adopted to encourage appropriate adaptation, mitigation and REDD measures. Cost-effective climate change adaptation and mitigation policies, strategies, decision-making processes and management instruments will be developed. The State Marketing Agency will be established and a Carbon Fund will be incorporated for ARCDM activities. REDD strategy will be developed and demonstrated. Accurate carbon accounting and verification methodology will be developed and adopted for different forest types. Technical datasets will be integrated with relevant social and economic information and traditional knowledge for risk management, especially bush fires and natural disasters. Human capacity will be strengthened to monitor and assess environmental, social and economic risks and effects of climate change through ARCDM and REDD initiatives. Community awareness on climate change and forest impacts will be enhanced, particularly on the flexible mechanisms, including monetary and ecological benefits from the forests.

The National Cereal Sector Plan (Piano di Settore Cerealicolo), developed by Italy’s Ministry of Agricultural, Food and Forestry Policies around 2009–2010, establishes a strategic framework to improve the competitiveness, profitability, and organization of the Italian cereal sector. Developed in cooperation with regional authorities and cereal supply-chain stakeholders, the plan addresses structural weaknesses affecting cereal production, processing, storage, and marketing. Its overall objective is to strengthen domestic cereal production, improve coordination across agrifood value chains, and enhance the sector’s competitiveness in increasingly international markets. The plan focuses on agricultural competitiveness, cereal production modernization, supply-chain integration, market transparency, and research and innovation. Key priorities include improving the quality and quantity of domestic wheat, maize, and other cereal production; promoting sustainable and economically viable farming practices; strengthening producer organizations and contractual agreements between farmers and processors; and modernizing storage, transport, and logistics infrastructure. Additional measures aim to improve market information and price transparency, strengthen the seed sector, encourage technological innovation and agricultural research, and expand access to international markets. Particular attention is given to the durum wheat–pasta, soft wheat–bread, and maize–livestock feed value chains, with the objective of improving profitability and reducing structural inefficiencies.

policy_description: Regional environmental program for sustainable development of Central Asia for the period 2020–2030.
policydecision_details: The Regional Environmental Programme for Sustainable Development in Central Asia 2020–2030, developed under the Interstate Commission on Sustainable Development (ICSD) of the International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea (IFAS), establishes a regional framework for environmental protection and sustainable natural resource management across Central Asia, including Kazakhstan. The programme aims to strengthen regional cooperation in addressing shared environmental challenges, particularly climate change, water scarcity, land degradation, biodiversity loss and pollution. It builds on earlier regional environmental initiatives and seeks to align national environmental strategies with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), promoting a transition towards a green economy and more resilient ecosystems. The programme focuses on climate adaptation, transboundary water management, ecosystem restoration, sustainable land use, biodiversity conservation and green economic development. Key priorities include developing a regional climate adaptation strategy, monitoring glaciers and climate-related hazards, improving water quality monitoring and wastewater management, and combating desertification through sustainable management of forests, agricultural land and pastures. Additional measures promote renewable energy, waste recycling, environmentally sustainable transport, restoration of degraded ecosystems and wetlands, and cross-border biodiversity conservation. Agricultural interventions include exchanging climate-smart technologies and coordinating pest and plant disease management. Implementation relies on regional cooperation mechanisms coordinated by the ICSD, joint project development, international financing, knowledge exchange and monitoring based on SDG indicators.

policy_description: Política Nacional de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutricional. Documento CONPES Nº 113
policydecision_details: The National Food and Nutrition Security Policy (Política Nacional de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutricional – PSAN), approved by the Government of Colombia through CONPES Social Document No. 113 of 31 March 2008, establishes a national framework to guarantee food and nutrition security, reduce hunger and malnutrition, and promote the right to adequate food. The policy adopts a multidimensional approach, addressing food availability, physical and economic access, consumption, biological utilization, and food quality and safety. The policy focuses on improving food availability, ensuring equitable access to nutritious food, reducing nutritional deficiencies, and strengthening food safety systems. Key priorities include increasing agricultural productivity, improving food distribution and market access, supporting vulnerable households through social protection programmes, promoting healthy dietary practices and nutrition education, and strengthening maternal and child nutrition. It also emphasizes food quality control, access to healthcare and sanitation, institutional coordination, and monitoring systems to address food insecurity and nutritional inequalities.

This Energy Sector Strategy is a nationwide sectoral document aiming at providing overall guidance on achieving Afghanistan’s energy sector goals in a timely and cost-effective manner. The Strategy is included in the Afghanistan National Development Strategy (ANDS), which reflects the commitment of the Government to poverty reduction and private sector-led economic growth for a prosperous and stable Afghanistan. The Vision for the energy sector seeks for an energy sector that provides citizens of Afghanistan and drivers of growth in the economy with long-term reliable, affordable energy access based on private market-based sector investment and public sector oversight. The Strategy contains an implicit prioritization of energy sub-sector activities (priority is then assigned to other sub-sectors based on their supporting role in electricity and in overall economic activity) and it is based on 5 pillars as follows (i) increased efficiency in existing operation instead of building a new generating plant; (ii) improved sector governance and public private partnership promotion; (iii) improved coordination and capacity development; (iv) rural energy versus rural electrification to be developed for economic activities that lack energy and that will pay for it, thereby subsidizing rural energy; and (v) expanded or new supply, considering alternative supplies such as wind energy or reducing consumption. Consequently, main goals of the Strategy are (i) restructured sector governance and cost-recoverable operations; (ii) rehabilitation and expansion of the public power grid; (iii) attraction of private investment in the energy sector to develop indigenous energy resources (including renewable, natural gas, coal and oil); (iv) improved rural energy access and electricity services; and (v) development of indigenous resources for power and energy use.

policy_description: National Strategy for the Prevention of Infections in the Health Service and Antibiotic Resistance (2008–2012)
policydecision_details: The National Strategy for the Prevention of Healthcare-Associated Infections and Antibiotic Resistance 2008–2012 (Nasjonal strategi for forebygging av infeksjoner i helsetjenesten og antibiotikaresistens), adopted by the Government of Norway on 9 June 2008, establishes a coordinated national framework to prevent healthcare-associated infections and combat antimicrobial resistance. Developed jointly by five ministries responsible for health, agriculture, fisheries, environment, and labour, the strategy aims to preserve the effectiveness of antibiotics, protect human and animal health, and ensure food safety. It recognizes the growing threat of antibiotic-resistant microorganisms in humans and animals and emphasizes the importance of reducing unnecessary antibiotic use and preventing the transmission of resistant pathogens. The strategy is structured around three main objectives: containing antibiotic resistance, reducing healthcare-associated infections, and strengthening research and knowledge. It identifies 31 specific sub-objectives, including improving national surveillance systems for antimicrobial resistance in humans (NORM) and animals (NORM-VET), monitoring antibiotic consumption, establishing a veterinary medicines register, and developing guidelines for responsible antibiotic use. Particular attention is given to veterinary antibiotic stewardship, surveillance of resistant microorganisms in food-producing animals, and reducing the environmental impacts of antibiotics. Additional interventions strengthen infection prevention in hospitals and elderly care facilities, vaccination, hygiene standards, professional training, and public awareness. Implementation involves the Norwegian Institute of Public Health, the Norwegian Veterinary Institute, the Norwegian Food Safety Authority, healthcare institutions, and other relevant agencies, coordinated through an interministerial steering group.

policy_description: National Action Plan to combat desertification/land degradation and to mitigate against drought
policydecision_details: The National Action Plan to combat desertification/land degradation and to mitigate against drought (NAP) is a national policy with a cross-sectoral approach.
