The objectives of the NAP are: (i) to protect water and land resources; (ii) to increase public awareness; (iii) to protect and value trees and forests; (iv) to develop a regulatory framework for the protection and sustainable development and management of rural land resources; (v) to develop appropriate mechanism to protect farmlands and forests from fire, pest and pathogen; (vi) to develop research, training and education programs to improve land assessments and evaluation, cultivation practices, farm and forestry productivity and values, and land use planning; (vii) to establish institutional reform to support and enhance capabilities in all rural sector activities; (viii) to develop good governance strategies to expand and diversify sustainable economic activity and increase employment; (ix) to engage with and contribute to global issues and instruments related to the environment, rural development, sustainable land management etc.; (x) to develop strategies for drought mitigation and early warning systems; (xi) to monitor and evaluate land degradation. The national land use and soil inventories will be completed and all information will be gathered in a database. The status of land degradation will be monitored and evaluated through assessments in all districts in Fiji. Public awareness will be raised on land resources, that soil, water and flora are interdependent and must be managed in an integrated way, and the responsibility of individual land users and the communities for preventing and or mitigating land degradation. The indigenous forests will be protected and managed for their biodiversity, conservation and production values by adopting Sustainable Forest Management (SFM) principles. The protection of the environment and management of water, land, forestry and other natural resources will be conducted in an ecologically sustainable manner. The land use planning processes will outline strategies for the prevention of land degradation. The plantation forests will be managed and administered in a manner that sustains site quality. Sound land use practices will be promoted to maintain and sustain soil qualities. A strategy will be developed for drought mitigation and early warning systems to increase awareness, preparedness and response and to improve climatic monitoring system.

policy_description: National Action Programme to combat desertification in The Bahamas
policydecision_details: The National Action Programme (NAP) to combat desertification in The Bahamas outlines the strategies, objectives, and actions to mitigate, and wherever possible reverse, the effects of land degradation by adopting measures to effectively preserve and manage the limited land resources of The Bahamas, through the participation and partnership of the various stakeholders. The NAP adopts a three-tier approach, consisting of preparatory activities, development and implementation stage and programme evaluation. The NAP addresses the issues of significance for combating desertification/land degradation, such as: uncontrolled land clearing; the use of exotic rather than native species; invasive alien species; pollution and contamination of freshwater resources; cultural practices of farmers; inappropriate building methods; wetland destruction; review and amendment of existing legislation; the enforcement of existing legislation; education and public relations; sustainable development; development of land-use plans; identification of sensitive areas and restoration of protected areas; and strengthening of research capacity. Tier 1 focuses on the identification of initial stakeholders and legal, financial, and human resources; the development of science-based assessments of land conditions in The Bahamas; strengthened data exchange and collection systems to ensure better understanding of those conditions leading to land degradation in The Bahamas; awareness raising on and assessment of the causes and effects of land degradation; and development of research activies and capacities. Tier 2 activities seek to create various networks and initiatives for addressing land degradation through sustainable practices and partnerships among the stakeholders. At this stage, priority will be given to the projects and programmes on public awareness-raising, reforestation, land use planning, water resource management, cultivation techniques, innovative applications etc. The effectiveness of these projects and programmes will be measures in Tier 3 through the implementation of benchmarks and indicators. Stakeholder subcommittees will be established for the implementation of programme audit activities. The evaluation of programmes, policies and legislation developed to combat land degradation will be strengthened. A National Coordinating Committee will be established to coordinate the implementation of the Convention as appropriate for The Bahamas, and serve as a focal point for the coordination of the NAP and other related programmes.

The National Strategic Plan of Barbados is a national policy with a multi-sectoral approach. The timeframe of the Strategy is 20 years between 2006 and 2025. The broad vision of the National Strategic Plan of Barbados is to achieve a fully developed society that is prosperous, socially just and globally competitive. The strategic goals of the Plan are cultural transformation, improved governance, national development, green economy, economic growth, and global success. Food security will be enhanced through safe food supply. A national food security program will be developed. Reliable supply of safe and nutritious food will be provided at the most economical prices to meet current and future needs. In order to provide safe drinking water, a long-term program will be established for the rehabilitation and expansion of the water supply system to ensure sustainability. The health status of all Barbadians will be improved due to the development of the health system. With the aim of a sustainable society that coexist in clean and healthy environment, green economy will be built through (i) effective environmental management, (ii) a safe and reliable water supply, (iii) energy efficiency and conservation, (iv) use of renewable energy resources, (v) sustainable land management, (vi) rational use of fertilizers, (vii) comprehensive waste management, (viii) effective management and protection of natural resources, (ix) effective management and conservation of water resources, (x) conservation of marine and coastal ecosystems, (xi) protection of wildlife habitats and significant flora and fauna, (xii) public awareness raising on the relationship between the environment and the well-being of each individual, and (xiii) the development of accurate data and information systems. A program will be established for the water supply to adequately meet the needs of domestic and commercial users and for irrigation purposes. Arable agricultural land will be safeguarded with sustainable land management practices. Social cohesion will be developed with non-discrimination principle. The number of community-based groups and organizations will increase. Furthermore employment opportunities for persons with disabilities will increase. The rights of all, particularly persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups, will be respected in all aspects of the society with a gender sensitive approach. Gender equity and equality will be ensured through the integration of gender into all areas of national planning and development. The role of the private sector, trade unions, non-governmental organizations and civic-based organizations will be promoted. Civil society will be integrated into all spheres of activity in Barbados, including decision-making processes. Capacity building of youth and youth organizations will be enhanced for self-development with social services, access to resources and education and entrepreneurship programs. The life quality of disabled and elderly will be improved. The basic necessities for the poor and disadvantaged will be met. Social security systems and the social protection network will be strengthened. Poverty eradication programs will be developed. Food safety requirements will be met regarding veterinary services, plant health, international food safety standards, pest and disease detection and control, and pesticide use. Fishing market infrastructure will be regulated to ensure Sanitary and Phytosanitary compliance and adherence to Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point principles. Smallholders will be promoted through credit, advisory, marketing and other relevant assistance. Development of entrepreneurial and business skills will be supported to increase the number of globally competitive entrepreneurs by 2025, new business enterprises and in the rate of expansion of existing ones. Private sector institutions will be strengthened to make a substantially higher contribution to economic and social development. A national research and development and innovation center will be established. Disaster management will be improved against natural and man-made hazards. The response capacity will be enhanced at the national and community levels. Appropriate development standards will be used to build resilience against the increasing intensity of natural hazards, including the effects of climate change. An integrated environmental health management system will be developed involving the principles of risk assessment and risk management. The National Emergency Operation Centre will be developed. The Ministry of Economic Affairs and Development shall be responsible for the implementation of the National Strategic Plan. A Special Unit will be created by the Ministry to monitor the implementation of the National Strategic Plan. This Unit will be controlled and assisted by the National Economic Council and the Social Council.

policy_description: Stratégie nationale des contrôles forestiers et fauniques au Cameroun
policydecision_details: The National Strategy for Forest and Wildlife Control (Stratégie Nationale des Contrôles Forestiers et Fauniques au Cameroun), developed by Cameroon's Ministry of Forestry and Wildlife in March 2005, establishes a national framework to strengthen forest and wildlife law enforcement, improve governance, and promote the sustainable management of natural resources.The strategy focuses on combating illegal logging and wildlife exploitation, strengthening institutional capacities, protecting biodiversity, and ensuring sustainable forest management. Its four strategic pillars include strengthening the capacities of enforcement authorities, promoting stakeholder participation, improving information, education and communication, and reinforcing good governance. Key measures include establishing clear inspection and enforcement procedures, improving sanctions for violations, strengthening interinstitutional coordination, and involving local communities in forest and wildlife management. The strategy also seeks to safeguard community rights, increase public revenues, create employment opportunities, and ensure the long-term sustainability of forest resources, in alignment with international forest governance initiatives such as AFLEG and FLEGT

policy_description: National Program “Engineering water management measures for the protection of settlements and agricultural land from floods in the most flood-dangerous areas of the region of Polesie" (2005-2010)
policydecision_details: The Programme for the Development of Oilseed Production, Oil and Fat Products, and Protein Feed in Belarus (2012–2015), approved through Resolution No. 799 of 31 August 2012, aims to strengthen domestic agricultural production, reduce dependence on imports, and improve the competitiveness of Belarus's oilseed and agro-processing sectors. The programme focuses on expanding oilseed cultivation, modernizing processing facilities, and increasing domestic production of vegetable oils and protein-rich animal feed. Key priorities include developing rapeseed, sunflower, soybean, and flax production, improving agricultural productivity, upgrading agro-industrial infrastructure, and strengthening domestic value chains. It establishes targets of 536,000 hectares under oilseed cultivation and at least 1 million tonnes of marketable oilseeds annually from 2014. The programme also supports technological modernization, investments in processing facilities, and increased export capacity.

policy_description: National Action Program to combat land degradation
policydecision_details: The National Action Program to combat land degradation is a national policy with a multi-sectoral approach. This policy outlines Palau’s commitment to achieving sustainable development by prioritizing efficient land management and responsible use of natural resources to support balanced social progress. It emphasizes the full development of management, scientific, and technological capacities, ensuring coordinated efforts across all sectors and levels. Key focus areas include: (i) establishing a land use plan that harmonizes forest resource utilization with ecological preservation; (ii) implementing inclusive land management strategies that safeguard the land’s biological productivity and its ecological and socioeconomic value for current and future generations; (iii) restoring degraded lands to reclaim their essential role in human well-being; (iv) enhancing watershed management to secure reliable water supplies, particularly during droughts; and (v) strengthening technical and institutional capacities to effectively monitor and address land degradation.

policy_description: National Action Programme to Combat Land Degradation
policydecision_details: The National Action Programme to Combat Land Degradation (NAP) is a national policy with a cross-sectoral approach. The goals of the NAP are: (i) to provide a framework for the implementation of the UNCCD; (ii) to implement UNCCD programmes and activities addressing other socio-economic problems such as poverty, in consistency with government's major goal of poverty alleviation; (iii) to highlight land degradation and desertification issues incorporated within the long-term plan; (iv) to define and demarcate all identified areas of land degradation in Dominica with the use of measurable and usable benchmarks and indicators; (v) to assess the needs of these degraded lands; (vi) to reinforce and develop all stakeholders engaged in land use and land management; (vii) to update and organize ecological restoration and conservation programmes to improve land conditions; (viii) to prioritize agro forestry for research among other land uses for and with local communities; (ix) to facilitate early detection of land degradation that will be cost effective by using local infrastructures and services to provide more reliable results. The institutional framework will be strengthened for the implementation of the NAP. The activities and constituted coordination of all stakeholders from the Government will be integrated to meet land degradation issues. All institutional capacity available will be used in addressing land degradation. The resources from UNCCD will be channelled to meet project implementations. The awareness on land degradation issues will be increased among community members. The environmental education unit will coordinate all awareness programmes on land degradation. The modules highlighting land degradation will be developed to be used at all schools. Trainings will be conducted on land degradation mitigation measures. Land use planning will be strengthened to complement all existing and future work on land degradation. Sustainable use of land resources will be actively promoted in land restoration activities. A strategy will be developed for sustainable use of major forest products in Dominica to manage the levels of exploitation. In addition, the NAP proposes programmes that promote the use of alternative fuel and energy resources and infrastructure development. The Environmental Coordinating Unit (ECU) is an established Unit of the Ministry of Agriculture and the Environment and serve as the secretariat and focal point for all UNCCD activities.

policy_description: National Program on Prevention and Control of Disorders Induced by Dietary Iodine Deficiency among the Population
policydecision_details: The National Programme for the Control and Prevention of Iodine Deficiency Disorders (2004–2010), approved by the Government of Armenia through Decision No. 353-N of 12 February 2004, establishes a national framework to prevent and reduce iodine deficiency disorders, particularly thyroid diseases and developmental impairments associated with inadequate iodine intake. The programme prioritizes universal salt iodization, micronutrient deficiency prevention, and improved nutritional health. It mandates the iodization of salt produced or imported for human consumption, establishes standards for iodine content, and restricts the import and sale of non-iodized edible salt. Additional measures include strengthening laboratory monitoring, improving the diagnosis and treatment of iodine deficiency disorders, training healthcare professionals, and conducting public awareness campaigns. The programme also considers iodine enrichment of animal feed and establishes monitoring and evaluation mechanisms to assess its effectiveness.

policy_description: Barbados National Action Programme to Combat Desertification and Land Degradation, and to Mitigate Against the Effects of Desertification, Land Degradation and Drought
policydecision_details: The National Action Programme to Combat Desertification and Land Degradation, and to Mitigate Against the Effects of Desertification, Land Degradation and Drought is a national policy with a multi-sectoral approach. The policy lays down three thematic areas, namely: agriculture, settlement and resource use and conservation. This policy is a comprehensive Strategy and Action Plan, including action plans for each thematic area. The aim of the agricultural action plan is to promote economic activity through agriculture, for the benefit the people and the development of the Scotland District. A comprehensive database will be established to compile information on soil type and location, volume of water resources and available technical resources. The programmes in the fields of education, access to water, access to roads and terracing, will be developed to meet the needs of farmers. Performance criteria will be created for land owners to reduce the burden of management on the Government. The capacity of the Soil Conservation Unit under the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development will be enhanced. Measures will be taken to further augment water resources. The capacities of farmers will be increased through education with the help of farming organisations already active in the areas. High value/exotic agriculture will be developed where possible through farm cooperatives. The impacts of settlements and associated activities within the Scotland District will be effectively managed to mitigate land degradation. The management of existing settlements, including lowland, highland and roads will be improved. Measures will be taken to combat degradation associated with settlements. Present and future settlements will be planned in a more rational manner. A comprehensive and integrated land use management plan will be developed for the Scotland District. An integrated management system will be established to preserve and enhance existing flora and fauna, sustainably use mineral resources, and preserve and foster the socio-economic and cultural activity of the area, to the benefit of all Barbadians. The Scotland District Environmental Standards Certification Programme will be developed for all activities within the area, with a special emphasis on the need for Environmental Impact Assessment with a primary focus on the impact of activities on the availability, quality and distribution of water, and on drainage as well as on recommendations to minimise impacts that could result in land degradation. All stakeholders throughout the Scotland District will be urged to create corporate environmental strategies that support economic and developmental initiatives aligned with the principles of sustainable development. The funding and assistance in sourcing funds will be provided to assist in the fight to combat desertification, land degradation and drought. An early warning system will be established for extreme climatic events such as storms and drought. Climate change and biodiversity concerns will be integrated with desertification. Relevant legislation will be updated and revised to effectively support the NAP and related policies affecting land degradation and drought prevention and mitigation.

policy_description: National Program Clean Water and Sanitation in Tajikistan
policydecision_details: The National Programme “Clean Water and Sanitation of Tajikistan” establishes a national framework for improving access to safe drinking water, sanitation infrastructure and water resource protection in Tajikistan. Developed in response to deteriorating water infrastructure, widespread contamination and the environmental challenges affecting the Aral Sea basin, the programme assesses existing water supply and sanitation conditions and identifies investment priorities and implementation measures extending to 2015. It highlights significant disparities between urban and rural areas: at the time of preparation, approximately 58.7% of the population used piped water, compared with only 41.1% of rural residents, while around 30% of water supply networks were not functioning. Its principal objective is to improve public health and living conditions by expanding reliable water supply, strengthening sanitation services and protecting surface and groundwater resources from pollution. The programme prioritizes the construction and rehabilitation of drinking water supply systems, expansion of sewerage networks, wastewater treatment, and protection of water sources from biological and chemical contamination. Key interventions include upgrading water treatment facilities, improving water quality monitoring, restoring deteriorated pipelines, extending centralized water supply to underserved rural communities, and developing sanitation infrastructure in urban and rural settlements. Particular attention is given to preventing pollution from agricultural runoff, fertilizers, pesticides, livestock activities, industrial discharges and untreated municipal wastewater. The programme also examines investment requirements, financing mechanisms, institutional responsibilities and potential reforms to water service management. Implementation is envisaged through public investment, participation by local authorities and service providers, and external financing, with infrastructure development priorities identified at regional and district levels.

The National Action Plan to Counteract Antibiotic Resistance 2000–2004 (Tiltak for å motvirke antibiotikaresistens 2000–2004), issued by the Norwegian Ministry of Health and Social Affairs in 2000, establishes a coordinated national framework to prevent and control antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The plan recognizes that excessive and inappropriate antibiotic use in human and veterinary medicine, together with the spread of resistant microorganisms through healthcare, food production and international travel, threatens the effectiveness of antimicrobial treatments. Its overarching objective is to preserve antibiotics as effective medicines by reducing unnecessary consumption, preventing the spread of resistant microorganisms, and improving knowledge of antimicrobial resistance in humans, animals, food products and the environment. The plan adopts a multisectoral approach involving health, agriculture, fisheries and environmental authorities. The plan identifies eight priority areas, including antimicrobial resistance surveillance, monitoring antibiotic consumption, responsible prescribing practices, public awareness, infection prevention, microbiological diagnostics, regulatory improvements and research. Key interventions include strengthening national surveillance systems, notably the Norwegian Monitoring Programme for Antimicrobial Resistance (NORM), improving monitoring of resistant microorganisms in humans, animals and food products, and promoting appropriate antibiotic use among physicians, veterinarians and dentists. Particular attention is given to veterinary antibiotic stewardship, food safety, animal health and infection control in agricultural and aquaculture production systems. Additional measures include improving hygiene standards, strengthening regulations governing antibiotic approval and marketing, expanding professional training and public education, and supporting research into resistance mechanisms and alternative treatments. Implementation relies on interministerial cooperation, public health institutions, veterinary authorities, healthcare providers and research organizations.

policy_description: The Concept of a Unified State Supervision in the Economic Complex
policydecision_details: The Concept of Unified State Supervision in the Economic Complex of the Republic of Tajikistan establishes a framework for reorganizing and strengthening state supervision over industrial activities, natural resource exploitation and occupational safety. The concept responds to the fragmentation of existing inspection authorities, which resulted in overlapping inspections, inconsistent assessments of industrial accidents and insufficient regulatory independence. Its main objective is to establish a unified, independent state supervisory authority responsible for ensuring safe production processes, protecting workers and the environment, preventing industrial accidents, and promoting the rational use of natural and energy resources. The framework seeks to improve regulatory efficiency, transparency and accountability while strengthening compliance with national legislation and technical safety standards. The concept proposes the consolidation of supervisory functions into a single national authority, supported by 14 specialized central inspectorates and regional inspection units. Key interventions include strengthening occupational safety inspections, regulating potentially hazardous industrial activities, supervising mineral extraction and geological operations, monitoring the use of primary energy resources, and enforcing compliance with environmental and technical safety standards. Importantly, the proposed institutional structure includes a dedicated inspectorate for the agro-industrial complex, forestry and wood-processing industries, alongside inspectorates responsible for chemical and metallurgical production, hazardous goods transportation, and other industrial activities. The framework also envisages greater autonomy for regional inspection units, improved technical equipment, a specialized diagnostic laboratory, and professional training courses for inspectors. Financing would come from state budget allocations, existing supervisory institutions and contributions associated with enterprises' occupational safety expenditure.

The National Policy on Ethiopian Women was established to address the systemic discrimination and socio-economic marginalization faced by women in Ethiopia. Recognizing women's vital roles as producers, caregivers, and contributors to national development, the policy aims to rectify historical injustices and ensure women benefit equally from the fruits of their labor. It acknowledges that women have been excluded from property ownership, decision-making, and access to basic services, particularly in rural areas, and seeks to create a framework for their full participation in political, economic, and social life. Central to the policy is the goal of achieving gender equality by eliminating prejudices and harmful traditional practices rooted in male supremacy. It outlines the need to reform laws, regulations, and customs that perpetuate discrimination, and to raise awareness across society to change attitudes toward women. The policy also emphasizes the importance of women's involvement in shaping government policies and development programs, ensuring their voices are heard and their needs addressed at all levels of governance. To implement these objectives, the policy proposes the establishment of Women’s Affairs departments within all government ministries and regional administrations. These bodies are tasked with coordinating women-focused initiatives, monitoring progress, and facilitating vocational training, education, and income-generating activities. Special attention is given to rural women, who face heavier workloads and limited access to resources. The policy also calls for support to women’s associations and ensures that aid from international donors is effectively directed toward women’s empowerment. Ultimately, the policy envisions a society where women are empowered to organize, advocate for their rights, and participate equally in national development. It assigns the primary responsibility for implementation to the government, particularly the Women’s Affairs Sector in the Prime Minister’s Office, while also encouraging collaboration with NGOs, international organizations, and civil society. The success of the policy depends on the active participation of all Ethiopians, with the understanding that the welfare of women is a national concern.

policy_description: Overall Plan for the “Three-North” Shelterbelt Forest Program.
policydecision_details: The Overall Plan for the Three-North Shelterbelt Forest Programme (2021–2050), approved by China's State Council and issued through Notice No. 32 of 6 September 2025, establishes a long-term framework to combat desertification, restore degraded ecosystems, and strengthen ecological security across northern, northeastern, and northwestern China. The programme covers approximately 4.49 million square kilometres across 13 provincial-level regions, aiming to improve forest and grassland coverage, reduce soil erosion, and enhance ecosystem resilience. The plan focuses on desertification control, afforestation, sustainable land management, grassland restoration, and biodiversity conservation. Key priorities include restoring degraded forests and wetlands, establishing protective forest belts around agricultural land, promoting sustainable grazing practices, improving water resource management, and integrating renewable energy development with desertification control. It also supports rural livelihoods through sustainable forestry, forage production, and ecological industries. By 2050, the programme aims to increase forest coverage by 1.9 percentage points, achieve 43% forest and grassland coverage, and restore virtually all desertified land considered suitable for rehabilitation. Implementation is supported by public investment, green financing, technological innovation, and strengthened environmental monitoring
